title: Account management
text: Local accounts, roles, grants and token recovery 中文：账号管理. Related: task grants, audit. Scope and interface Administrators open Accounts and grants to create identities, edit roles and task scopes, disable or re-enable accounts, rotate tokens and delete accounts. VIEWER and OPERATOR cannot call account administration APIs. This page covers local bearer-token accounts. Deployments with multiple Controllers use shared accounts and sessions. Shared access VIEWER reads granted tasks, OPERATOR also controls them, ADMIN manages globally. An empty selected list grants no tasks; all current/future tasks uses taskIds: null . ADMIN cannot be scoped. Unloaded task IDs are retained for advance grants; wildcards are rejected. The last enabled ADMIN cannot be disabled, deleted or demoted. Deletion retains audit identity: the token is revoked and the ID cannot be reassigned. Disabled accounts can be re-enabled. The directory supports at most200 identities including tombstones,10000 exact task IDs per identity; this is not an external-directory capacity claim. Configuration and managed authority Default accessMode: CONFIG preserves startup configuration behavior. authToken/users may reference environment variables. The account page initially displays them read-only. Reviewing the list and explicitly enabling managed accounts transfers them into the durable directory. Once activated, controller.json is authoritative, even if configuration still says CONFIG. Restart does not overwrite managed tokens/grants from old configuration. Changing a Secret/environment variable is not automatic managed-account rotation. Startup configuration still undergoes syntax/identity validation. To remove bootstrap credentials after initialization, use platform-managed.yml: accessMode: MANAGED , no authToken/users , same controller/task directories. An empty directory without an administrator fails startup; it never creates anonymous access. Linux and Docker deployments reuse the persistent directory. The managed Helm and native Kubernetes examples require initialized Controller storage and matching audit data. Reuse the initialized PVC when replacing the Pod. See the deployment evidence for the tested storage and rollout profiles. Helm values · Native YAML · Deployment evidence Tokens and uncertain responses The interface generates32 random bytes using browser crypto. Save the token and acknowledge that before submitting. Preview excludes it; lists/audit/responses never return tokens or their digests. New managed tokens require32–4096 visible ASCII characters; imported bootstrap tokens retain the24-character compatibility minimum. Use generated tokens rather than low-entropy strings. Only SHA-256 token digests are durable; authentication compares digests. No new persistent browser credential storage is used. Closing the editor/directory or signing out clears token inputs. Follow existing deployment security guidance for transport and bearer protection. Rotation immediately revokes the old token for subsequent requests. Successful self-rotation updates the page credential; disabling/deleting yourself signs you out. Permissions refresh on subsequent requests. Already accepted asynchronous operations may continue: revoking an identity is not pausing a dataflow. Task mutation commit checks the authorization revision and rejects stale callers with AUTHORIZATION CHANGED . After lost responses, unchanged drafts retry the same request identity/body. If the mutation committed and invalidated the session, sign in again and inspect the current directory. The server retains up to500 account mutation receipts; expired old requests still cannot bypass revision checks. If your self-rotation committed but its response was lost, use the previously saved new token. Do not delete state or modify synchronization checkpoints to fix login. Durability, concurrency and audit Mutations require expectedRevision and X-Request-ID . Concurrent edits return ACCOUNTS REVISION CHANGED ; reload and review. Identical retained requests do not reapply, and identifiers cannot be reused for another actor/body. Unknown fields and invalid scopes are refused. Directory changes, version and audit outbox are atomically saved together. Audit chain and a persistent directory-version anchor follow. Unavailable audit fails management requests; already committed changes recover through the outbox rather than pretending rollback. Events record actor/action/subject/version, never credentials. The audit interface shows the affected task/account. Local managed access stores the account directory in Controller format 2. At startup Rivomesh verifies the directory against its audit version anchor. Missing or mismatched state stops startup. Back up the Controller directory, audit store and configuration versions together. A consistent older backup can restore previously revoked credentials. Review grants, revocations and tokens after restoration, then compare the audit chain with the independently stored checkpoint when available. Audit checkpoint Offline administrator recovery If every administrator token is lost: 1. Stop the controller; retain its storage and audit data. 2. Prepare platform configuration pointing to the same directories. Supply a configured ADMIN/token through authToken ( legacy-admin ) or users ; prefer an environment-provided random token. 3. Run: 4. The command requires the exclusive controller lock, restores only the selected configured administrator, preserves other identities and task intents, records ACCOUNT RECOVER , and starts no workers. It refuses while the controller runs. 5. Start the service, sign in and review identities/audit. Other configured credentials are not all reactivated. Missing/corrupt directory or mismatched audit is not mere token loss. Recovery does not bypass those guards; restore coordinated backups first. Do not manually lower state versions. API ADMIN only. Mutations require JSON, X-Request-ID , expectedRevision . Method/path Other fields --- --- GET /api/accounts Returns mode/revision/redacted identities POST /api/accounts/activate None; explicit durable management activation POST /api/accounts id,role,enabled,taskIds,token PUT /api/accounts/ id role,enabled,taskIds; token is refused POST /api/accounts/ id /token token DELETE /api/accounts/ id None; retained identity soft deletion Common409 codes: ACCOUNT LAST ADMIN , ACCOUNTS REVISION CHANGED , REQUEST ID REUSED , ACCOUNT EXISTS , ACCOUNT TOKEN COLLISION . Revoked tokens return401; account administration without permission returns403; ungranted task routes remain404. FAQ and evidence Will the old configured administrator work after restart? Managed access does not resurrect it. Explicit offline recovery restores the selected configured administrator. Does deleting an account stop its dataflows? No. Task intents are separate; an authorized operator must pause the dataflow. How do I revoke every task grant? Select scoped tasks, clear selections/additional IDs and save. Do not choose all current/future tasks. Which store determines whether I can sign in? With local managed access, check the directory and audit anchor in the Controller's persistent storage. With shared access, check the shared SQL authority from either Controller. Shared access The verification archive tracks account grants, session persistence, revocation and the tested deployment profiles. Verification archive See browser sessions for reload recovery, sign-out and invalidation of all sessions after directory changes.

title: Browser sessions
text: Browser sessions and login recovery 中文：浏览器会话. Sign-in and recovery Sign in with an existing configured or managed-account token. The page exchanges Bearer credentials once through POST /api/session , clears the input, then authenticates with an HttpOnly cookie. Long-lived tokens are never saved in localStorage, sessionStorage or URLs. Reloading or opening the same site first calls GET /api/session to restore identity, grants and CSRF credentials, then loads tasks. Invalid sessions return to sign-in. Language preference may still use localStorage. Standalone uses a bounded in-memory session store and requires sign-in after restart. Multiple Controllers can keep sessions with the configured shared access store. Sign-out clears UI permissions, drafts and raw differences immediately, then revokes the server session. BroadcastChannel tells other tabs to sign out; without it, their next request/poll discovers revocation. Sign-in and sign-out are serialized within each page so a delayed login response is also revoked. Late API responses cannot revive cleared UI state. If refresh discovers a different cookie session, it clears the previous identity drafts/details before restoring current grants. Failed server sign-out is reported and can be retried; clearing the page alone is not proof of revocation. Configuration PlatformConfig.sessions and the Helm top-level sessions have the same fields: Field Default Meaning --- --- --- enabled true Permit browser-session exchange; disabling it preserves Bearer APIs secureCookie true Production Host-rivomesh-session cookie; requires HTTPS, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Path=/ and no Domain publicOrigin unset Exact external origin behind a proxy, e.g. https://sync.example.com , with no trailing slash, path, query or user info idleSeconds 1800 Idle deadline after the last validated API request, including automatic polling; 30–86400 seconds absoluteSeconds 28800 Hard lifetime since sign-in, at least idleSeconds and at most 604800; polling cannot extend it rememberBrowser false Default session cookie; true adds Max-Age bounded by the absolute lifetime, but restart still invalidates it maximum 1000 Active sessions per controller, 1–10000; expired entries are purged on creation and capacity rejects new sign-ins These are adjustable policies, not throughput claims. Polling extends server idle time; a human-inactivity timeout is a separate future policy. Browser session-restore features may retain session cookies, so closing the browser does not replace sign-out. Production proxy configuration: Terminate TLS at the proxy; the controller remains HTTP. Restrict backend access to authorized networks and provide HTTPS to browsers. publicOrigin declares the external origin; client-supplied X-Forwarded- headers are not trusted. Without it, origin validation expects https://Host . Cookie-authenticated mutations require an exact Origin and matching X-CSRF-Token . The HTTP development preview at http://127.0.0.1:18088 and local examples explicitly set secureCookie: false , using rivomesh-dev-session . Use the HTTPS settings above in production. Helm defaults to Secure; local port-forward preview can explicitly use --set sessions.secureCookie=false . Production can set --set sessions.publicOrigin=https://sync.example.com . Edit the same ConfigMap fields for native Kubernetes manifests. API and revocation contract Request Authentication/result --- --- POST /api/session Valid Bearer only; returns identity, CSRF credential and absolute expiry, and issues Set-Cookie; browser Origin must match configuration GET /api/session Cookie returns identity, scope, csrfToken and expiresAt; Bearer retains its previous identity view and does not issue a cookie POST /api/session/logout Cookie + Origin + X-CSRF-Token; revokes the session and clears the cookie; available to all roles Other APIs Cookie mutations validate Origin/CSRF, then retain role, task-scope, revision, request-ID and audit checks An explicit Authorization header always uses Bearer validation and never falls back to a cookie. Valid credentials for different accounts return 409 AUTHENTICATION CONFLICT . Same-account explicit Bearer uses API rules without cookie CSRF. CLI/API clients need not adopt cookies. Session IDs and CSRF credentials never enter audit records; identity and operation outcomes do. The current strict directory-revision policy invalidates all existing browser sessions on that controller after any managed-account creation, modification, enable/disable, deletion, token rotation or managed activation . This includes the administrator making the change, who must sign in again. After a confirmed self-token rotation, the page can exchange the newly saved token for a fresh session automatically. Bearer credentials are still checked against the current directory on each request. Config-mode identity changes require restart, which clears sessions. Sign-out does not undo already executed task operations; inspect their operation records. FAQ and recovery - Sign-in appears after reload: check absolute expiry, controller restart, directory changes, cookie policy and origin. Requests switching between controllers are not yet supported. - HTTP sign-in does not persist: Secure cookies are not sent over HTTP. Explicitly disable Secure only for local development; configure HTTPS in production. Different hostnames/protocols do not share the session. - Independent deployments on different ports sign each other out: cookies are not isolated by port. Use different hostnames to avoid overwriting same-name cookies. The application uses root paths and does not support multiple controllers under different URL subpaths on one site. - 403 ORIGIN REJECTED: align the browser URL, publicOrigin, TLS and proxy configuration; preserve Origin/CSRF checks. - 403 CSRF REJECTED: reload to recover the current CSRF credential. Credentials from old pages/sessions cannot be reused. - Account edits sign everyone out: this is the current strict revision policy. Sign in again; disabled or rotated old tokens remain invalid. - 409 SESSION CAPACITY REACHED: closing a page does not revoke its session. Sign out unused sessions, wait for expiry, or increase maximum within the memory budget. Restart clears all sessions but is not routine capacity management. - Sign-out was not confirmed: restore connectivity/audit availability and retry sign-out. Another administrator can disable the account or rotate its token to trigger revision revocation. An API failure is not success. Acceptance covers single-controller real HTTP, a TLS proxy, expiry/revocation, Bearer conflicts and DOM races. Full-browser/accessibility and multi-controller acceptance remain separate. Consult this iteration's archived evidence for actual results.

title: Source capture recovery
text: Capture recovery 中文 When a V3 task enters ERROR during source connection, reading, decoding, snapshot, discovery, DDL or normalization, an administrator can open Review capture recovery in the failure card. In a fixed-Agent deployment either controller routes the read to the owning Agent. The report lists potentially affected subscriptions, the original checkpoint hash, source admission and the recovery steps. The review checks the pipeline identity, original position and snapshot dependencies. It performs admission reads against the source. Refresh and repeat the review if the task generation, checkpoint or configuration changes during the check. Observation Recovery step --- --- SOURCE LOG GAP Preserve the GTID and any retained binlogs. Restore the missing logs or have the database operator restore an eligible primary with complete history. Retry the original checkpoint after review. POSTGRESQL REQUIRED WAL UNAVAILABLE Preserve the original slot, required WAL, journal and LSN evidence. Evaluate whether the original slot and WAL can be recovered. Review a new baseline and the affected destinations when recovery is unavailable. SOURCE CHECKPOINT AVAILABLE after decode, DDL or snapshot failure Preserve the original event, resolve the decoder, schema or read permissions, then retry. Admission confirms the original source position meets the recovery checks. UNPROVEN SOURCE RANGE Verify transaction boundaries and contents against the original logs and checkpoint. Include every subscription in the potential impact. For a MySQL DDL failure, the report can compare the latest recorded schema with the current catalog. It lists bounded changed-table details, visible column changes, identity-key changes and definition hashes. The source catalog may already include later DDL. Resolve the required schema changes before retrying, and preserve the original binlog position. FAQ Why does the destination have data while capture remains paused? The destination may retain data delivered before the failure. Check the source checkpoint and each subscription acknowledgment to establish its progress. When can I skip a transaction? Use the transaction skip workflow when a complete destination transaction is available for review, the target state is established and the approval requirements are met. RC-04 tracks subsequent source-range quarantine and approved exclusion. Native MySQL transaction headers For a supported SOURCE DECODE fault, the review can show the first transaction after the durable checkpoint. It reads up to 256 native event headers from the same server and binlog file, requires continuous offsets through Xid , and lists the GTID, file coordinates and affected tables. The nextTransactionHeaders field uses BINLOG HEADERS ONLY as its scope. Retain the original binary log for row-content review and approvals. Rotation, a gap, a backend change, unfamiliar events or an incomplete boundary can leave the header evidence absent. Read permissions follow the existing MySQL replication account. MySQL binary log event reference · Native evidence Verify the complete transaction byte range once the capture lease has cleared. The supported initial profile covers one CRC32 binlog row transaction up to 4 MiB. The verification reads the retained source range over the replication connection, checks every event checksum and matches the GTID and file offsets through commit. The CLI prints the digest and metadata. For retention, create the operator-owned directory with 0700 on a filesystem supporting hard links. Each 0600 archive contains the context, checkpoint hash and exact binary frames. Retrying the same retained evidence reuses its SHA-addressed file. Include the directory in your protected evidence retention and backup policy because the binary frames contain row values. Both commands preserve the original journal checkpoint. Native evidence Retain from a management entry An administrator can select Retain original transaction after reviewing the native boundary. In a separated cluster the durable command goes to the Agent that owns the task. The command binds the reviewed boundary hash, configuration revision and capture error generation. Inspect the command receipt for the archive file and SHA-256. The binary event contents stay in the Agent's private capture-evidence/ taskId directory, with a 256 MiB per-task archive budget. The original capture position and error remain unchanged. A retry with the same request observes the same receipt across management entries. For API clients use POST /api/tasks/ id /actions with an X-Request-ID and the reviewed values. New archives retained through global task control also have a private authentication receipt. The original Agent signs the exact archive filename, byte count and SHA-256, together with the owner directory, task, configuration fingerprint, journal generation, checkpoint, error generation and reviewed boundary. The Agent creates this receipt before publishing the raw file. If interrupted between the two writes, retry recovers only when the original binlog can be read again and the bytes match. Back up the receipt and its Agent-local key alongside the raw archive under the same private access controls. Archives written before this change can still be reviewed through their existing recovery paths. An Agent can verify an archive with this receipt through the handoff custody probe. It grants no transfer or recovery authorization. Native acceptance uses a full-image MySQL 8.4.13 commit that exceeds the configured row limit. The original Agent retains the native bytes, then replays the same GTID after an approved increase to the row limit. Both SQL destinations match the source, and the journal generation, fingerprint and snapshot IDs stay the same. After the task drains, the candidate verifies the separately mounted raw archive. The custody probe reports the original task owner and returns executionAuthorized: false . After both Agents verify the same raw archive, open the handoff preparation and select Stage reports and receipts . The Controller verifies the preparation and sends the bound candidate the exact archive descriptor. The candidate stores the raw ZIP and its sealed binding in private handoff-raw-staging storage. The response adds rawCapture and the console shows the verified archive count. Retry the same staging request from either Controller to reverify the sealed copy after a shared mount outage. The original Agent keeps its HMAC key. Publishing this inactive archive leaves the source checkpoint and task owner at the reviewed cut. A prepared PostgreSQL-managed writer handoff can publish this exact staged ZIP to the committed candidate's private handoff-adopted history while its Worker is stopped. Both Controllers serve GET /api/tasks/ taskId /handoff/raw-history with the archive digest, size, capture count and the adoption digest. The administrator needs access to the task and both Agents. The endpoint verifies the private copy and remains available after a candidate restart, even if the shared mount is gone. The original Agent retains the archive, receipts and HMAC key. The adopted archive provides historical inspection. Transaction skip, target writes, and Worker start require their own authorization. If the task also retains signed failure records, the same preparation stages both kinds of history. The two history endpoints return one adoption digest after commitment. Failure history handoff Approve a source transaction skip After retention succeeds, select Review source transaction skip from the operation receipt. Check the single GTID, affected tables and all affected destinations. Enter a reason and confirm the impact. The task stays paused after the skip. This profile requires a same-file, committed row transaction with the original checksummed binlog bytes retained. Mapped affected tables require a completed InnoDB snapshot with a primary key. Affected destinations use transactional SQL. Keyless tables, unsupported target protocols, incomplete snapshots or a native boundary that can no longer be verified require recovery of the original source or a reviewed rebuild. If MySQL purged required logs, retain the archive and recover the logs or choose an eligible source with the required history. On success the journal records the exclusion and adds exactly that GTID to the capture position. Destination acknowledgments remain at their previous positions. After Resume , later transactions can be delivered, while each affected destination's contiguous applied position stops at the source gap. View source gaps shows the durable receipt after Agent restart. Reconcile the affected tables and verify a common cut before business takeover. The original exclusion remains in history. API clients send CAPTURE EXCLUDE to the same actions endpoint with an X-Request-ID , expectedRevision and the plan's errorCount . Include captureExclusion with boundaryHash , archiveSha256 , planHash , reason and acceptDataLoss: true . Administrators can list receipts through GET /api/tasks/ id /capture-exclusions?limit=20 . Pass the returned nextCursor as after to read the next page.

title: ActiveMQ Classic
text: ActiveMQ Classic 中文：Classic 手册. The implementation uses native OpenWire persistent local transactions, an event queue and a separately retained receipt queue on one fixed broker. Independent actual-release Java8 native acceptance passed persistent publication, selected-consumer ACK, invalid-selector/purge refusal, restart and actual old nonempty-backup protection. MySQL8.4+PostgreSQL17 pipeline acceptance also passed snapshot/CDC, process kill, broker outage, SQL constraint repair/retry and purge isolation; this does not establish cluster acceptance. The fixture broker is Apache ActiveMQ 5.19.12. Rivomesh pins client 5.16.8 and isolates its JMS, SLF4J and Hawtbuf packages from other SDKs. The original Java 8 profile remains in the verification archive. Current deployments use Temurin 21 LTS. Client 5.16 is inactive. Track its security lifecycle separately from the broker. See Apache downloads and archived releases. Use config/classic-v3.yml. Product is ACTIVEMQ CLASSIC , endpoint activemq://host:61616 (or activemqs://host:61617 ), explicit messaging.broker , stream prefix and authenticated HTTP(S) messaging.adminUrl ending /api/jolokia/ . Credentials are separate from URLs. check connects to OpenWire and reads broker/JMX capabilities without creating business queues. Wire broker ID/name must match management; persistent, non-slave KahaDB is required. HTTP redirects and ambiguous JSON/JMX responses cannot become confirmations. TLS requires a separately verified certificate and JVM trust configuration; no real TLS acceptance yet. Resources and consumer contract The physical event queue is prefix . 64-character binding hash ; the receipt queue appends .receipts . Both retain a persistent OWNER record with a random shared owner nonce, binding and both queue names. Source journal identity binds the nonce; native progress binds a receipt JMSMessageID and batch content digest. Consumers MUST use exactly: The application reads channel/key/event-ID properties and the ordinary V3 JSON bytes envelope. Deduplicate stable event IDs and stage/validate transaction boundaries, counts and ordinals before business commit. A producer confirmation is not consumer completion. Acknowledge events only after durable downstream commit; multiple consumers still need transactional staging/order handling. Never consume OWNER records or any receipt messages. Queue size includes the retained owner; it does not equal the number of outstanding event messages. Before publication, management checks that event subscriptions have the exact selector and that receipt queues have no subscriptions. External JMS browsers also count; use JMX browsing for administrative inspection. Broker ACLs must deny readers access to .receipts and deny OpenWire accounts permission to create missing queues. Bootstrap uses explicitly authorized JMX addQueue . An operator must retain OWNER/receipt records, disable inactive-destination GC, avoid expiry/discard policies and configure KahaDB journalDiskSyncStrategy=always and enableJournalDiskSyncs=true . The current standard MBeans do not prove all those policy/flush settings at runtime; provision and audit broker configuration. The isolated fixture illustrates the contract and is not a production secret file. Management needs read/search and narrowly authorized addQueue / getMessage ; destructive operations belong to a separately controlled recovery process. Confirmation and recovery One local JMS transaction writes the event batch and a persistent receipt, then native receipt content is read back. Only then can the fenced source journal save transport progress and schema/snapshot/transaction confirmation. Lost responses can replay the same application event IDs; no distributed XA or exactly-once downstream guarantee is claimed. An older owner's in-flight request cannot be revoked by journal fencing; shared pause remains explicitly unconfirmed until quiescence is established. Resume validates both ownership records and the last saved receipt before any resource creation/publication. Missing initialized queues, owner changes, missing or changed receipts require a recovery/rebuild plan. Normal EVENT consumption retains ownership and receipts. Whole-store rollback can retain old owner IDs; the later receipt is still required. Arbitrary selective deletion of historical events is not a complete-history checksum and cannot be repaired by ordinary resume. Receipt retention/compaction is not implemented. Metadata grows per publication batch, and native message lookup can scan retained queue history. Capacity/soak, separate-store replication, network connectors, TLS and broader mixed-product pipeline acceptance are outside the shared KahaDB proof described below. Shared KahaDB primary and standby Classic 5.19.12 can start two broker processes with the same broker name and the same KahaDB directory on a filesystem that enforces exclusive locks between the processes. One process acquires the lock and opens OpenWire. The other waits for the lock, then opens OpenWire after the active process releases it. Verify the filesystem lock semantics for the actual deployment. Configure a positive lockKeepAlivePeriod and retain the file lock throughout operation. Shared-file-system failover, storage lockers, 5.19.12 release. Keep one stable OpenWire address and one stable authenticated Jolokia address. Route both to the same current lock holder. Rivomesh compares active broker name and ID across the two connections and requires the saved OWNER and receipt when opening a new publisher. Whole-store recovery requires the shared store itself to remain available. Each broker can keep its process-local temporary files in its own data directory. Run the isolated native profile with the packaged candidate and Temurin 21: All five checks passed with the ARM64 Classic 5.19.12 image and a Temurin 21 Rivomesh process. The fixture starts two real brokers with a common Docker KahaDB volume. A loopback forwarder routes OpenWire and Jolokia together. The checks cover the initial standby lock wait, native EVENT and receipt confirmation, a retryable publication attempt during isolation, and the same original standby PID taking over after the primary is killed. The reopened publisher reads the saved native receipt under the same ownership identity, consumes the retained and retried EVENTs, and continues after the old primary rejoins in standby. It records artifact, broker image, fixture hashes and cleanup in the output manifest. It covers the real publisher/consumer path with an external endpoint switch. It does not cover an independent storage failure, production load-balancer automation, multi-host filesystem or a complete MySQL-to-Classic Worker promotion. FAQ Why separate receipts? Ordinary queue consumers remove events. A durable receipt must survive consumer acknowledgments to verify a later restart/backup. Wrong selector or lost owner? Stop the consumer, preserve remaining history, review the gap and repair/rebuild under a plan. Resume retries the failed source transaction; it never recreates ownership over initialized empty queues. Broker outage? Connection/HTTP transport failures retry from the persisted checkpoint. Authentication, policy or confirmed-history failures pause this target. Other target subscriptions keep their independent checkpoints. How do I route Classic traffic after broker promotion? Keep the configured OpenWire and Jolokia addresses stable and switch both upstreams to the active broker. The connector accepts a direct activemq:// or activemqs:// address. Independent KahaDB stores and ActiveMQ client failover: URIs have separate requirements and are outside this shared-store profile. HTTP403 from a current broker? Classic5.19.12 also defaults Jetty management access to loopback IPs. Authorize the synchronization worker's actual management network using explicit InetAccessHandler include rules, retaining authentication and Jolokia permissions. HTTP403 is not evidence of a missing queue. Queue existence uses successful exact-MBean searches because the server may redact exception types; failed management calls never authorize resource recreation. Strict origin checks: The client sends Referer containing the management endpoint's own scheme/authority. Allow that exact origin in Jolokia CORS policy and retain strict checking; no global JVM header override is required. Jolokia explicitly supports Referer fallback in its security manual. Native HTTP200 plus Jolokia status403 remains an access failure, not a queue absence. The accepted fixture policy allows both http://classic:8161 and http://classic:8161/ : this Jolokia version compares the full Referer value, including its trailing slash. For another deployment, allow the exact value management-scheme :// management-authority / , retaining strict checking. Recorded acceptance target/classic-subscription-selector-fixed.log :2 SDK classification tests and 63 core/API tests passed,0 failures/errors/skips. target/ui-classic-first.log :20 DOM passes. target/classic-native-selector-fixed.log : actual release/native Java8 acceptance described above. Release145723459bytes SHA256 1a1945e3f91658e3f666a79af66b5da1d6ec0eb8ea2ff00cd3d9f8242a017115. Earlier native logs failed and are not acceptance. target/classic-pipeline-first.log built successfully but its harness failed because the Maven Java8 image has no Python; it is not acceptance. The corrected target/classic-pipeline-prebuilt.log passed ONE actual release pipeline case, with host verification of fresh source/tests and native inspector classes compiled against that release. Source/MySQL and target/PostgreSQL were real, with LOCAL H2 journal. Both pre/post SHA256 were 6eb2a8bb053fcf777b765713e5c21aeb675e586f53c79098e5dffb2103afb954, 145723578bytes. Snapshot/current rows were reconstructed from received envelopes by stable IDs, row identities and completed transactions. The consumer persists its received batch before ACK. Worker SIGKILL, broker outage/catch-up, PostgreSQL CHECK failure with Classic continuing, removing the constraint/resuming its original error generation, and purging the initialized Classic queue with SQL continuing all passed. Pause reports SQL FENCED and MQ UNCONFIRMED. Run bash tests/classic-pipeline-run.sh ; an unchanged verified release can use RIVOMESH TEST PREBUILT=1 . Python runs on the host for verification, not as a runtime dependency in the Maven/JRE8 containers. All own resources were cleaned. Final package: target/classic-final-unit-package.log 2 SDK +63 core/API passes,0fail/error/skip; UI20 passes. Current145723617-byte release SHA256290adcc746a64c427ccefc6de712b8fbb7bbdc7ed4d48fcd2757485e99b6c2fe. All65091 class files were compared with the accepted pipeline release; only AdapterCatalog.class changed (status text). Runtime protocol resources are byte-identical. See archived evidence.

title: ClickHouse
text: ClickHouse versioned materialization 中文：ClickHouse 手册. V3 supports a direct ClickHouse HTTP/HTTPS destination alongside transactional databases and message destinations. The accepted initial server is ClickHouse 25.8.33.6, using Atomic databases, local MergeTree receipts and ReplacingMergeTree data. The business names are query views using FINAL and filtering tombstones. This profile serves analytical queries; transactional business takeover requires its own database/application compatibility assessment. Configure and start Use the complete example. Set product: CLICKHOUSE , a direct http://host:8123 or https://host:8443 endpoint, separate username/password, an exclusive metadata database and explicit source-database to target-database mappings. Authentication material is never placed in the URL. The endpoint accepts no credentials, query parameters or non-root path. Use the normal V3 multi-target wizard or YAML import; credentials are masked in previews. check reads source/catalog capabilities and checks ClickHouse UInt128, canonical-query formatting and required MergeTree settings. It creates no target database/table. run requires database/table/view creation, INSERT and SELECT permissions, including access to the relevant system catalog. Existing non-Atomic databases and foreign business objects are rejected. A missing initialized object is not silently recreated at an old checkpoint. One deployment can configure several target instances and independently mapped databases. Use a fixed direct server endpoint for this profile. Load-balancing between independent servers, Distributed/Replicated/Shared engines, Keeper failover and ClickHouse Cloud require separate profiles and acceptance. Data and indexes Source representation Initial ClickHouse storage --- --- Boolean UInt8, retaining NULL where allowed Signed / unsigned integers Int64 / UInt64 Decimal Decimal with source precision/scale, up to 76 digits Float32 / Float64 Native binary floating point; nonfinite values rejected Text / JSON String; JSON number text remains lossless Binary / geometry Raw String bytes, decoded from the internal base64 wire value Date / time / datetime / timestamp Lossless String, including values outside native temporal ranges SQL NULL Nullable flag; distinct from JSON literal null Generated columns Source/normalizer-computed values, stored as ordinary columns Temporal text avoids truncating MySQL's wide calendar range and TIME durations. Use explicit analytical conversion expressions where appropriate. Original schema details remain in the owned metadata. MySQL collation, default-expression and generated-expression execution semantics are not installed in ClickHouse. Logical identity keys feed stable row identities; source sequence and row ordinal select the latest version. Identical keyless occurrences retain separate identities, and a delete removes one occurrence. PK moves delete the old identity and insert the new one. Query business views to obtain the logical current rows; underlying physical parts can contain earlier versions and replay duplicates. uniquePolicy: DOWNGRADE BUSINESS is required. Business UNIQUE constraints are not enforced in ClickHouse. Source PK/identity selection is retained through the versioned view. All target writes during synchronization belong to the synchronization service, as agreed for constraint downgrades. Secondary index conversion The new-task wizard and example explicitly set clickhouse.secondaryIndexes: DATA SKIPPING . For backward compatibility, omitted options retain the earlier NONE data-only profile. check returns clickhouseIndexPlans , with each source index, action, reason and physical index names. The accepted table schema record persists that plan. Source secondary index Physical access structure --- --- BTREE, business UNIQUE, simple column GSI/GLOBAL/GLOBAL BTREE One non-unique skipping index per indexed column Numeric/boolean/decimal column minmax , granularity 1 Text/binary/temporal-text column bloom filter(0.01) , granularity 1 Composite or descending index Split into per-column structures; source ordering is not reproduced Repeated column across indexes One shared physical index Expression, prefix, FULLTEXT/SPATIAL or unsupported column type REQUIRES PLAN ; automatic table creation stops Source primary/identity key Retained by stable row identity; never weakened into optional acceleration These structures do not enforce uniqueness, provide a B-tree point lookup, reproduce MySQL collation/order, or retain GSI routing/global uniqueness. They accelerate matching analytical predicates where data distribution permits; a planner may choose not to use them. Temporal String indexes accelerate equality, not native calendar-range operations. Bloom false positives add reads, not rows. See the official skipping-index guide. Generated views explicitly enable use skip indexes if final=1 and use skip indexes if final exact mode=1 . Exact mode expands candidate ranges to include newer versions before FINAL; disabling it can resurrect stale matches. The accepted server's settings source describes that requirement. Do not edit the owned view or query physical history as if it were the current business table. New table creation checks the complete canonical definition, including indexes, before persisting schema confirmation. Index/view alterations after confirmation pause this target. Earlier data-only ClickHouse tasks: omitted options or explicit clickhouse.secondaryIndexes: NONE retain the original configuration fingerprint and existing layout. This is an explicit index omission, recorded as OMIT BY CONFIGURATION , not a completed conversion. Changing from NONE to DATA SKIPPING changes the fingerprint; it does not run ALTER against initialized data. Use a separately planned new generation and snapshot/rebuild. Do not erase journal metadata to bypass this guard. The UI wizard uses DATA SKIPPING for new tasks; importing YAML supports either mode. Omitted fields in earlier task files do not trigger an automatic layout migration. Confirmation and recovery Rows use native RowBinary, bounded requests and synchronous inserts. Each batch groups rows by table; writes precede a durable native receipt, which precedes the fenced application-journal checkpoint. Receipt/data tables request fsync after insert=1 , fsync part directory=1 and min rows to fsync after merge=1 . Actual power-loss and storage-controller behavior still require hardware testing. HTTP 200 alone cannot confirm a ClickHouse query. The client checks exception headers, complete JSON/count/shape and an empty command response; it rejects trailing error bodies and redirects. The HTTP client does not automatically repeat a request after losing its response. The sink replays through stable versions and receipt checks, without claiming SQL transaction atomicity. VERSIONED MATERIALIZATION means rows and tables within one source transaction may become visible in separate batches. Full-copy rows can also be visible before snapshot completion. Monitor the durable target checkpoint and snapshot acknowledgements when deciding whether a dataset has caught up. Each target has independent checkpoints and error generations. Network failures retry automatically; permanent SQL/schema/ownership failures pause that target and retain its original events. Other targets continue until shared journal capacity/backpressure requires intervention. After correcting a retryable plan or permission issue, use the console's generation-bound target resume. Resume retries the original data and never skips it. Shared pause reports UNCONFIRMED IN FLIGHT MATERIALIZATION : it fences the application journal but cannot retract an HTTP write already running on the server. A business cutover must establish quiescence and reconciliation first. Do not infer a transactional target's exact local SQL fence here. Review a failed transaction's preceding receipt Pause the whole pipeline when ClickHouse is already paused on a complete incremental apply failure. Use its subscription error generation in the read-only review command. PRECEDING RECEIPT VERIFIED confirms that the current native receipt table contains the saved last COMMIT receipt of the acknowledged preceding transaction. The review checks the original table identity, receipt hash, ClickHouse publication checkpoint and retained failed-head hashes. It reports acknowledgment and failed sequence, then rechecks the journal cut after native I/O. The result covers the preceding receipt. Whether the failed transaction partially materialized remains a separate recovery question. If saved transport progress refers to a different or later batch, the command reports CLICKHOUSE RECOVERY PUBLICATION UNCERTAIN . Missing or changed native receipts require restoring consistent history or planning a new baseline. Keep all original state and use Resume this target after correcting a recoverable fault. ClickHouse transaction skip and before-image compensation are unavailable. Recovery modes Operational FAQ Why are both metadata and physical data tables present? The service owns generation/fingerprint comments, stable object UUIDs, schema records and native batch receipts. Keep them with the data. They are part of recovery, not disposable temporary tables. Their retention/compaction and large-catalog capacity work remain explicit platform backlog. Can consumers read only the business view? The view uses invoker security. Grant the consumer SELECT on that view and its specific underlying physical data table, without INSERT/ALTER/DROP. SHOW CREATE TABLE target database.table identifies the physical dependency. Queries should use the business view's version/tombstone selection. Credentials, grants and user management remain the database administrator's responsibility. The target restored an older nonempty backup. Can it resume? Startup checks the saved native receipt and schema/object identities. Missing or changed confirmed history raises a rebuild-required error, even if old UUIDs remain. Retain the journal and investigate the backup boundary. Reconciliation/rebuild planning is required; deleting receipt rows or creating empty replacement views does not repair a checkpoint. Arbitrary earlier-row corruption is not proven absent by checking the latest receipt. What if journal storage disappears? LOCAL requires its original persistent directory; shared/multi-host operation requires an EXTERNAL transactional journal. Target rows alone cannot reconstruct keyless identities, capture positions and all receipts. Restore coordinated metadata or plan a full rebuild; independent metadata rollback is not an automatic recovery contract. Why does a decimal string omit trailing zeros? ClickHouse formatting can omit them. Verify the numeric value and declared precision/scale; the native acceptance checks both, including Decimal(65,30). Can I edit schemas, clear tombstones or write target rows? Synchronization assumes exclusive service writes. Schema/UUID changes are checked; arbitrary external DML can invalidate materialization. Preserve tombstones and receipt history. Live source DDL, nonempty foreign-target adoption, automatic repair and business takeover remain separate planned workflows. Recorded acceptance target/clickhouse-native-protocol-decimal.log : real server typed boundaries, binary/JSON/NULL, UInt128 version replay, restart identity/history and deletion. target/clickhouse-materializer-release.log : actual release JAR, read-only check, automatic tables/views, PK move, keyless multiplicity/delete, duplicate replay, client/server restart and refusal after restoring an older nonempty target. target/clickhouse-pipeline-first.log : 24 executions passed, including a real MySQL 8.4 → ClickHouse + PostgreSQL release-JAR pipeline with LOCAL H2 journal, JSON/unsigned/decimal/ binary/generated columns, target outage with SQL continuing, automatic catch-up, worker kill/restart, and missing-view isolation. target/ui-clickhouse-first.log : 18 DOM cases passed. These do not establish replicated/cluster/TLS/power-loss, large-catalog and soak acceptance. Temurin 21 passed the ClickHouse 25.8.33.6 materializer against a real server with a LOCAL H2 journal. After restarting from its original volume, it confirmed sequence 3. Restoring an older nonempty volume removed a later visible row. The adapter refused to write with CLICKHOUSE CONFIRMED HISTORY MISSING REBUILD REQUIRED and kept the journal-backed checkpoint at sequence 3. The test also covered NONE reopen, BTREE/GSI-derived skipping indexes, FINAL, keyless rows and duplicate replay. Run bash tests/clickhouse-materializer-run.sh with the packaged JAR. Exact acceptance Historical compatibility acceptance: target/clickhouse-index-compat-unit.log 58PASS/0fail/error/skip and target/ui-clickhouse-index-compat.log 19PASS. target/clickhouse-index-native-compat.log actual-release Java8 native acceptance passed explicit NONE create/reopen without indexes plus indexed FINAL/replay/restart/old-volume rollback protection. Omitted config options retain NONE and the old fingerprint; new wizard/example explicitly opt into DATA SKIPPING. Archived artifact 144098892 bytes, SHA25695dbdbb462929ed1a262072e80d1db885696fa53007d5315c38c4d951c193212. Earlier28-pipeline acceptance predates this default-only compatibility adjustment. All own test resources cleaned.

title: Commit acknowledgement recovery
text: Confirm an already committed destination transaction Status: RC-05 bounded profile accepted:UI,API,protocol6 admission,atomic ACK/receipt and cross-entry recovery. Evidence.中文 The initial profile uses a MySQL source and transactional PostgreSQL/MySQL destinations,retained complete raw/normalized transactions,and destinations written only by the synchronization service. Snapshot faults,unbounded/incomplete capture or decode failures,and other destination protocols cannot use this operation. Workflow 1. Pause the whole task and confirm native destination fencing. A paused subscriber alone is insufficient. Whole-task pause revokes the old Worker epoch. 2. Retain new evidence for the failed subscriber after pausing. Earlier evidence remains readable,but cannot authorize this confirmation. 3. Review source position,complete transaction,destination and hashes. The checkpoint comparison must report committed but unacknowledged,without a lagging destination epoch. 4. Enter a reason of at least eight characters,check the review declaration,and select Confirm committed transaction . The form requires administrator permission and a current matching pause/error observation. 5. Inspect the completed operation receipt. ACK advances exactly one proven committed transaction;the subscriber error generation increments. Task and subscriber remain paused. Business rows are not rewritten. 6. Inspect the next transaction and repair the cause before explicitly resuming the subscriber and task with current error generations. If the form is absent,check the cluster capability,pipeline pause,observation freshness and destination fence. Do not edit checkpoint tables manually. First deployment Configure all controllers and Agents using thefirst-release baselinebefore startup. Development-version in-place upgrades/automatic mode migration are unsupported. Linux,Docker,Helm and manual Kubernetes share identity/storage requirements. Metadata DDL requires appropriate privileges;restart recovery and missing-history refusal remain supported. API and receipt POST /api/tasks/ task /actions returns202. Use the current task revision and preserve X-Request-ID plus all parameters when retrying. Cookie requests retain CSRF/Origin protection. Poll the operation. Successful results contain receipt and its hash . The receipt binds operation/evidence identity,actor,reason,old/new error generations,confirmed sequence and native checkpoint. Operation audit does not contain event row values. FAQ Did a timeout commit? Retry the original request ID and parameters. ACK and receipt commit in one journal transaction;an already committed operation returns its receipt. In the UI,refresh and inspect the original operation first. Can I confirm an unadvanced checkpoint? No. Native progress must equal ACK+1 with identical transaction ID and projected hash. Unadvanced progress does not prove absent rows or authorize skipping. Why fresh evidence? Whole-task pause,Worker restart or another failure can change epoch/error generation. Historical evidence is not execution approval. Does this skip,compensate or resume? No. It confirms a proven native APPLY. Use the separate guides for skipping, compensation, row correction and gap verification. Does it change other targets or source GTID? No. Only the selected subscriber ACK changes;source transactions/GTID and other ACKs remain intact. Whole-task pause applies during the operation;explicitly inspect/resume subscriber and task afterward. Common refusals? FAILURE ACK DISABLED :enable the capability. FAILURE ACK REQUIRES PIPELINE PAUSED :pause the whole task. FAILURE ACK TARGET FENCE REQUIRED :confirm native fencing. FAILURE ACK COMMIT NOT PROVEN :commit content mismatch. ERROR GENERATION CHANGED / FAILURE CHECKPOINT JOURNAL CHANGED :retain fresh evidence. FAILURE ACK METADATA NOT TRANSACTIONAL :repair metadata storage. FAILURE ACK REQUEST CONFLICT :the operation ID was reused with different approval content.

title: COMMON_CUT repair
text: COMMON CUT repair: initial CLI The first MySQL8.4/PostgreSQL17 repair profile passed all four real journal modes. Evidence. Broader production/vendor/capacity acceptance remains incomplete. The console now offers authenticated plan review,execution,cancellation and retry;see Managed repair. A completed, sealed SQL row report and its unchanged globally PAUSED cut are required. Initial execution is limited to MySQL/PostgreSQL transactional destinations owned by this task with completed snapshots and matching schemas. Only the synchronizer may write business tables, including during repair. Accepted initial tables are synchronizer-created with no triggers/foreign keys. The executor rejects detected triggers,incoming/outgoing FKs and PostgreSQL row policies/inheritance;MySQL requires verifiable metadata visibility. Full dependency migration planning is not implemented;see the managed handbook. Other vendors, analytical destinations and queues need separate repair protocols/acceptance. A destination blocked on an earlier failed transaction cannot necessarily reach this cut. Fixing the SQL cause and retrying the original transaction remains its recovery path. Failed-transaction before-image compensation, manual skipping and explicit consistency-gap handling are pending; do not change GTIDs/checkpoints to bypass errors. Review and execution Use the effective V3 task configuration and private report directory: Select explicit nonmatching target/table identities from the report, not SQL table names. The first command writes REPORT UUID/repair-plans/PLAN UUID.json and prints its review content/hash. Review exact table scope, schema/data roots, missing/extra/changed counts and budgets before passing its SHA256 to execution. Plans bind source seal, configuration fingerprint, generation, epoch, sequence, error version and physical destination checkpoints; they contain no raw business values. Keep report/plan files private. REQUEST UUID is a UUID generated for this request. CLI actor IDs are trusted host-operator assertions, not Web authentication, dual approval or controller audit. Do not expose this CLI through an anonymous HTTP wrapper. Authenticated managed repair with revision checks/durable jobs is separately implemented in the managed handbook. Defaults:100000 differing identities,1GiB probe budget per table,4MiB row limit,a10minute paused write-phase budget. Report integrity checks and connection preflight take additional time;this is not a10minute whole-job deadline. Plans retain the full certificate with an8MiB file ceiling. Compact certificates/paged planning and UI budget editing remain pending. Logical quotas require filesystem/container hard quotas for physical enforcement. Transactions and recovery Reports are rechecked for source seal, raw-row integrity, historical destination roots and plan identity. A journal job-row lock prevents concurrent resume/ownership changes. Each table keeps one physical destination checkpoint lock/connection through a full live scan, private disk sort, business DML, full post-scan and receipt commit. The live root/count must match the reported before state. Extra/changed rows are deleted first, then missing/changed source rows inserted. Keyless occurrence IDs are preserved exactly, including duplicate rows. Post-scan root/count must equal the sealed source. Business changes and rm3 sink repair receipt commit in the same local transaction without advancing stream sequence, GTID, transaction ID/hash. Receipts contain plan/schema/before/after hashes, unchanged checkpoint, counts, actor assertion, request hash and timestamp; no business values. Explicit preparation creates only receipt metadata, never missing job/schema/ownership metadata. MySQL DDL may implicitly commit, so fences are reacquired before business work; business tables and all three metadata tables must use InnoDB. Existing receipt columns and primary key are checked; do not drop metadata to bypass identity errors. - SQL failure, drift, corrupt report, count mismatch, quota or deadline rolls back the current table and leaves the pipeline paused. Retry the same plan after fixing its cause; changed target contents require a new validation/plan. - Lost commit reply or process restart:retry the same plan/hash. A matching destination receipt returns alreadyApplied=true without repeating DML. - Multiple tables/targets use separate local transactions. Earlier tables may already be committed when a later table fails. Receipts support partial-progress retry; there is no cross-destination ACID promise. - Once every table is committed, historical receipts can resolve even after resume. They do not prove current live equality. No automatic resume occurs. Review receipts/results, explicitly resume with existing controls and obtain a new cut/report when needed. The original report remains historical and retains its differences. FAQ and boundaries Arbitrary nonempty adoption/schema changes, dependency ordering for foreign keys/triggers, constraint restoration and cutover remain separate work. Deleting changed identities before inserts permits same-table UNIQUE value swaps, but does not establish cross-table/vendor compatibility. SQL failures roll back the current table. Normal exit removes owned probe files. SIGKILL may leave private scratch directories; retry creates fresh probes and never accepts incomplete sorted output. Full scratch retention/cleanup remains pending; never remove active directories. The journal and destination are not a distributed transaction. Journal pause locks guard controls, while destination locks/checkpoints and receipts guard local ordering/commit identity. Extended journal-disconnect/network-partition/node-loss matrices remain pending.

title: Connector, runtime & API compatibility
text: Connector, runtime and API profiles 中文 Choose a profile by source version and topology, target product and mode, then Java runtime. Each row records the scope with native evidence or identifies work still pending. Check the exact candidate hash in the verification baseline and machine-readable manifests before selecting a build for acceptance. Sources and coordinates Configuration Native scope Configuration and recovery --- --- --- MYSQL 5.7.44 Temurin 21 standalone and three-member single-primary Group Replication to MySQL and PostgreSQL. Async GTID promotion and missing binlog refusal passed with a PostgreSQL target. Pipeline configuration, missing-log recovery MYSQL 8.0.46 Temurin 21 standalone and three-member single-primary Group Replication to both SQL targets. Async GTID promotion passed with a PostgreSQL target. Pipeline configuration, recovery runbook MYSQL 8.2.0 Temurin 21 standalone and three-member single-primary Group Replication to both SQL targets. Async GTID promotion passed with a PostgreSQL target. Version-specific test commands MYSQL 8.4.13 Temurin 21 standalone, async GTID promotion and three-member single-primary Group Replication to both SQL targets. Binlog admission and the former group primary returning read-only have separate native proofs. 8.4 binlog profile POSTGRESQL 17.12 Experimental Temurin 21 profile. Synchronized-slot promotion resumes automatically and an earlier timeline is refused. Common-cut verification is pending. Source guide, task example POSTGRESQL 18.7 Experimental Temurin 21 profile. PostgreSQL 17.12 materializes published stored generated columns as ordinary columns. Source guide and publication ORACLE 26ai Free 23.26.4.0.0 Temurin 21 with a separately supplied Oracle JDBC driver. Single-PDB Flashback and single-thread archived CDC to PostgreSQL. RAC and source promotion remain pending. Probe privileges and recovery, V3 example MySQL uses the logical source cluster ID and untagged GTID sets. PostgreSQL uses the logical source ID plus system ID, timeline, slot and LSN. The Oracle probe uses DBID, resetlogs SCN, PDB GUID and SCN. SourcePosition.formatVersion is currently 1 and is interpreted by sourceType . Compare coordinates within the original authority and protocol. The multi-database sample uses formatVersion: 3 , source.clusterId , databases and an explicit mappings object per target. Use independent configurations for separate MySQL clusters. Targets and consistency Target identifiers Scope and delivery contract Manual --- --- --- MYSQL , POSTGRESQL MySQL 8.4 and PostgreSQL 17.12 native transactional targets with business writes and checkpoint in one commit. Relational pipeline GAUSS openGauss 7.0.0-RC3 native transactional profile. Commercial distributed GaussDB constraints, GSI behavior and deployment acceptance are pending. Gauss index policy and takeover DM , KINGBASE , GBASE 8C The first archived native transactional profiles used Java 8. Consult each guide for the exact server mode, driver, field conversions and recovery checks. DM, Kingbase, GBase 8c GBASE 8A , GBASE 8S Planned separate products. Product status OCEANBASE The archived CE 4.3.5.6 MySQL-mode profile passed native transactions, snapshot, CDC, restart and SQL recovery on Java 8. Oracle mode and clusters remain pending. OceanBase CLICKHOUSE , DORIS , HIVE First native analytical profiles. Versioned materialization and receipts, with visibility and replay rules defined per engine. ClickHouse, Doris, Hive KAFKA , PULSAR , RABBITMQ , ROCKETMQ , ACTIVEMQ CLASSIC , ACTIVEMQ ARTEMIS , REDIS STREAMS , NATS JETSTREAM Bounded broker profiles with confirmed at-least-once publishing. Deduplicate stable event IDs and track consumer completion separately. Messaging, ActiveMQ Classic The V3 wizard reads GET /api/capabilities for source availability and limits destinations to the selected engine’s supported products. PostgreSQL and Oracle source forms preserve their separate version, source identity, namespaces and credentials. For each planned or experimental deployment, check the product manual's topology, authorization, retention and backup scope. Release runtime Eclipse Temurin 21 LTS is the sole supported build and runtime. The release uses Java 21 class files. Controller, Agent and Worker processes use Temurin 21 on Linux, Docker and Kubernetes. Record the actual JVM version, architecture and artifact SHA in each native run. Use the matching Temurin 21 fixture to verify a new source, destination, journal or recovery profile. Reproduction commands Each result in the source and destination tables applies to its original candidate and environment. Earlier runtime experiments and profiles such as fiveJdkProcesses , postgresqlSourceRuntimeMatrix and postgresqlStoredGenerated retain their original artifact hashes and reproduction commands in the archive. Verification manifests · Fixed historical snapshot Management requests Use Bearer credentials for CLI or an HttpOnly browser session. Browser writes supply the configured Origin and X-CSRF-Token . VIEWER reads task-scoped status, OPERATOR can issue routine commands within its grants, and ADMIN can configure, inspect sensitive row evidence and authorize data repair. Browser sessions · Grants Endpoint family Request and result --- --- /api/session , /api/session/logout , /api/nodes , /api/tasks Identity and scope, node/owner observation and task pagination. Global creation includes ownerNodeId . Console API /api/tasks/ id /configuration and /api/tasks/ id /actions Mutations bind to the current expectedRevision and original X-Request-ID . Local create returns 201 and local configuration update returns 200. Global mutations and action admission return 202. Follow the persisted operation receipt. Configuration · Command lifecycle /api/tasks/ id /capture-recovery , /api/tasks/ id /capture-exclusions , /api/tasks/ id /failure-evidence Read the retained source failure generation and the authorized target evidence. Source review · Transaction evidence /api/tasks/ id /recovery-plans , /api/tasks/ id /gaps , /api/tasks/ id /gap-verifications , /api/tasks/ id /corrections , /api/tasks/ id /validations Inspect evidence and immutable plan references, then submit the matching action and generation. Skip · Verification · Correction · Managed repair /api/accounts , /api/audit ADMIN account directory and authorized audit reads. Accounts · Audit For example: Use the revision from GET /api/tasks/orders . A repeated request ID reuses the same committed command identity with matching content. Retry uncertain delivery under that ID and reconcile its receipt. Plan IDs, hashes, report IDs, command receipts and pipeline/subscription error generations remain tied to the reviewed source, target and configuration. The recovery runbook shows payloads and completion conditions. A 400 response indicates invalid input, 401 missing or invalid credentials, 403 missing permission or rejected browser authority, and 404 an absent or inaccessible task. A 409 response requires inspecting the returned conflict code and refreshing the revision or generation. A 503 response indicates unavailable shared authority or audit persistence. Resume with the same request ID only if retrying the same action and payload. Global control Upgrade boundaries Record the artifact hash, profile, active configuration version and last confirmed checkpoint before changing JDKs, drivers or deployment settings. Quiesce operations and review destination receipts, journal retention and every persistent store before restoring or changing a topology. Follow the first-release baseline, deployment guide and cutover runbook. Update both language versions and their configuration or API example when a field or profile changes.

title: Configuration revisions
text: Configuration revisions 中文：配置编辑. The console edits configuration, rotates credentials and restores revisions without resetting checkpoints. An earlier Java 8 candidate passed a MySQL 8.4 → PostgreSQL 17 pipeline covering target password rotation, revision restore and controller restart. See the acceptance record for its scope. Only ADMIN can read/edit configuration or its history. GET responses replace passwords, tokens and credential-bearing URLs/options with opaque references; they do not return saved values or ENV references. Retain the reference to keep a value, replace it with a new string to rotate it, or use null/empty where the adapter permits clearing. References are scoped to task, revision, location and target identity. Do not move them between targets. A restart or conflicting edit can require reloading references. No configuration is echoed by a save response. Stop the local task first; a completed PAUSE also permits editing. Pending controls and running workers block updates. Preview reports changed paths and whether migration is required, without old/new secret values. The task ID, synchronization fingerprint and physical journal binding must remain unchanged for this workflow. Changing mappings, products, semantic profiles, databases or journal location requires a separate migration plan. A v2 URL containing embedded credentials is part of its legacy fingerprint: use dedicated password fields for ordinary rotation; this editor does not rewrite legacy checkpoint identity. Save preserves STOPPED/PAUSED intent. Check connections, then explicitly start/resume; shared pause/error generation is never bypassed by a configuration update. Each committed configuration has immutable owner-readable YAML and metadata files under dataDirectory/config-versions/ taskId / . Metadata links its parent hash, editor identity, request ID and time. The controller registry atomically selects one head; staged unreferenced files are not committed history. Canonical task YAML and worker-config files become repairable projections. Workers launch from the committed version, whose content is checked before launch. A missing projection is repaired on restart; a damaged committed version blocks the task and never silently falls back to an older file. Back up the registry, versions, original task files and journal coherently. Existing externally supplied files retain their original startup loading mode until edited through this workflow. UI-created/edited files are controller-managed; editing a projection on disk does not change the committed configuration. Use the editor/API. Independent CLI task files remain ordinary files. Historical versions retain prior credentials: protect the entire private directory, not just current YAML. Automatic version/orphan retention cleanup is not implemented. History is paginated in 20-record pages with signed cursors. Restore previews the paths that change, then creates a new revision linked to the current head; it does not delete history or revert database checkpoints. Old history cursors/references may expire after controller restart or a new configuration head. Fetch history again. Idempotency receipts remain actor/role-bound; their existing bounded retention is separate from configuration history. Version integrity hashes detect corruption relative to the registry. This is configuration provenance, not a tamper-proof security audit against privileged filesystem administrators. Denied/authentication events and asynchronous results now use the separate security audit with retention/export. Exact task authorization is implemented. External immutable anchors and account management remain unfinished. Console workflow 1. Sign in as ADMIN, select a task and open Configuration & history . You can inspect and prepare changes while running; stop the local worker or finish pause before saving. 2. Edit usernames, snapshot chunk rows, poll/retry intervals. For passwords/tokens, choose Keep current value , Replace or Clear . Saved values stay hidden. Advanced JSON supports other fields; newly typed credentials are visible there. 3. Preview changes and review paths. Migration-required changes cannot overwrite the task. Editing again invalidates the preview. 4. Save, check connections/objects, then explicitly start or resume. Saving never starts a worker, clears shared pause or skips a failed transaction. 5. Select a committed revision, preview restore, then save the restore as a new revision. Check connections again: old credentials can fail after a database password change. Closing the editor or signing out clears drafts. Sensitive historical revisions remain in private storage. Load more after each 20 records; the separate 40-operation limit does not truncate configuration history. FAQ Does editing repeat the snapshot? Credential/runtime edits preserve synchronization and journal identity. Actual acceptance retained stream/snapshot identity and continued CDC. Mapping, identity or journal-location changes require migration. What if a task file is edited or deleted? Managed projections are repaired from the committed version. Do not edit projections to change configuration. Damaged versions/registry require a coherent backup restore; removing them is not a recovery shortcut. Why is a revision/history reference rejected? Reload current configuration/history and review concurrent changes. Controller restart or a new configuration head can invalidate old references. What if the old worker cannot stop? WORKER STOP UNCONFIRMED blocks updates. Identify and handle the old process before proceeding; do not bypass confirmation by starting a second configuration. Why are projections pending after save? The version is committed. Repair storage capacity/permissions or conflicting directories and let the controller retry. Keep the registry, versions and journal intact. API - GET /api/tasks/ id /configuration : redacted document and optimistic revision. - POST .../configuration/validate : config, expectedRevision or YAML variant. - PUT .../configuration : same body plus X-Request-ID ; immutable commit. - GET .../configuration/history[?cursor=...] : metadata and restore references. - POST .../configuration/restore/validate : reference, expectedRevision . - POST .../configuration/restore : same body plus X-Request-ID . VIEWER/OPERATOR are rejected before reading mutation bodies or config documents. Version history returns metadata only. Concurrent/stale edits receive 409; malformed or oversized/deep documents receive 400. A successful save can include configurationProjectionPending=true when a non-authoritative file cannot yet be materialized. Preserve the version directory and fix storage permissions/capacity; the controller retries projection repair. It does not pretend an uncommitted file write succeeded or erase previous history.

title: Console & deployment
text: Console, multiple tasks, and deployment Updated: 2026-11-18. 中文：控制台与部署. This page describes implemented behavior; see platform design for the full roadmap. Runtime scope Independent tasks run in isolated JVMs with bounded heap and concurrency. The multi-database wizard configures relational, analytical and eight messaging destinations plus local or external journals. See the connector catalog for product profiles. Legacy single-target tasks remain supported. The bilingual workbench provides creation, connection/source-object checks, start/stop, shared pause/resume, progress/backlog, and operation history. Independent VIEWER/OPERATOR/ADMIN tokens enforce access. ADMIN can edit configuration, rotate credentials and restore revisions. Row validation and reviewed repairs at a common paused cut are available. Transactional PostgreSQL and MySQL have scoped profiles for commit confirmation, transaction skipping, gap verification, compensation and manual correction. Configure the corresponding gates in the first-release baseline. Plan business cutover separately. See validation and repair. Local task control is the default. Opt in with cluster.sharedAccess=true and cluster.sharedTasks=true for fixed-owner global tasks. Any entry manages authorized remote tasks while distinguishing durable admission, actual outcomes and uncertainty. See global control for private directories/keys, upgrade refusal, Helm and native two-node deployment. Automatic execution takeover remains open. Local startup Use Eclipse Temurin 21 LTS for Maven, the Controller, the Agent and each Worker. Open http://127.0.0.1:8080 and enter RIVOMESH TOKEN. Default binding is loopback; tokens require at least 24 bytes and never belong in URLs. Use an appropriate TLS entry point/tunnel for remote access; the embedded server currently serves HTTP. Creation does not start replication. Check connections/objects first, then start. Checks read source definitions and test target connectivity without DDL; startup still validates empty initial targets and DDL/replication privileges. Advanced candidate-node configuration can be loaded from files. Independent configurations Place task YAML files in config/tasks and restart, or use the YAML import button/wizard. Paths resolve against platform.yml. Other directories are not scanned and external edits are not hot-reloaded. Externally supplied tasks not yet edited in the console use private worker snapshots; external reload requires controller restart and identity validation. UI-created/edited tasks use private committed versions and a registry head. Task YAML/worker snapshots are repairable projections; editing them does not change configuration. ADMIN uses Configuration & history to preview/save/restore. See the configuration handbook. Use unique jobIds and distinct replication client serverIds on the same physical topology. Configured destination business/metadata namespace overlap is rejected. Operators must also avoid overlapping physical destinations hidden behind aliases/VIPs. Invalid files are reported independently without blocking valid tasks. Setting Default Meaning --- ---: --- maxTasks 20 Maximum loaded tasks maxRunningTasks 2 Concurrent workers; others wait for capacity workerHeapMiB 256 Maximum worker heap; additionally budget native memory, controller, and databases controlThreads 4 Bound on checks/status/control concurrency pollMillis 3000 Scheduler/status interval autoStart false Initial intent for newly discovered files only; saved intent wins, UI creation always starts stopped Unexpected exits restart with backoff; after five exits CRASH LOOP requires repair and Start/retry. Saved running tasks recreate workers after controller restart using target checkpoints. Changed identity/connection configurations are not silently substituted. Stop, pause, resume - Stop local worker affects this controller's worker only; another deployed standby may take over. - Shared pause persists PAUSED and invalidates owners on initialized tasks. Before initialization only local intent is paused, reported as LOCAL PAUSED NOT INITIALIZED. - Resume after repair is bound to an error generation and retries the original failed transaction. Old requests cannot clear newer failures; restart does not bypass pause. No queues are deleted or GTIDs changed. Database administrators still repair source replication errors. Failed status reads show the last successful time and an explicit stale-data indication. The workbench shows at most 100 tables/task with the total count; other tables continue syncing. Full table status remains available through CLI; paginated search will follow. V3 task details show the Worker process and capture lease separately. captureLeaseState is CLAIMED , EXPIRED , or UNCLAIMED as observed using the journal's clock. The console shows an unknown lease when it cannot read fresh journal state. Consult the source failure stage and checkpoint to diagnose a Worker that is running while capture is stalled. An administrator can open Capture diagnostics in a V3 task from either management entry. The owner supplies timestamped capture-start, phase-failure, retry and journal backpressure events. It scans at most two 64 KiB segments and returns up to 25 records per page using opaque cursors. Endpoint GET /api/tasks/ id /diagnostics?limit=20&after= cursor uses the existing authorization and owner-query limits. A lost owner returns an unavailable query. An expired cursor requires reopening the first page. Phase events omit driver messages, SQL, row values and credentials. The raw Worker logs remain private. Durable files and APIs tasksDirectory stores configurations; dataDirectory/controller.json stores intent, revisions, and operation history using atomic replacement. A file lock permits one controller per directory; corrupt state is not silently reset. V2 checkpoints remain in target metadata. V3 stores capture/snapshot artifacts/subscriber ACKs in LOCAL or EXTERNAL journals, transactional checkpoints with target business data, and confirmed message receipts in the journal. LOCAL uses dataDirectory/journals/pipelineId; use EXTERNAL for cross-host HA. Never delete a journal and continue from old target checkpoints. dataDirectory/worker-configs holds the selected startup configurations and must receive the same credential protection as task files. Configuration files may contain credentials and are written with mode 0600. Task status APIs omit passwords, raw JDBC URLs, row payloads and snapshot key values. ADMIN configuration APIs return editable documents with opaque references for credentials and credential-bearing URLs; ordinary credential-free URLs are visible. Protect directories/backups too. Worker logs rotate between two approximately 8 MiB files and are not served by the Web API. API Purpose --- --- GET /healthz, /readyz Unauthenticated process probes. Readiness returns 503 if configured control services are unavailable.
