GET /api/tasks Sanitized tasks/status/load errors/operations POST /api/tasks Create stopped task using config object or yaml string GET /api/tasks/ id Single-task view POST /api/tasks/ id /actions START / STOP / PAUSE / RESUME / RESUME TARGET / CHECK GET /api/tasks/ id /configuration, /configuration/history ADMIN redacted configuration and revisions POST /api/tasks/ id /configuration/validate, /configuration/restore/validate ADMIN preview edits or restore PUT /api/tasks/ id /configuration, POST .../configuration/restore ADMIN commit/restore a new revision without reverting checkpoints GET /api/capabilities Implemented/partially verified/planned adapters Use Authorization: Bearer. Writes require JSON and X-Request-ID; actions carry expectedRevision and RESUME also global errorCount. RESUME TARGET needs subscriptionId and its independent errorCount. Message pause can leave in-flight publication unconfirmed and does not establish a business cutover fence. HTTP 202 means accepted, with final results under operations. Identical request replays are idempotent. Retain 500 request receipts and 40 operations/task; old requests remain subject to revision checks. One pending operation per task. Docker Compose exposes loopback port 8080, persists control/configuration data, and allows 90 seconds to stop. The image runs nonroot; MAVEN IMAGE/JAVA IMAGE build arguments support prepared internal bases. Images are not publicly published; build/import them. Review bundled driver distribution terms before external release. Linux service Install the JAR at /opt/rivomesh/rivomesh.jar and create a rivomesh account. Copy deploy/linux/platform.yml to /etc/rivomesh/platform.yml and place the token in administrator-readable /etc/rivomesh/platform.env. Install deploy/linux/rivomesh.service, allow the service account to write /var/lib/rivomesh, adjust the Java path, then run systemctl daemon-reload and systemctl enable --now rivomesh. Kubernetes: Helm and native manifests Build and push/import an accessible image first. Prepare a private, untracked .env file containing token=your-private-token: Choose one manager for these resources, not both. Native YAML is rendered from the same Chart defaults. Helm supports existing Secrets/PVCs, storage class, resources, and concurrency, with schema/template validation. Regenerate native manifests using helm template rivomesh deploy/helm/rivomesh --namespace rivomesh. The control plane currently uses one replica, Recreate updates, and persistent PVC. Scaling replicas does not provide controller HA. Existing per-task database lease recovery remains; coordinated multi-controller scheduling is future work. Source outages/paused tasks do not fail process probes. Restart after Secret/native ConfigMap changes under an operational plan while preserving task identity. Manifests include persistence, restricted privileges, read-only root filesystem, temporary storage, graceful shutdown, and probes. Validate actual clusters, CSI, architectures, and OS dependencies separately; rendering is not live Kubernetes acceptance. FAQ Does controller restart repeat the snapshot? Matching task configuration/intact target state resumes existing checkpoints. Controller files do not replace target data/checkpoints. Can another node write after pause? Shared pause uses the same task-row lock as business transactions, so old owners cannot commit new work after pause finishes. Before initialization, local pause has no global effect. Why is a task queued? maxRunningTasks is reached. Stop another worker or adjust configuration/restart within hardware capacity. Why did resume fail? The error generation changed, the target is unavailable, or configuration differs. Refresh/repair rather than editing checkpoints. Do these manifests run every planned target? No. They deploy implemented functionality; planned adapters remain marked unavailable. Development verification Maven verify runs unit and API tests. With Eclipse Temurin 21 LTS, tests/matrix.sh defaults to the V3 standalone, asynchronous GTID failover and Group Replication profiles for MySQL 5.7.44, 8.0.46, 8.2.0 and 8.4.13. Optionally run npm ci --prefix tests/ui --ignore-scripts and npm test --prefix tests/ui for the actual HTML/JavaScript DOM interactions. Node is a development-test dependency only, not a service requirement. After building, python3 tests/deployment-check.py --image rivomesh:0.1.0-SNAPSHOT checks Helm/native parity, nonroot image, authentication, file permissions, request replay, and volume recovery. It removes only its own containers/volumes and never deploys into user Kubernetes clusters. A Chrome smoke test opens the real console, signs in with the keyboard, verifies session restoration after reload and checks the accessible diagnostics dialog and mobile viewport. Broader workflows and browsers have separate acceptance. Browser record The console uses the Rivomesh website wordmark and its light and dark palettes. It follows the browser's system preference until you choose an appearance with the moon or sun control in the navigation. Your browser remembers that choice. Keyboard users can use the first link, Skip to main content , to bypass navigation. Individual access roles Use platform-rbac.yml instead of the shared-token example, set its three token environment variables, then run java -jar rivomesh-app-0.1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar serve config/platform-rbac.yml . Each token must be distinct printable ASCII, 24–4096 characters; unresolved environment references are rejected. At most 32 configured users are accepted, with unique IDs and at least one ADMIN. Tokens are not passwords. Browser sign-in exchanges the token for a revocable short-lived session that survives reload; see sessions, HTTPS/CSRF and sign-out. Role Read tasks/status/catalog Check/start/stop/pause/resume existing tasks Create/import Read/edit configuration and revisions --- --- --- --- --- VIEWER Yes No No No OPERATOR Yes Yes No No ADMIN Yes Yes Yes Yes Roles determine actions; users[].taskIds can restrict VIEWER/OPERATOR to exact tasks. Omission preserves deployment-wide access, an empty array grants no tasks, and ADMIN is deployment-wide. See task grants and revocation. OPERATOR is restricted to CHECK, START, STOP, PAUSE, RESUME and RESUME TARGET; unknown future actions require ADMIN until explicitly authorized. The API rejects forbidden requests before reading a mutation body or invoking the task service. UI buttons reflect those permissions, but the server remains the enforcement boundary. GET /api/session returns the current identity, role, permissions and task scope, never tokens or other accounts. The console refreshes permissions and clears drafts on logout/auth loss; stale responses cannot clear a new login. Default CONFIG uses startup identities. After explicit managed activation, the durable directory is authoritative and restart/configuration changes do not overwrite managed grants. ADMIN account UI/API, rotation and offline recovery are documented in accounts. In CONFIG/bootstrap mode, authToken is the global legacy-admin ; omit it when using only individual accounts. Configured identities require distinct credentials. Managed activation preserves the current identities, after which the durable directory controls changes. Local user/grant UI, rotation and offline recovery are implemented. OIDC/SSO, token expiry and external immutable audit anchors remain unfinished. For Linux use the selected platform file in the existing service command/environment. For Docker or native Kubernetes mount it as the platform configuration and inject the referenced tokens through the deployment secret/environment mechanism. The default Helm/native profile keeps the backward-compatible shared token. For individual roles use the example below; neither profile embeds token values. Do not put literal tokens in committed values or exported diagnostic bundles. For Helm roles, provision Secret rivomesh-accounts with distinct admin-token , operator-token , viewer-token keys, then use helm upgrade --install rivomesh deploy/helm/rivomesh -n rivomesh -f deploy/helm/rivomesh/values-rbac.yaml . For manual YAML use deploy/kubernetes/rivomesh-rbac.yaml instead of the default manifest; choose one manager/profile for the same resources. Both native files are rendered from the Chart and checked for parity. Custom users use auth.users: [ id, role, secretRef: name, key ] , with auth.legacyTokenEnabled: false to disable shared access. At least one ADMIN is required. Duplicate IDs/Secret keys, invalid roles and literal token values are rejected during rendering; different Secret keys with equal actual credentials are rejected by the application at startup. For CONFIG/bootstrap identity only, Secret environment values are read at startup; updating a Secret requires a controlled rollout. Managed identities must instead be rotated through account UI/API. To omit bootstrap credentials use accessMode: MANAGED with matching initialized controller/audit storage; see accounts. New configurations created through HTTP record createdBy , createdRole , createdAt . Task operations record the authenticated actorId and actorRole , including their asynchronous outcome, and retain them across controller restart. The server supplies these fields; request-body identity fields cannot impersonate another account. New idempotency receipts also bind the request ID to that identity/role: matching identity replay is idempotent, another identity receives REQUEST IDENTITY CHANGED . Older receipts without attribution retain their compatibility behavior; old records and direct filesystem/internal API changes are not assigned an invented identity. This is bounded operational history: 40 operations per task and 500 request receipts in the controller registry; the UI displays the most recent eight operations. The independent global store records denied API/security events and asynchronous outcomes, with integrity checks, retention, export and an audit screen; see the security audit handbook. External immutable anchors remain unfinished. ClickHouse V3 targets use native versioned materialization and FINAL query views; transactions can become visible in separate row batches. The wizard defaults to non-unique skipping-index conversion. After Check , expand Check results and operation details in task history to review clickhouseIndexPlans , including unsupported indexes and lost uniqueness/order/global-routing guarantees. YAML import supports explicit clickhouse.secondaryIndexes: NONE for earlier data-only tasks; omitting the new field retains NONE automatically. See the ClickHouse handbook before changing profiles. The Doris wizard configures SQL/Stream Load HTTP origins, redirect allowlist, replicas/buckets and index policy. Default3 replicas; one-BE tests explicitly select1. Expand dorisIndexPlans in check results. Pause leaves materialization in flight unconfirmed, not a cutover barrier. Initial identity checks require a Doris ADMIN account; see the Doris handbook. Optional protocol5 adds administrator evidence creation,raw/normalized pages and typed image review. See review operations for activation/upgrade and deployment profiles. Default legacy profiles do not upgrade automatically. See implementation status for scoped recovery. Two-node live verification The same ARM64 build passed Helm and native YAML on two-node Kubernetes v1.31.0. Each format verified cookie login after refresh, initial delivery, remount of the same RWO CSI volume, incremental recovery, configuration rollout and Secret rotation. The node-local profile uses hostpath.csi.k8s.io . The shared NFS CSI profile also verified a replacement application image and same-claim relocation to another live node without resnapshot or manual START. Load the candidate image on every node of a disposable cluster and enable csi-hostpath-driver . The runner creates and deletes namespaces with unique names. For the shared volume profile, provide a StorageClass that can attach a ReadWriteOnce volume to either node sequentially. Load both images on every node. The isolated NFS fixture uses a Ganesha service and temporary storage. Install the NFS CSI driver and create a StorageClass with provisioner nfs.csi.k8s.io , the Service ClusterIP as parameters.server , parameters.share: / and the tested mount option nfsvers=4.0 . For a planned move, confirm the old Pod has exited before attaching its claim on the new node. Keep the claim UID, PV backing volume and application configuration. Verify the original snapshot ID, a newer lease and incremental delivery before declaring recovery. An external journal can fence concurrent Workers. Agent handoff to a different private directory has separate requirements. See the verification record. The worker-outage profile stops a worker in a disposable Minikube cluster while the database remains on the control plane. CDC resumes with the same volume and a newer lease when the worker returns. Add --worker-outage-node test worker to run the native YAML outage profile. Java 21 deployment The Docker build defaults to the Temurin 21 Maven image and the Temurin 21 JRE. Helm and native Kubernetes use the built application image. For Linux, confirm that the service's Java executable reports Java 21. For a rolling application update, keep one management entry available and follow the durable task checkpoints and owner lease through each replacement. Record the deployed image digest, Java version and application SHA in the deployment evidence. Before replacing a Java 21 application image, record the exact JAR and image IDs, confirm the old version's intended task state and take consistent backups of the Agent directory, control store and external journal where used. Keep the same persistent volume on a rolling restart. If restoration is necessary, stop writers, restore a coordinated point and reconcile target-native receipts before restarting from the saved position. A prior development-format application is outside the first-release rollback scope. Live evidence

title: 达梦 DM
text: DM destination and FAQ 中文：达梦 V3. Example: dm-v3.yml. Scope and instance requirements product: DM is wired into V3 configuration, CLI, bilingual wizard, independent transactional destinations and type plans. Availability remains EXPERIMENTAL . The first DM8.1.4.80 ARM64/vendor Java8 JDBC8.1.3.140 native transaction and actual MySQL8.4.13+PostgreSQL17.12 snapshot/CDC/outage/catchup/worker-kill/separate-SQL-repair/missing-table isolation profile passed; see evidence. Empty-layout guards, text-key case/trailing spaces and four-byte Unicode also passed. PostgreSQL-protocol results do not prove DM support. Use dm.jdbc.driver.DmDriver , jdbc:dm://host:5236 , and pinned Maven Central com.dameng:DmJdbcDriver18:8.1.3.140 . The vendor POM declares Apache-2.0; full distribution license/NOTICE review remains pending. Database installation packages/licenses are not distributed with Rivomesh. The first profile requires COMPATIBLE MODE=0, UNICODE FLAG=1(UTF8), CASE SENSITIVE=1, BLANK PAD MODE=1, NORMAL/PRIMARY and OPEN instance state, and IMMEDIATE/BATCH,WAIT COMMIT WRITE. Each physical connection verifies vendor/version, instance role and these conditions, sets session UTC and checks empty strings remain distinct from NULL. It never changes global parameters or promotes a replica. WAIT is local log-flush durability, not a substitute for storage, replication or fencing policy. Encoding/blank-padding are initialization choices. They protect quoted identifiers, VARCHAR primary keys and trailing-space identities from merging. Other mode/parameter combinations need separate adaptation. Have the DBA assess existing instances and migration/provisioning; do not disguise them as PostgreSQL or reset checkpoints to bypass checks. Configuration and operation Provision the instance and account first. The destination needs mapped-schema/table/index creation, business/checkpoint read/write and directory/instance/parameter read permissions. Apply least privilege in production rather than copying fixture SYSDBA. A successful connection check does not prove every DDL/DML privilege. Each MySQL database maps explicitly to a DM schema; PostgreSQL, messaging and other targets may run independently in the same pipeline. Source GTID/ROW/FULL requirements are in the V3 handbook. Use MYSQL PASSWORD / DM PASSWORD environment references or protected configuration. check returns dmStoragePlans . JSON and precision 38decimals require dm.acknowledgeTextConversions: true ; the wizard explains and requires this acknowledgement. Advanced configurations containing only native types may keep the default false. Acknowledgement does not change layout identity or permit pretending an existing layout is another type. Linux, Docker, Helm and native Kubernetes share the task document; manifests do not deploy DM itself. V2 and the DM Journal backend are not enabled. journal.product: DM is rejected. LOCAL Journal supports same-host recovery; cross-host workers use supported external PostgreSQL/openGauss/MySQL journals. Types and indexes Source model First DM mapping --- --- BOOLEAN / INT64 / UINT64 BIT / BIGINT / DECIMAL(20,0) DECIMAL precision≤38 Declared precision/scale DECIMAL precision 38 VARCHAR(precision+3), lossless decimal text at source scale; acknowledgement required JSON CLOB preserving JSON text/numeric precision; acknowledgement required, not native JSONB STRING Bounded VARCHAR(n CHAR), large text CLOB Bounded binary / large binary VARBINARY / BLOB DATE / DATETIME / TIMESTAMP DATE / TIMESTAMP(6) MySQL TIME INTERVAL DAY(2) TO SECOND(6), preserving sign/microseconds/over24hours Wide decimal text preserves values, not native numeric ordering/comparison/aggregation. Review SQL/types before takeover. JSON text is not equivalent to every vendor JSON type/version. Supported generated expressions follow source support and become ordinary columns. Keyless tables retain rivomesh row id and duplicate multiplicity. Business UNIQUE defaults to ordinary indexes under valid source constraints, complete ordered replication and exclusive synchronization writes. Primary/actual identity keys remain. Simple business GSI can become ordinary indexes, losing global routing/uniqueness. Prefix/expression/descending/fulltext/spatial indexes need plans. CLOB/BLOB indexes cannot be silently copied: DM LOB INDEX REQUIRES PLAN. Existing UNIQUE is never automatically dropped. Arbitrary nonempty adoption, procedures/triggers/foreign keys/partitioning and full DDL evolution still need migration workflows. Transactions, failures and FAQ Business changes and the destination checkpoint commit in one DML transaction, using metadata row locks and increasing epochs to fence old workers. DM DDL may auto-commit; preparation reacquires the fence and never inserts DDL into the business transaction. Targets acknowledge independently rather than using a global atomic commit. - Network/instance outage: recognized transient connection errors back off/reconnect; other sinks continue until journal backpressure. Database operations promote/route primaries. Full primary/replica cluster acceptance is separate. - SQL failure: only that subscription pauses. Repair permissions/constraints/types, then resume in the UI or with resume config/dm-v3.yml dm-business errorGeneration using the current status and the same JAR prefix. Original transactions retry; restart does not skip failures or bypass a pause. - Missing table/owner/checkpoint: refuses an empty replacement under old progress. Preserve evidence and plan a rebuild/reconciliation. - Precision overflow: do not force65digits into38. Review the lossless text plan and business SQL, acknowledge, then recheck. - Character capacity: VARCHAR may default to bytes. Existing layouts check ALL TAB COLUMNS CHAR USED/CHAR LENGTH/DATA LENGTH; byte-based VARCHAR must have worst-case four-byte UTF8 capacity. Binary width is checked and intervals need at least DAY(2)/SECOND(6). Character semantics, large values and page/row limits still need assessment; identical length numbers alone do not prove compatibility. - Case/empty-string/trailing-space differences: check actual initialization/compatibility parameters. Existing custom column rules require separate assessment. - Existing rows/extra constraints: never overwrites rows or silently removes constraints. Normal resume is not the full adoption tool. Reconciliation/repair/cutover workbench remains pending. - Trial expiry: supply a lawfully licensed vendor build. Initialization may report trial limits; no license files/checks are bypassed or modified. Run bash tests/dm-pipeline-run.sh with a locally supplied lawful image, or override RIVOMESH DM IMAGE for the same-layout build. The test creates an isolated project and removes only its own containers/volumes, without privileged mode/host parameter changes. Different images/versions require acceptance; fixture resource limits are not hardware capacity standards. Native Dameng connection with an external Java 21 driver The external-vendor candidate ran on Temurin 21.0.13 with operator-provided Dameng JDBC 8.1.3.140 against Dameng 8.1.4.80 ARM64 in native UTF-8 mode. The test confirmed both external driver origins, missing-driver refusal and the real Dameng missing-table error. MySQL 8.4.13 delivered exact DECIMAL(65,30), UINT64, JSON, binary and keyless data to Dameng and PostgreSQL 17.12. Dameng reconnected on its original endpoint after a database restart. Worker termination preserved the snapshot and progress, and each destination retried its original failed SQL transaction independently. Run with a Java 21 JDK, a locally available compatible Dameng image and the two separately obtained driver files. See the external vendor JDBC build and classpath. Official references: JDBC, initialization, SQL definitions, storage/commit settings.

title: Apache Doris
text: Doris target, recovery and FAQ 中文：Doris V3. Example: doris-v3.yml. Current scope Native MySQL-protocol DDL/metadata and HTTP Stream Load are implemented. Independent native recovery and the actual MySQL+PostgreSQL mixed failure pipeline passed; see archived evidence. The first environment uses official apache/doris:all-in-one-4.1.3 ARM64, internally reporting doris-4.1.3-rc02-7126cf65d96 . This is not acceptance of every Doris release, cluster or production capacity. Doris is an analytical materializer, separate from transactional relational sinks. It is neither a generic transactional MySQL Sink nor an external Journal. Sources remain MySQL; explicit database mappings and fan-out apply. Layout and visibility Each source table owns a private Unique Key/Merge-on-Write physical table in metadataSchema . A source-named view in the mapped business database projects the original column order, hides internal fields and excludes retained tombstones. Internal names derive from pipeline/subscription/generation/table identity and fit the 64-character limit; full ownership hashes remain checked. The internal key represents source PK/identity or normalized keyless occurrence identity, not business UNIQUE(email). Identical keyless values retain distinct occurrences. Sequence/row ordinal fit a LARGEINT version; older writes cannot replace newer state. Deletions retain a current-version tombstone instead of relying on native soft-delete cleanup. Query business views; never mutate private tables or remove tombstones. A Stream Load has native visibility within its table batch, but source transactions can span multiple table/row batches: cross-table source transaction visibility is not atomic . Incomplete snapshots/backlogs are not cutover barriers. Only the sync service writes; this analytical layout is not an equivalent OLTP write takeover. Types and indexes Source normalized type Doris storage --- --- BOOLEAN / INT64 BOOLEAN / BIGINT UINT64 LARGEINT, still checked against the source unsigned-64 range DECIMAL DECIMAL(P,S), configured range 1–76; decimal256 session enabled; MySQL 65-digit values tested FLOAT32 / FLOAT64 FLOAT / DOUBLE; nonfinite input rejected STRING / JSON / DATE / TIME / DATETIME / TIMESTAMP Lossless STRING text, not native JSONB/temporal semantics BYTES / GEOMETRY Base64 STRING, recoverable to original bytes Within the source adapter’s supported expression set, generated columns copy evaluated source values; target expressions are not recreated. NULL differs from missing fields and full images are required. num as string=true prevents intermediate JSON double conversion; source JSON travels inside a string, preserving its internal numbers. Default secondaryIndexes: INVERTED converts plain BTREE/business UNIQUE/generic GSI metadata to nonunique per-column inverted indexes; composites can split. Business uniqueness, source ordering/collation, composite-prefix and global routing semantics are not preserved. Internal row identity is never downgraded. Expression/prefix/fulltext/spatial and unsupported types require a plan; NONE explicitly omits secondary indexes. dorisIndexPlans in check results records decisions/differences. Changing an initialized index/bucket/replica profile requires migration. Connections and permissions url is the FE MySQL-protocol entry, usually 9030. doris.loadUrl is an HTTP origin, optionally a direct BE, usually 8040. FE 307/308 redirects require exact configured redirectOrigins (scheme/host/port), identical paths, no URL credentials/query, and no HTTPS downgrade. Every entry must belong to the same cluster; receipt checks do not replace correct network configuration. Use separate username/password fields and environment references. Initial metadata identity checks use SHOW FRONTENDS/SHOW TABLETS, requiring a dedicated Doris ADMIN account; a least-privilege alternative is unfinished. Console roles are separate. Business readers should access views only. SQL/HTTP TLS still requires acceptance. Default three replicas requires enough BEs. One-BE tests must explicitly select replicas: 1 ; the service never silently lowers redundancy. Replicas range 1–5; buckets default 4, range 1–64. Compose resource limits describe fixtures, not throughput standards. The Web wizard exposes SQL/HTTP origins, redirect allowlist, replicas, buckets and index policy. Check before starting. Check reads source definitions and probes SQL features/HTTP health; it creates no tables and does not establish LOAD/DDL privileges. SQL enforces finite connect/socket timeouts and disables Connector/J cancellation timers to avoid their disconnect-cleanup null pointer. Arbitrary programming errors are not reclassified as networking. HTTP has independent connect/read/request/response bounds and never silently retries an ambiguous PUT internally. Confirmation and failures Loads require strict mode, zero filtering and exact input-row confirmation. Publish Timeout/running labels do not advance checkpoints. Each attempt uses a new load label: versioned rows/permanent destination receipts provide idempotency, not cancelled/expired labels. Success/finished labels still require native row key/version/tombstone/value verification; metadata content is also read back. After confirming data, the service persists a target batch receipt, then Journal transport progress, then the subscription checkpoint. Ambiguous responses/crashes can replay. Destinations acknowledge independently: relational targets can progress through a Doris outage until journal quota imposes backpressure. Restart checks native tablet identity, ownership, DDL, views and latest confirmed receipt. Initialized missing objects are not recreated empty at an old checkpoint. Restoring a coherent older nonempty FE+BE backup while keeping a newer journal is refused when the newest receipt is absent. Restore the right target or plan a rebuild. Coordinate data, metadata and journal backups; arbitrary per-table/incoherent rollback or external tampering requires reconciliation and is not comprehensively detected. Pause reports UNCONFIRMED IN FLIGHT MATERIALIZATION ; already submitted requests cannot be retracted. Relational targets may report FENCED. This is not a Doris business cutover barrier. Deterministic data/schema/permission faults pause that subscription; after repair resume its error generation without skipping the original transaction. FAQ Where are business UNIQUE/GSI constraints? They become nonunique acceleration. Source enforcement and exclusive synchronization preserve caught-up data; external writes are unsupported. Doris internal UNIQUE KEY protects row identity, not business uniqueness. Why views and private tables? They hide occurrence IDs, versions and tombstones while preserving public column order. Do not replace views with unrelated tables or treat private storage as identical source DDL. SQL connects but loading fails? HTTP health does not test LOAD privilege, and SQL/HTTP are separate entries. Verify same-cluster origins, accounts, privileges and explicit FE redirect destinations. Does one SQL fault stop all targets? Deterministic faults pause their target. Repair and use independent UI resume or resume config.yml subscriptionId expectedErrorGeneration ; do not edit GTIDs/checkpoints. Can it adopt existing nonempty objects? Current ownership checks create missing private objects/views and reject conflicting existing data/layout. Adoption, live DDL, layout migration and cutover workflows remain unfinished. Does retained space clean itself? Source journals reclaim by independent ACK. Target receipts/tombstones/indexes are outside logical journal quota and need storage monitoring. Receipt compaction/retention, soak and hardware capacity reports remain unfinished. Primary references and limits Design references: Stream Load, Unique Key concurrency, JSON precision, tablet identity/privileges, official fixture image. Product documentation is not project acceptance; see validation. Complete clusters/compute-storage separation, combined FE/BE faults, TLS, huge catalogs/transactions, adoption/repair/migration and capacity matrices remain pending. SQL modes and text validation Catalog, receipt and row-verification values use binary server-prepared MySQL parameters. The adapter forces useServerPrepStmts=true and emulateUnsupportedPstmts=false ; an unsupported protocol fails instead of silently reverting to literal interpolation. DDL comments contain safe internal identifiers only. Actual Doris4.1.3/Java8 EMPTY and NO BACKSLASH ESCAPES profiles passed quoted/backslash names, Unicode/emoji text, snapshot, CDC and session reconstruction. Malformed UTF-16 fails deterministically with DORIS TEXT ENCODING INVALID , rather than retrying invalid text indefinitely; see additional evidence. Sources: Doris prepared statements, string literals. After the binding change, current release9a087 also passed an actual MySQL8.4.13→PostgreSQL17.12+Doris4.1.3 pipeline with outage catch-up, worker kill, SQL repair/retry and missing-view isolation. The native mode/old-backup case used11667063; all14Doris adapter classes match9a byte-for-byte. See additional evidence for artifact and scope distinctions. Java 21 outage and receipt verification The ARM64 fixture uses MySQL 8.4.13, PostgreSQL 17.12 and the single-container Doris 4.1.3 image. During the Doris outage, PostgreSQL advances while Doris retains its acknowledgement and exact receipt. The original receipt and its successors remain readable on the same Doris metadata tablets after the target and Worker restart. After a PostgreSQL constraint violation, replay to that subscription leaves the Doris receipt unchanged. The fixture also verifies that a lost Doris view pauses that subscription and marks its pause fence as unconfirmed. Run RIVOMESH TEST PREBUILT=1 bash tests/doris-pipeline-run.sh after building the Java 21 release JAR and test classes. The fixture uses disposable databases and the same Doris volumes across its stop and start. Its single FE and BE cover connector behavior, with multi-node failover outside this profile. Apache Doris all-in-one test image · Verification record

title: Controller and Agent lifecycle
text: Separate management entries and execution Agents 中文 · Global control The protocol4 separated profile passes348app/actual-JAR tests,76DOM and5x152controls,PG/MySQL stores,actual multi-database/two-target CDC,all-controller loss,store outage,pending accepting-entry recovery,nonroot processes and SQL role races.Automatic Agent takeover and complete journal/adapter/JDK matrices remain open. Evidence. Configuration role Registry role Responsibility --- --- --- COMBINED CONTROLLER WORKER Compatible management/local execution in one process CONTROLLER CONTROLLER UI/API,shared login,configuration and durable admission;execution capacity0 AGENT AGENT Fixed-owner execution,Worker supervision,observations and typed reads;HTTP probes only Activation Every member sets cluster.sharedAccess=true,sharedTasks=true,separateExecution=true and an explicit role. Control database,cluster.id,namespace and Base64 task key match; node IDs and private directories/volumes are independent. separateExecution=false keeps protocol3 combined behavior; defaults do not silently become separated deployments. Separation uses protocol4. Stop all old members normally and confirm STOPPED before upgrade; expiry/unreachability is insufficient. Preserve tasks,journals,reports,keys and directory UUIDs. Old programs refuse the new protocol; direct database downgrade is unsupported. An existing combined owner with tasks retains its original nodeId/directory when reopening as AGENT. A controller refuses an execution directory with tasks,including shared ownership hidden behind an empty replacement directory. Legacy local-to-global import remains a separate migration. Controllers cannot receive execution tasks. Create requests specify an Agent; the UI filters controllers and pages to find Agents. Committing transactions recheck role/ownership instead of trusting an earlier directory/role read. Linux The controller example uses8080;the Agent example uses8081. Adjust control connections and supply token,control credentials and task key environment values,then run independently: Use separate configuration copies/directories and distinct ports on one host. Supervise with separate systemd services; management service dependencies must not stop the Agent. Agent termination stops its own supervised Workers. Docker Build the current image first. Supply RIVOMESH TOKEN,RIVOMESH TASK KEY,RIVOMESH CONTROL URL,RIVOMESH CONTROL USERNAME,RIVOMESH CONTROL PASSWORD. The example assumes PostgreSQL control storage: It creates controller-a,controller-b,agent-a with three private volumes. Management ports bind loopback8080/8082;Agent probes bind8081. Browser access still needs HTTPS/proxy configuration for production cookies. Stopping management must not delete/stop Agent state. The file does not create the external control database. Helm and native Kubernetes Use the shared Secrets documented under global control,then install independent releases: Without Helm,adapt/apply native manifests A,B,Agent. Each release has one replica/private PVC. Add Agents with distinct releases/node IDs/volumes. Static rendering/invalid-setting checks exist;live Kubernetes/CSI/node-fault acceptance is separate. Deployment profiles Deployment Single instance Multiple management entries and Agents --- --- --- Linux Systemd unit and platform file Independent Controller and Agent launches above Docker Standalone Compose Execution Compose Kubernetes with Helm Chart defaults Controller values and Agent values Native Kubernetes Standalone manifest Controller A, Controller B, Agent A For either Kubernetes path create the namespace, provide the control database accessible from pods, and create rivomesh-auth (key token ) and rivomesh-control-store (keys username , password , task-key ) from protected files. Linux and Docker pass the same values through the environment. Set sessions.secureCookie: true and the same HTTPS sessions.publicOrigin on each management entry behind one ingress. Keep Agent probes on the deployment network. Use database TLS and trusted CA settings supported by the selected JDBC profile. See session deployment and shared credentials. If there is no independent database available for control metadata, deploy standalone with its private directory. LOCAL journals use the owning Agent's private directory or PVC. EXTERNAL journals put capture transactions, snapshot pieces and subscription checkpoints in a separate database namespace. Shared task definitions, accounts, sessions and command metadata remain in the control store. Agent-local validation/repair reports, audit projections, keys and Worker configuration remain part of the owner recovery set. Journal settings · Shared control Enrollment, maintenance and restoration 1. Enroll each Controller and Agent with a unique stable nodeId and private directories. Verify the role and fresh registration in Nodes and GET /api/nodes . Choose the intended Agent when creating a task. Record the owner and directory or PVC identity. 2. To drain an Agent for planned maintenance, stop assigning new tasks, issue STOP through either entry for each owned task and wait for original request receipts and stopped Workers. For a controlled cut, pause first and verify destination acknowledgments. Confirm capture leases are inactive before stopping the Agent service. Restart the same node/volume and explicitly start stopped tasks when maintenance is complete. 3. For a coordinated backup, quiesce the tasks and management writes. Back up the control database, all private node directories and keys, external journals if configured, and target business/checkpoint stores at the approved cut. Use a database-consistent backup method for each store. Preserve permissions and volume identity. Restore a matched set in an isolated environment, verify the node/configuration identities and each target receipt, and only then resume. Recovery and cutover 4. Before changing the release, runtime or drivers, record the active artifact, configurations and checkpoints. Keep the same node IDs, paths and keys during the rehearsal. Use separate validation for deployments with mixed versions or cross-node volume replacement. The initial release procedure uses a controlled stop and restart. First-release configuration · Compatibility matrix The live evidence includes Helm and native YAML on a two-node Kubernetes cluster, configuration and Secret replacement, local CSI remount and Worker-node interruption. Cross-node CSI availability and automatic Agent relocation have separate acceptance. Kubernetes live evidence Recovery FAQ What if every management entry stops? The Agent independently reads the shared queue. The tested LOCAL/H2 profile continues CDC;management rejoin reads the same owner and authority. This does not relocate execution to another Agent. Does CDC survive control-store failure? In the tested LOCAL/H2 profile,the same Worker continues source capture and independent business writes. Management APIs/registration readiness refuse control without local-account fallback. Recovered storage permits renewed registration and observations. External-journal shared failures,other adapters and production topologies require their own profiles. Why does the Agent have no login page? Its HTTP endpoint serves GET /healthz and /readyz only;administration paths return404 AGENT PROBE ONLY. Use management entries;typed owner queries travel through shared storage. What if the Agent exits or is killed? Its Workers are affected;management shows pending/unknown. Restore original Agent directory,nodeId and keys;queued offline STOP is processed before restoring old RUNNING intent. Expiry does not prove process termination. Automatic takeover/stale-Worker fencing remain CP-04. Are Agent secrets least-privilege isolation? No. Agents remain in the trusted control domain;Workers filter controller environment variables. Roles do not establish tenant/OS isolation. Least-secret/external-identity work remains separately tracked. NODE ID IN USE after restart? SIGKILL leaves an old lease until expiry;never bypass the guard.Supervisors may retry normally;if another member keeps renewing,fix duplicate configuration. VALIDATION BARRIER MOVED immediately after configuration restart? Process liveness and already-equal rows do not establish a new journal claim.Check shared state and actual incremental catchup before retrying.The task detail shows the capture lease separately from Worker process status.

title: Failed transaction diagnostics
text: Failed-transaction diagnostics and manual recovery 中文 The UI supports destination phase summaries,original incremental retry,snapshot-part recovery and administrator transaction review. Bounded inspection/durable evidence now back explicit raw/normalized event pages. Administrators can review the transaction skip, before-image compensation, typed correction and common-cut repair workflows. UI workflow 1. Open the paused destination in task details. Record destination ID,error generation,ACK,error code,phase and failed sequence when available. 2. For activation faults,check connectivity,credentials,permissions and metadata. For apply faults,check types,constraints and destination data. For projection faults,check mappings and historical schemas. For reconciliation faults,verify native receipts and journal ACKs before changing anything;do not manually advance positions. 3. Fix the cause and select “Resume this target.” The request binds its error generation,retrying the whole original incremental transaction or reconciling/resuming snapshot parts. Stale generations refuse. Pipeline resume and destination resume are distinct. 4. Check catch-up and run appropriate reconciliation. Accepted commands,live processes or matching ACKs alone do not prove business takeover readiness. Activation can fail before a transaction is identified,so no invented failed sequence is shown. Legacy pauses without trusted phase records remain Unknown. Corrupt diagnostics are visibly unavailable and raw inspection refuses. Equal SQLStates do not make activation and apply faults equivalent. Existing global task queries carry summaries through different management entries. Summaries contain only phase,sequence and failure epoch;no event IDs,row values,SQL or credentials. Existing task-view grants apply. Ordinary status does not gain raw-value access. Initial preparation/snapshot have dedicated diagnostics;legacy records may remain Unknown. Source diagnostics appear separately at task level. See native snapshot evidence. Accepted scope and evidence cover internal inspection,two-entry real SQL fault/restart and five-JRE foundation contracts;they do not accept the complete manual recovery workflow. Recovery by target product Adapter capabilities shows the recovery modes supported by each destination. GET /api/capabilities returns transactionSkip , transactionCompensation , failureReceiptReview , gapNotification and rebuildMode for target entries. Target Transaction skip and compensation Rebuild --- --- --- PostgreSQL, MySQL Review the complete failure, then use the available local transaction or before-image workflow. The task must meet its pause, fence and evidence requirements. Plan a fresh baseline and empty destination manually. Other selectable destinations Restore the original connection, schema or broker history and retry the original event. Skip and compensation are unavailable. Plan a fresh baseline manually when the old history cannot be recovered. Planned destinations Unavailable Unavailable MANUAL NEW BASELINE describes an operator-managed project. Keep the original journal, destination receipts and evidence until the new baseline has been checked. A resume action uses the existing destination identity and checkpoint. Read the preceding destination receipt Pause the task and select Check destination receipt on the failed ClickHouse, Doris, Hive, ActiveMQ Artemis, ActiveMQ Classic, RocketMQ, Redis Streams, NATS JetStream or Pulsar subscription. The review requires a complete failed incremental transaction and a retained acknowledged predecessor. It verifies the original target resource and the exact native COMMIT receipt. A later partial batch or an older snapshot receipt fails verification. The review preserves the failed transaction and all subscription positions. Use POST /api/tasks/ task /destination-receipt with expectedRevision , subscriptionId and errorGeneration . A permitted administrator can submit the same read through either Controller. Use java -jar rivomesh.jar review-destination-receipt config.yml target error-generation from the CLI. Classic's independently retained receipt binds the last event digest as well as the batch digest. Older receipt records can resume normal synchronization. They become eligible for exact failure review after the next confirmed COMMIT. Artemis browses its original non-destructive queue, and RocketMQ reads the known commit-log offset without committing a consumer offset. The review exposes only the saved cut and digest. Redis Streams uses XRANGE on the saved entry ID, JetStream reads the saved stream sequence and checks the stream creation timestamp, and Pulsar reads the saved ledger and entry through its admin API. Verification requires the retained record, the original ownership binding and the exact event digest. Before this feature was enabled, an existing subscription needs one newly acknowledged COMMIT to obtain a receipt. Purging or trimming the saved record blocks verification. For a RabbitMQ quorum or classic queue, use manual reconciliation based on retained consumer evidence if the business message has already been acknowledged. An open gap, a prepared skip review or a destination that has fallen behind can retain journal payloads past a restart. The collector checks the minimum acknowledged sequence across destinations and retains raw and normalized bytes for unresolved gaps. During incremental capture a full journal reports JOURNAL BACKPRESSURE and preserves that evidence. The Kafka notice operation reports a failure and preserves original synchronization progress. Kafka approvals and recovery Source pipeline failure phases A blocked capture records error stage , the error generation and the latest valid GTID in task details. The Worker reports an observation when it cannot open the journal. Destination retry, compensation and skip actions depend on reviewable destination evidence. Phase Action --- --- Source connection, discovery or binlog read Check primary availability, permissions and required GTID history. Verify that capture resumes when the source becomes available. Source snapshot Check read grants and snapshot locks. Verify chunk progress and the baseline position. Decode Retain the original binlog and inspect the row images and event profile. If the transaction boundary is uncertain, restore the required logs, use an eligible source containing that history, or establish a new baseline. DDL or normalization Compare the historical schema, field types and failing transaction before reviewing the schema plan. Journal storage or acknowledgment Restore journal access and capacity. Verify the target receipt, journal acknowledgment and capture position. Internal inspection limits Journal.inspectFailure(subscription, expectedErrorGeneration, maximumBytes) reads only a paused subscriber's next whole transaction. It binds stream generation,current epoch,configuration fingerprint,error generation and ACK and verifies raw/existing normalized hashes. It never connects to or activates business destinations,creates normalization,changes keyless identities or advances ACK. Missing complete boundaries refuse rather than being guessed. Raw and normalized payloads share a maximum4MiB budget;diagnostics have a separate16KiB limit. Stored-length checks and bounded character streaming enforce limits,with UTF-8 byte verification. Unconsumed normalization reservations may conservatively refuse a payload early. Oversize refuses the whole review rather than approving a truncated transaction. Streaming large-transaction review remains open. This low-level inspection is not an execution plan;managed access adds durable creation,authorization and audit. Its returned object alone is not durable evidence or approval. Paused ACKs pin history;resume can allow collection. UI review reads retained records. For a proven target commit with a missing journal acknowledgment, use the commit acknowledgment workflow. Explicit transaction skip records a gap for the selected target. Preparation/snapshot faults explicitly refuse inspection as failed incremental transactions. FAQ Can I skip an error like a MySQL replica? Use controlled transaction skip for a full transaction at a supported destination. It records the native receipt and a durable gap. Editing ACKs or GTIDs or deleting logs breaks the history needed for recovery. What if the destination committed but the response was lost? Automatic delivery verifies destination checkpoints,transaction IDs and projected-content hashes before repairing journal ACKs. Unknown outcomes stop/retry rather than authorizing skip. Manual compensation must reconcile first too. Can a source update fix an old transaction? It creates a new transaction;persisted old events remain unchanged. Fix the destination condition preventing old replay. Use compensation preview to compare historical images with the current destination. Does restart clear an error? No. Pause,error generation and phase diagnostics persist. Explicit resume remains necessary. Healthy destinations may continue while the paused subscriber retains history and consumes quota. Can Unknown be treated as an apply error? No. Legacy records,corrupt diagnostics and capture/decode faults do not establish a known skippable transaction. Inspect source history,retention and historical configuration first. What if required binlogs were purged or cannot be decoded? Destination resume cannot recreate source history. Restore logs,use a qualified source retaining required history or prepare a new baseline/rebuild. Capture-side range exclusion remains open under RC-04. Can I patch destination rows directly? Synchronization assumes exclusive destination writes. Unplanned edits can affect constraints,keyless identities and replay. To edit approved rows while the task is paused, use typed correction.

title: Failed transaction evidence
text: Failed-transaction evidence storage 中文 · Recovery Storage/capture now backs managed review,including administrator/task authorization,audit and protocol5 gates. This page explains files/limits. Successful retention does not prove destination non-commit or authorize skip,compensation or takeover. Earlier internal acceptance is distinct from the current managed profile. Contents and identity Immutable evidence binds review/request IDs,actor/time,task,original execution node/directory,configuration revision,stream generation/epoch,error generation,ACK and whole-transaction hashes. It retains raw/existing normalized transactions and their referenced historical schemas. Missing normalization remains explicit;review does not normalize or change keyless identities. Schema lookup uses only referenced tableId/schemaVersion pairs,not the full catalog. Missing,corrupt or mismatched schemas refuse capture. Published evidence remains readable after journal collection. It records a historical observation;execution still requires fresh configuration,position,native receipt and drift checks. FailureEvidenceCapture.capture first checks an existing review ID against request,actor,revision,destination and error generation,returning the original result without requiring retained journal history. Changed content,identity or request parameters cannot overwrite the original. Private files and quotas - Defaults:256MiB directory budget,1000records,8MiB per record,configured through internal FailureEvidenceStore.Limits . Files,keys,authority and orphan temporaries count toward the budget;this is not total disk-block/database/backup capacity. - Directories use0700;created records,keys,authority and lock files use0600. Reject symlinks including parent paths. Preserve private permissions in installation and backups. - A random32-byte evidence.key authenticates records; authority.json binds original task/node/directory. Content hashes and strict JSON parsing refuse truncation,duplicate fields and trailing JSON. - Cross-process locking,private temporaries,file fsync,atomic publication and directory fsync protect publication/quotas. Busy locks refuse explicitly;callers retry the original request. - Full quotas refuse new evidence without deleting old records. Automatic expiry/GC/key rotation is not exposed. Orphan .pending files are not valid evidence,remain counted and are not silently deleted. Physical disk/power-loss acceptance remains open;unit tests do not establish it. Summaries and pages Summaries expose identity,phase,positions,hashes and event counts without row images or SQL. Raw/normalized events paginate separately,at most100events/256KiB per page. A single oversized event refuses rather than returning truncated images. Every page carries the immutable evidence hash and next index. Journal inspection still limits combined raw/normalized content to4MiB and historical schemas to2MiB. Streaming large-transaction review remains open. File/page limits do not bypass capture limits. Preserve history during an Agent handoff For a managed writer with a verified stopped cut and journal and control state in the same PostgreSQL database, the original Agent authenticates stored failure records with its private HMAC key. After verifying the same archive, the candidate stages the signed authority, original records, validation reports and closed operation receipts in its private directory. Approve ownership transfer using the same preparation in the console. The commit binds the verified stage to the journal cut and successor configuration. The Worker remains stopped. An administrator with access to the task and both Agents can use GET /api/tasks/ taskId /handoff/failure-history through either Controller. The response lists the evidence IDs, byte lengths and SHA-256 digests, with an adoption digest. Supported closed operation receipts remain searchable by request ID through /api/tasks/ taskId /recovery-receipts/ requestId . The console shows how many records were staged and adopted. Historical reads verify the candidate copy and survive a candidate restart without the shared archive or staging directory. The original Agent keeps the HMAC key. The candidate stores the original signed bytes in handoff-adopted/ id /historical-failures , separate from the live evidence store. The API serves metadata and digests. Use the normal recovery approvals for corrections, skips, target writes or Worker start. When a Controller is interrupted before commit, replay the same ownership request through either Controller. When a task has both kinds of history, use one preparation to stage the MySQL raw capture ZIP and the signed failure records. Ownership commit verifies both private stages against the same approved cut and refuses a missing or damaged copy. After adoption, both history endpoints return the same preparation ID and adoption digest. For an older stage sealed without these records, release the preparation and stage a fresh one. Managed handoff controls FAQ Can a lost key be regenerated? No. Existing authority/evidence without the key refuses initialization;wrong keys fail signatures. Restore key,authority,evidence and original directory identity together,including private permissions. How can I retain evidence when transferring the task? Use the reviewed handoff to preserve the original signed files as read-only history. A copy into a different Agent’s live evidence directory fails the owner and directory checks. Does retention freeze destination commit status? No. Capture does not connect to or activate business destinations and never assumes non-commit. Manual native-checkpoint reconciliation remains RC-05. How can I skip or correct data after reviewing evidence? Use the recovery flow that supports the destination. It rechecks the current cut, native receipts and approval scope, then records the gap and recovery receipt. Use handed-off history to locate the original incident and its closed receipts. Transaction skip · Managed repair

title: Retain and review failure evidence
text: Managed transaction evidence review 中文 · Diagnostics · Files/quotas This workflow passes the documented bounded profile. Review only retains/reads historical evidence. It does not skip,compensate,change GTIDs or automatically resume. First deployment Configure all controllers and Agents using thefirst-release baselinebefore startup. Development-version in-place upgrades/automatic mode migration are unsupported. Linux,Docker,Helm and manual Kubernetes share identity/storage requirements. Metadata DDL requires appropriate privileges;restart recovery and missing-history refusal remain supported. Start from a paused destination 1. Sign in as ADMIN and check the paused destination's phase/error generation. Preparation/snapshot faults use their own recovery paths rather than failed incremental review. 2. Select “Retain transaction evidence.” The operation persists its review ID before capturing the whole head transaction/historical schemas.202means accepted only. After success,select “Review transaction evidence” in operation history. 3. Inspect original task revision,configuration fingerprint,owner/directory,source identity,GTID/log position,transaction/event range,historical tables,image availability and hashes. ACK/epoch are historical observations,not current destination commit proof. 4. Explicitly show raw or normalized events. Historical column names/types accompany before/after images. SQL NULL,JSON text null ,Not provided and Not applicable remain distinct. Expand raw details for internal row identities. 5. Page through complete events bound to the same evidence hash. Oversized events refuse rather than truncate. Missing retained normalization disables that view. OPERATOR/VIEWER cannot create/read evidence,including direct URLs. Raw values do not enter ordinary task status,operation results or audit bodies. Logout clears/closes review and stale responses cannot reopen old-session data. Both entries use the same durable command/original-owner query. Repeating the same request ID retains one review ID. Original-directory Agent recovery preserves evidence,including after journal GC. Unavailable original Agents/control stores refuse rather than returning invented local data. configurationRevision in the summary is the create action's original task revision. The configuration fingerprint is separate;this field is not a configuration-history restore reference. API mapping Create through the existing action route with X-Request-ID : Poll task operations for completion/ failureEvidenceId . Retry the original request parameters/ID. - GET /api/tasks/ task /failure-evidence/ id :administrator summary. - POST /api/tasks/ task /failure-evidence/ id /events :administrator pages with "view":"RAW","from":0,"limit":20 or NORMALIZED . - Cookie POSTs retain CSRF/Origin checks;Bearer APIs remain compatible. Stale generation/revision,authorization changes,corruption and limits refuse explicitly. Native checkpoint comparison and proven-commit confirmation New review operations attempt a read-only native checkpoint comparison for transactional PostgreSQL/MySQL destinations. The operation retains the observation; the evidence dialog displays it: - Checkpoint not advanced : native progress equals journal ACK. This does not prove business data is absent. - Committed but unacknowledged : native progress is exactly ACK+1 and transaction ID/projected hash both match. Reconcile acknowledgment before any skip or compensation. - Unavailable/refused : display a safe problem code. Missing normalization, changed epoch/error generation, collected history, unavailable/unsupported destinations must not imply a commit verdict. Retained evidence remains readable. This is a historical observation made while retaining evidence. Opening old evidence does not query the destination; retain new evidence to compare again. Inspection neither activates targets nor advances ACK. A lagging target epoch is explicitly reported as requiring fencing before a later mutation. Older members returning no observation are shown as unavailable. Eligible administrators can use proven-commit confirmation;skip and compensation remain unimplemented. The bounded read-only profile passed. The managed confirmation bounded profile also passed;skip and compensation remain separate,and RC-02 historical scope is unchanged. FAQ and limits Does saving resume replication? No. Business data,ACK,GTID and pause intent remain unchanged. Fix the cause and explicitly resume separately. Can review edit or skip? No. Proven commits can be acknowledged through the separate confirmation workflow. Administrators can use separate reviewed operations for whole-transaction skip, compensation and target corrections. Why is creation unavailable to an administrator? Shared review may be disabled. Old profiles do not accept new commands;follow normal stop/upgrade steps for every member. Why no transaction or a changed generation? The target may have resumed,changed fault,lack a complete incremental head or lack historical schemas. Recheck state;do not advance positions manually. Why refuse a replaced directory/key? Evidence binds the original directory and HMAC key. Restore records,key,authority and directory identity together rather than substituting empty storage/new keys. Are files encrypted or automatically cleaned? Files use private permissions/HMAC integrity;business content is not encrypted by this store. Protect backups,volumes and accounts appropriately. Automatic cleanup,key rotation and an evidence directory management UI remain open;full quotas preserve old records and refuse additions.

title: First-release configuration
text: First-release configuration baseline No first release has been published. In-place upgrades between development candidates,old package aliases and automatic control-mode migration are unsupported. Internal format numbers are not released versions. Eclipse Temurin 21 LTS is the sole supported runtime for building and running the release. Controllers, Agents and Workers all use Temurin 21. Choose the control store,access mode,roles,keys and persistent directories before first deployment. Enable full managed recovery consistently across all members: Namespaces are created directly in the configured mode. Mismatches refuse immediately,even after every member stops. Existing development environments require a separately assessed new test baseline;deleting code history does not authorize clearing business data or moving only cursors. Linux/Docker use the same role configuration and independent persistent directories. Helm overlays controller/Agent values with values-recovery-skip.yaml ;manual Kubernetes can reference rivomesh-skip- .yaml . Examples do not establish liveK8s/CSI acceptance. Restart recovery,leases/epochs,authorization revocation and damaged/stale-backup refusal are current behavior rather than obsolete development compatibility. Replace superseded development implementations directly. Do not retain branches,configuration aliases or upgrade tests solely for old prerelease candidates. Documents describe current behavior;duplicate evidence/build snapshots converge on one verification baseline. Keep tests that validate current data correctness,recovery and security boundaries. Remove temporary containers,obsolete project images and intermediate builds once unused. Back up and restore a LOCAL journal Stop the task and close every process connection to its H2 journal before copying the LOCAL directory. Create a coordinated recovery point that includes the task configuration, journal, and destination business data, snapshot metadata and transaction receipts. Include applicable Agent and control-store state for managed tasks. Use each destination's consistent backup procedure and retain the source log history needed by the saved checkpoint. H2 backup procedure Restore into isolated storage first. Check the pipeline and journal generation, snapshot IDs, source position, target checkpoint and receipt before resuming. A divergent target checkpoint pauses delivery. A pending journal transaction with a damaged payload checksum fails on read. Preserve the original backup while investigating either failure. The current-package fixture copies a closed LOCAL journal and an H2 JDBC test destination, feeds synthetic MySQL GTIDs and verifies restore, deduplication, mixed-time checkpoint refusal and pending-payload corruption refusal. The native MySQL 8.4 to PostgreSQL 17 drill shuts down the Worker and H2, takes the cold journal and a PostgreSQL custom-format dump at one fenced checkpoint, then restores the database contents in a single transaction. The original PostgreSQL database retains its cluster identifier and database OID. The restart delivers a MySQL transaction committed during the outage from the original GTID, preserving both snapshot IDs. Restoring the dump into a separate database and changing the configured target URL fails with JOURNAL IDENTITY MISMATCH . PostgreSQL dump · PostgreSQL restore Run the drill with a Java 21 JDK, Docker Compose and local mysql:8.4 and postgres:17 images. V2/V3 execution consolidation is a separate pending batch. Seecurrent status;cleanup does not close unrelated feature gaps.

title: Data-gap verification
text: Data-gap verification 中文 · Transaction skipping · First-release configuration Plans,approval,fresh scans and durable receipts are implemented for transactional PostgreSQL/MySQL destinations. Verification neither repairs data nor reapplies skipped transactions,nor automatically resumes replication. Console workflow 1. Resolve differences and run a new complete common-cut comparison. Select a COMPLETE,MATCH report with sealed source data. An old report alone does not establish current target correctness. 2. Click “Select gaps and prepare verification” in the report. Choose a target and unverified gaps,enter a reason and maximum duration. A plan covers at most100 gaps/1000 affected tables;default300seconds,range1–86400seconds. 3. Open the prepared plan in “Transaction recovery and data gaps”. Review target,report,cut,table names,source counts,content roots,gap scope and duration. Tables are paged in groups of50. 4. Confirm scope and exclusive sync-service target writing,enter an approval reason,and choose “Approve scope and verify again”. ADMIN is required;202 only acknowledges command admission. 5. Inspect the resulting VERIFIED AT COMMON CUT receipt. It establishes reviewed table equality at that historical cut only. Original SKIP history remains and the task stays paused. Cutover requires separate checks. External application/administrator writes bypass this fence and invalidate its operating assumption. Planner and approver are separately recorded;different accounts are not mandatory. Management entries may differ;the original Agent uses its recoverable report directory. Moving only a cursor does not replace journals,reports or original records. API Require ADMIN,task/node grants and matching expectedRevision ;cookie sessions also require CSRF. Use a stable X-Request-ID . An unknown response is retried with the identical ID and original body,without changing reason/scope. Send POST /api/tasks/ task /actions : errorCount is task status error count ,the whole pipeline generation rather than a subscriber's error count. The command request ID becomes the plan ID. Read it through GET /api/tasks/ task /gap-verifications/ planId . After review,submit GAP VERIFY EXECUTE with the same target,current task revision and the plan's errorGeneration : Execution cannot select another report,gaps or duration. GAP VERIFY CANCEL carries no gap object. Inspect task operations and the original plan for final results. Responses exclude business row images. Gap sequence / next values are strings;never convert them to JavaScript floating-point numbers. Failure handling and FAQ Situation Handling --- --- GAP LIVE DATA DIFFERENCES Fresh scans still differ;no successful receipt is written. Resolve differences and obtain a valid report before review. Resume,moved cut/native checkpoint/schema Refuse;obtain a new comparison and plan rather than editing stored scope. GAP VERIFICATION PLAN CHANGED / GAP VERIFICATION RECORD CHANGED Restore consistent persistent state;missing history is never silently recreated. Agent/network interruption or unknown response Inspect the original receipt. Identical approval replay returns committed history without another scan/write;uncommitted source transactions roll back. Cancellation A request is not proof of rollback. GAP VERIFICATION CANCELLED CHECK RECEIPT requires reading the original receipt;commit may have completed. hasGaps=true , hasOpenGaps=false SKIP history exists with common-cut receipts;this is not live equality. gapCountLimited=true Counts are lower bounds from a bounded window. hasOpenGaps=null means unseen unresolved gaps are unknown;continue paging. Accepted loss Acceptance creates a gap,not equality. Fresh full affected-table comparison must pass before recording verification at a cut. Plans,original SKIP history and receipts remain in source-journal metadata. Native target receipts/business data are unchanged. Source transactions persist plans and atomically commit verification receipts with all selected gap links. First-release schemas are created directly without in-place prerelease-candidate migrations. Progress semantics Field Meaning --- --- captured sequence Captured incremental-log sequence as an exact decimal string covered sequence Minimum safe coverage across targets,including explicit skips subscriptions[].safeCoveredSequence Target acknowledgment coverage subscriptions[].contiguousDeliveredSequence Contiguous non-skipped prefix,stopping before the first historical SKIP subscriptions[].firstSkippedSequence First historical skip or null subscriptions[].progressSemantics SQL COMMITTED,BROKER ACCEPTED or MATERIALIZER ACKNOWLEDGED For SQL,the contiguous prefix represents ordered committed projections. Verification never changes SKIP into APPLIED. Broker receipt is not consumer completion;materializer acknowledgment is not visibility on every replica. New progress values are strings beyond JavaScript integer precision. Snapshot completion remains a separate state.

title: GaussDB index policy
text: Gauss index conversion, correctness, and application takeover Updated: 2026-11-14. 中文：Gauss 索引策略. See requirements and decisions for scope and open questions. Status: v3 implements ordinary secondary indexes and business UNIQUE downgrade; v2 still creates columns/PK only. IndexPolicy produces explicit actions and JdbcSink executes supported indexes on new tables. Expressions/prefixes/descending/special methods and existing UNIQUE/GSI require separate plans, never blind DROP. Business GSI model entries may become ordinary indexes; identity GSIs are not downgraded. Commercial distributed GaussDB still needs hardware acceptance. See the V3 manual. Accepted synchronization policy MySQL is authoritative. Only the synchronization service writes to targets during synchronization; applications may read them. Validate data and restore required constraints before application writes take over. For newly created Gauss business tables: Source object / target requirement Synchronization policy --- --- MySQL PRIMARY KEY Preserve stable row identity and uniqueness; never downgrade to an ordinary index Business secondary UNIQUE(email) or composite UNIQUE Create a nonunique ordinary index with corresponding columns/order; preserve compatible column definitions and NOT NULL Ordinary secondary index Create an ordinary index supported by the target GSI contemplated for secondary uniqueness or query acceleration Use an ordinary secondary index, without global routing/uniqueness guarantees Unique structure required for PK, row identity, or internal correctness Excluded from relaxation; choose compatible distribution/constraints or fail preflight Metadata transaction deduplication, owner/lease, and checkpoint uniqueness Preserve; business-index relaxation does not apply Existing target UNIQUE, GSI, FK dependencies, etc. Inspect dependencies and produce a difference/migration plan; do not automatically DROP or weaken An ordinary index cannot replace a PK. Replacing a global UNIQUE with UNIQUE(email, distribution key) is not equivalent: it allows duplicate email across distribution keys and still enforces a constraint that may be unnecessary during synchronization. This topic covers openGauss/distributed GaussDB. Other adapters may also relax incompatible business secondary UNIQUE constraints under declared policies. Preserve PK/candidate identity and internal correctness; analytical Unique Key/materialization identity is not an optional secondary constraint. See platform design. Review the index plan before starting In the v3 console, run Check connections & objects , then expand Check results and operation details for that operation. The v3 CLI check command returns the same gaussIndexReview section. It reads source index metadata for the MySQL databases mapped to each Gauss target. PostgreSQL and Oracle currently report SOURCE INDEX METADATA UNAVAILABLE because their source discovery does not supply secondary index definitions. Action Expected outcome --- --- CREATE The sink plans an ordinary index with the indicated columns and uniqueness. DOWNGRADE UNIQUE The sink plans a nonunique ordinary index for a business UNIQUE. Restore any required constraint before application writes. REPLACE GSI The sink plans a nonunique ordinary index for a modeled business GSI. Global routing and uniqueness are lost. MySQL discovery does not report native Gauss GSI definitions. REQUIRES PLAN Resolve the reported index requirement before starting. GLOBAL IDENTITY REQUIRES DISTRIBUTION PLAN calls for a distribution plan that preserves row identity. Expressions, prefixes, descending columns and other unsupported definitions have a separate reason. The counts cover all discovered index decisions across Gauss mappings, so the same source object may count once per target. distributionPlanRequired is part of requiresPlan . Ordinary primary keys are created separately and excluded from this review. Details place blockers first and allow up to 24 entries and 8 KiB of compact UTF-8 JSON for each of the blocker and planned groups. omittedEntries counts details outside this limit. Details contain identifiers, actions, reasons and planned index properties. Source expressions, SQL and connection credentials are excluded. A successful connection check can still report REQUIRES PLAN . The live writer recalculates the same policy at startup and stops before business DDL for a blocked index. This check does not execute DDL, inspect existing target indexes or confirm distribution capabilities. Validate openGauss catalog and writer behavior separately. For commercial distributed GaussDB, perform the multi-CN/DN acceptance below on the exact build, compatibility mode, GTM mode and JDBC driver you will deploy. Reproduce the openGauss catalog check The disposable fixture compares the v3 check plan to the physical openGauss indexes, including names, column order and uniqueness. It checks that UNIQUE(email) becomes an ordinary index on the target while MySQL enforces the original constraint. It verifies the composite business primary key, the native receipt keys and recovery from the same target data and journal. Use the sync Worker as the only writer of the selected target tables until the required constraints have been restored. openGauss PG INDEX The native run used MySQL 8.4.13, openGauss 7.0.0-RC3 build f08516a2 in compatibility mode A on ARM64, and Temurin 21 with bundled Gauss JDBC. The target restart and Worker restart retained the original snapshot, receipt and all five index OIDs. The next source transaction advanced the native checkpoint by one. The separate prefix-index case returned REQUIRES PLAN and the writer stopped before creating the mapped schema. The fixture uses local Docker images and records their IDs, the database versions and the bundled JDBC driver. Commercial distributed GaussDB and physical GSI require separate acceptance. What UNIQUE(email) means Example source definition: Logical target example, not current generated output or a universal version-independent script: Omitting target UNIQUE does not itself create duplicates. Final correctness depends on complete replication. At the same fully applied source transaction boundary, each source PK should correspond to the same target row if: 1. Every source transaction is logged and captured completely, with FULL row images, correct ordering, and correct routing. 2. PK mapping is one-to-one; target PK comparisons do not merge distinct source keys. 3. Snapshot/CDC handoff has no gaps, and durable GTID/checkpoints plus idempotent application handle redelivery. 4. Business changes and apply checkpoints commit atomically; retries never skip failed transactions; stale owners are fenced. 5. No external writes, trigger side effects, lossy conversions, or accidental merging of source tables occur. Under these conditions, the source enforces email uniqueness and the target reproduces its rows. The target ordinary index no longer enforces email uniqueness. Retry idempotency relies on PKs and transaction checkpoints, not the email index. Removing UNIQUE is not a recovery mechanism. Preserve multiple NULLs allowed by the source; GROUP BY email HAVING COUNT( ) 1 alone is not a valid constraint check. Case, collation, trailing spaces, empty-string/NULL behavior, and type conversion can change equality semantics. Source uniqueness does not guarantee that a future target UNIQUE constraint will build successfully. Temporary duplicates during snapshot The current snapshot uses online chunks followed by log replay, not one database-wide point-in-time snapshot. For example, the scanner reads id=1,email=a ; a source transaction changes it to b and inserts id=2,email=a ; the scanner then reads id=2. Before catch-up, the target may contain two distinct PKs with email=a even though every committed source state was valid. Temporary secondary-key duplicates are not duplicate PK rows and must not cause data to be discarded. Complete ordered replay must restore the source state at the declared boundary. Snapshot/early catch-up output is not promised to be consistent; consumers requiring consistency wait for an agreed barrier and read protocol. Ordinary secondary indexes permit these intermediate states, which fits the current scan method. Preserving selected target UNIQUE constraints in a future design would require revisiting snapshot/replay semantics and constraint timing, not merely adding UNIQUE to generated DDL. Can GSI become an ordinary index? Yes, an ordinary index can be selected during new-table index planning to retain a basic access path on corresponding columns. This is a replacement with changed capabilities, not a lossless native conversion. MySQL has no Gauss GSI; keyword substitution in source DDL cannot implement it. Huawei documents GSI distribution independent of the base table. Its example contrasts an ordinary index visiting all DNs with GSI routing a qualifying lookup to one DN.
