Durable work and cancellation Admission persists the explicit scope,report and predetermined plan UUID before queuing. Restart reuses that identity. A saved plan with an unfinished controller operation is loaded and checked against its original creator,time and scope. A bounded maintenance queue is separate from normal controls;each task has at most one pending operation. Cancellation persists first,then interrupts the worker. Checkpoint/dependency waits and target scans/DML observe interruption. The current uncommitted table rolls back;previous commits remain. A cancellation can race a successful commit,so a cancelled result does not prove that nothing changed. Review/retry the same plan to resolve native receipts. Completion records per-table counts,original checkpoints and whether a prior attempt committed. Controller audit links authenticated actor,request and plan hashes. Raw business values never enter operations/audit. CLI actor assertions retain their separate host-trust model. The controller data directory contains operations,plans and sealed row reports;an external journal does not replace it. Persist/back up this directory for Linux,Docker and K8s. Local disk loss,multiple controllers on a shared PVC and live K8s node faults require separate acceptance. Never bypass identity/hash checks while restoring older files or metadata. Dependency refusal Plan creation and each table mutation check dependencies. Initial execution rejects incoming/outgoing foreign keys and triggers. PostgreSQL also rejects row security,partitions/inheritance and extra rewrite rules,and takes a table lock during these checks. Nothing is automatically disabled or dropped. MySQL trigger metadata requires TRIGGER privilege;an empty result with insufficient privilege cannot establish absence. See the official MySQL8.4 documentation. Initial visibility checks conservatively require direct global SELECT and TRIGGER grants and reject observed partial revokes. Role-only/schema/table-level combinations are not resolved yet and may return REPAIR METADATA VISIBILITY REQUIRED. Use an organization-reviewed migration account/profile rather than bypassing inspection. The synchronizer must remain the exclusive business writer. Arbitrary concurrent DDL/external writes are outside this contract. Changed roots produce REPAIR TARGET DRIFTED and require a new validation/plan. These checks do not establish arbitrary vendor/procedure/dependency coverage. API Use existing authentication,X-Request-ID and current expectedRevision with POST /api/tasks/TASK ID/actions: The202response already persists operations[].repair.planId. Wait for REPAIR PLAN READY,then GET /api/tasks/TASK ID/validations/REPORT UUID/repairs/PLAN UUID. This review projection contains counts/budgets,no raw rows or guarantee of current eligibility. Execution requires controller desired PAUSED. Cancel with REPAIR CANCEL and no repair payload. Idempotent replay uses the original request ID,body,revision and identity. A new request with a stale revision is rejected before creating another job. FAQ and boundaries A reviewed plan can become ineligible:execution rechecks current data,schema,configuration and pause cut. Wrong hashes are refused by the executor;stale revisions are refused at admission. Retry the same plan to resolve commits after cancellation. A complete real-time progress catalog,independent receipt browsing,report/scratch retention and cleanup remain pending. This mode requires a common cut. For a failed transaction, see compensation or reviewed skip. Nonempty adoption, constraint restoration and cutover remain open. Plans display default CLI repair budgets;UI budget editing is not implemented. Full vendor/version/cluster/capacity/security/controller-HA matrices remain incomplete. COMMON CUT foundations · Managed validation Development note:the existing general shape guard initially rejected triggers before the repair-specific check,producing a generic console failure. The guard remains intact;repair dependency checks now run first to return the explicit refusal. The corrected specified profiles pass;the failure and correction remain in the evidence.

title: Managed validation
text: Managed data validation Use the validation workflow to select SQL destinations, set time and storage budgets, run or cancel background checks, retry destination comparisons against a sealed source, and review per-table results. To correct differences reported at a common cut, use managed repair. To review a stalled MySQL source transaction, see capture recovery. Use the console 1. Complete V3 snapshots, run the local Worker and verify shared RUNNING state. Selected destinations must be able to reach the common cut; unselected destinations can be paused/offline. 2. As ADMIN, select transactional SQL destinations under Data validation. Messaging/analytical destinations are excluded. First native row profiles cover MySQL/PostgreSQL; other SQL product versions/modes require separate acceptance. 3. Set source-gate, source-read and per-target-table deadlines plus logical/per-row budgets. Gate maximum is120seconds, reads24hours, rows32MiB. Total logical budget must be at least four times the row budget and includes source, destination and keyless identity records. Physical storage is additional. 4. Start comparison. After checking the current configuration revision, scope, report ID and budgets are persisted before execution in a separate background queue. Establishing the cut briefly blocks MySQL instance writes; business writes can continue after gate release while replication retains its durable pause. 5. Follow operation history, then open the report. Results show source/target counts and missing/extra/changed rows per table,50table results per page. A historical result does not establish current equality. 6. Inspect results/shared state and explicitly resume using the current error version. Validation never clears/repairs business tables, rebuilds UNIQUE or transfers write ownership. Cancel and recover Cancel is a durable request, not resume. Owned read connections/locks are aborted and complete sealed source data is retained. The response does not guarantee release at an exact millisecond:driver/connect/network timeouts also matter. Observe task state and database sessions. Cancellation before establishing a barrier can leave shared RUNNING state; the controller stops its local Worker and displays actual shared state. Once a barrier is established, cancellation never bypasses PAUSED. A sealed source allows Retry target comparison after loading the report. Original configuration/positions/epoch/physical target checkpoints and source integrity are checked; partial destination scans are discarded and reread, even with the source offline. The report's staging budget is retained; retries default to ten minutes per target table. Existing-report quota expansion and richer retry planning remain pending. An incomplete source MVCC view cannot survive process loss. Keep the failed report, inspect/explicitly resume as appropriate, and establish a new cut. Never mix source views or rewrite report hashes/GTIDs. Controller restart can reuse a report ID when complete source data survived but the operation completion did not; without a complete source view/local Worker, it fails explicitly rather than resuming the shared pipeline. One validation runs at a time; ordinary controls use a separate pool. Access, audit and storage ADMIN starts/cancels/retries; OPERATOR/VIEWER read summaries only for granted tasks. Cross-task access is hidden. Mutations require current revision and request ID; replay does not create another job. Previously accepted asynchronous work can continue after authorization changes; subsequent requests use current grants. Audit records actor, task, report ID, request hash and acceptance/completion/cancellation/read events. Corresponding audit writes are required before the HTTP response. Raw business values are excluded from summaries/history. Reports live under platform.dataDirectory/validations/ taskId / reportId . The H2 files contain unencrypted row values. Put them on a protected persistent volume and include them in coordinated backups. The console keeps approximately 40 recent operations per task. Reports can still be opened by ID or browsed in the historical directory. A restarted Agent must have access to the original report directory. API POST /api/tasks/ taskId /actions with X-Request-ID and current expectedRevision : Retry uses VALIDATE RETRY and validation: "reportId":" UUID ","targetMillis":600000 . Cancel uses VALIDATE CANCEL without validation input. GET /api/tasks/ taskId /validations/ reportId reads a summary. VALIDATION REPORT NOT CREATED means inspect the operation failure; VALIDATION REPORT BUSY means retry after the active scan. Core contract and FAQ / 中文 Job recovery paths First native managed acceptance passed LOCAL/H2 and external PostgreSQL/MySQL/openGauss journals with MySQL8.4/PostgreSQL17 destinations, including cancellation during an actual relation-lock wait, sealed-source retry and report/audit persistence across controller restart. See evidence and failure corrections. Administrator difference details For a completed report, ADMIN can open differences per target/table, page by identity hash, then explicitly reveal raw values. Stored source column names/types accompany expected/actual cells. An absent row is distinct from a present SQL NULL cell. Keyless source/target occurrence IDs are displayed without generating replacements. POST /api/tasks/ taskId /validations/ reportId /differences with "target":"postgres","tableId":" table ID ","after":"","limit":25 returns items/next; maximum limit is100. POST .../values with the target/table and identityHash returns columns and expected/actual cells. Null for an entire side means absent row; cell value:null means SQL NULL. OPERATOR/VIEWER remain limited to summaries. Before releasing values, the server checks difference hashes, raw-row checksums and row identity and requires report/scope-linked audit. Business values never enter audit/controller operations. The API checks total UTF-8 raw JSON lengths before fetching CLOBs and refuses more than1MiB with VALIDATION DETAIL TOO LARGE; it never truncates or substitutes an empty row. Large-row chunking/streaming export remains pending; complete private report data is retained. Values remain in page memory and are cleared on logout. These are historical cut values, not live queries or repair. Repair is separate from read-only validation. The new managed repair workflow requires plan review and explicit confirmation;validation itself never changes destination data. Historical report directory In Data validation , choose Browse historical reports to open reports retained in the task owner's data directory, newest first. Open a report to read its summary. It remains readable after the original operation leaves recent history and after the Agent reopens its original directory. Detailed differences and row values require administrator permissions for the task. Report cards show the creation time. Expand Report ID to copy the identifier. When you already have an identifier, select Open by report ID from the directory. This opens one report for the current task using the same summary grants. Back to report directory restores the page you were browsing. While you navigate with the keyboard, background status updates keep focus on the same available report control. Clients can page metadata using GET /api/tasks/ id /validations?limit=20 and pass nextCursor as after . The task owner removes abandoned summary staging files when it next acquires the report lock. Include retained reports and review evidence in the task's protected backup policy. The catalog lists report metadata without opening the H2 database or reading row values. Opening a report that is currently in use returns VALIDATION REPORT BUSY . Wait for the operation to finish and open it again. Use Previous and Next to page through identities for the selected destination and table. An administrator can explicitly reveal raw values for a selected difference. There is no automatic expiration of report or recovery evidence. Budget for the retained files in addition to the current job's quota. Keep a report while a retry, repair plan, gap verification, or audit relies on it. Removal from recent operation history does not release any report storage. Check report storage An administrator can select View storage on a report card, or use GET /api/tasks/ taskId /validations/ reportId /storage . The response contains observed byte lengths for the report database and the known summary and diagnostic files. Protected means the owning Agent observed the report in use in its process. Activity unknown covers other processes. Use the observations for storage and backup planning. File lengths can change during an active operation. Review a report's minimum retention Set validationRetentionMinimumDays on the Agent that owns the report, or on the standalone server. The default 0 disables new reviews. Values from 1 to 3650 enable the workflow and set its minimum duration. Apply the setting to the platform configuration for Linux, Docker or native Kubernetes. With Helm, set platform.validationRetentionMinimumDays for the Agent release. In View storage , enter the minimum number of days to retain the completed report and confirm the review. The server checks the current task revision, the last review ID and the original report lock. Reviews can extend the existing minimum date. Active or incomplete reports return an explicit refusal. Once accepted, watch the request in the task's operation history and reopen View storage to see the committed date and reviewer. The equivalent request is POST /api/tasks/ taskId /validations/ reportId /retention with the usual request ID and session protection. Pass expectedRevision , minimumDays , and approved: true . Include expectedReviewId from the previous review when one exists. A retry with the same request ID and body keeps the original result. The Agent stores the review alongside the report and links its outcome to the report ID and actor in the audit trail. Back up the attachment with the original report. Reaching the minimum date keeps the files in place until an eligible reclamation is approved. Recover a report from a sealed copy Set validationArchiveDirectory on the report's owning Agent or standalone server to a private persistent directory. Keep that directory outside the validation report tree and restrict access to the server account. For Linux, Docker and native Kubernetes, configure and mount the directory in the server's platform configuration. Helm exposes platform.validationArchiveDirectory ; provision the mount independently. Use separate storage if the copy must survive loss of the live report volume. For a completed report with a submitted retention review, select View storage and confirm Create recovery copy . The Agent holds the original report lock, copies the report database and summary, and verifies byte lengths and SHA-256 before sealing the descriptor. One copy may be sealed per report. The database limit is 128 MiB and the summary limit is 1 MiB. This copy contains the same sensitive data as the report. Preserve the original report directory, its archive descriptor, the Agent owner identity, retention and repair records in coordinated backups. If the live report database is missing, the report remains in the directory and live reads return VALIDATION REPORT ARCHIVE RESTORE REQUIRED . Select View storage and confirm Restore report . The Agent verifies the copy and scope again, preserves every existing file with differing content, and restores missing files under the original lock. An interrupted restore blocks live readers and handoff custody until recovery completes. During normal operation the archive and original files both occupy storage. For API clients, POST /api/tasks/ taskId /validations/ reportId /archive accepts operation: "COPY" and expectedReviewId , or operation: "RESTORE" and expectedArchiveId . Both require the current expectedRevision , confirmation with approved: true , and an authenticated request ID. Reclaim a verified duplicate of the live report database Set validationArchiveReclaim: true on the report's Agent or standalone server to enable reviewed reclamation. Helm exposes platform.validationArchiveReclaim . Stop the task, wait until its Worker has exited, open View storage , and review the recovery copy SHA-256 before approving Reclaim live report storage . The API uses the same archive endpoint with operation: "RECLAIM" , expectedArchiveId , expectedArchiveSha256 and expectedReviewId , along with the current revision, request ID and confirmation. The Agent requires an elapsed retention hold, an exact private archive, and a completed differences report with at least one mismatched table at every compared destination. This preserves reports eligible for gap checks or UNIQUE restoration. The presence of repair or recovery plans or scratch space also prevents reclamation. If any check fails, preserve the report and review the displayed outcome. The Agent audits the exact approval and commits a durable reader fence before reclaiming the duplicate rows.mv.db . Report summaries, repair plans, operation receipts, archive files and business databases stay in place. The report remains searchable. Restore the report from the copy before using its row-level evidence. Keep both the owner identity and the original report directory. An interrupted request retains its fence and can resume under the original command. A later explicit restore can also reconcile an interrupted reclamation. Find a recovery operation receipt In global task control, an administrator can choose Find receipt by request ID in the task details. A current recovery operation also has a View receipt shortcut. The exact lookup GET /api/tasks/ taskId /recovery-receipts/ requestId reads the persisted control-plane result after the request has left recent history, including while its Agent is unavailable. The response includes the recorded operation state, actor, owner, time and available report or plan identifiers. For example, a correction receipt can show its associated failure evidence ID. A report ID assigned only on the Agent may be available through the historical report directory. Destination commit and gap evidence remains in its native ledger. The receipt lookup uses both task and node grants and returns the same absence response for unrelated request IDs.

title: Manual target corrections
text: Manual target corrections 中文 Administrators can add missing rows, correct values and delete extra rows after a destination SQL failure. The first profile covers transactional PostgreSQL and MySQL destinations and uses the existing recovery permissions and pause fence. 1. Pause the whole task and confirm the destination fence. Retain fresh failure evidence. If the original destination commit is ahead of the journal acknowledgment, reconcile it first. 2. Choose “Correct target rows” in the evidence dialog. Select an affected table and action, fill the fields and add the edit to the batch. To import, choose a JSON file or paste the original JSON. 3. Preview the corrections. Review the destination, tables, identities, before and after values and row count. Generate a fresh preview after changing the batch. 4. Enter an approval reason and confirm. Check the operation status and the destination before explicitly resuming the original transaction. Action Input --- --- Insert A keyed table and complete values, including nullable columns and materialized generated columns Update All key fields or an existing ROW ID, plus the fields to change Delete All key fields or an existing ROW ID Each batch supports up to 50 rows and 128 KiB of input. Preview values are limited to 512 KiB. An identity can occur once per batch. JSON string values preserve precision, JSON null represents SQL NULL and JSON columns accept JSON text in a string. Send expectedRevision , subscriptionId , the subscriber's errorCount , correction.evidenceId and correction.evidenceHash to POST /api/tasks/ task /corrections/schema or /corrections/preview . Preview also accepts either correction.batch or original correction.importJson . Submit that same content to the task's /actions endpoint with action: CORRECTION EXECUTE , the preview hash as approvedHash , an approval reason and an X-Request-ID . Retry a lost response with the same request ID and original body. Situation Action --- --- The checkpoint, task revision or target row changed Retain current evidence and preview again A keyless table contains identical values Use the exact ROW ID from normalized evidence A row write or receipt fails Inspect the error and constraints before generating a new preview. The target transaction rolls back the entire batch The table has unsupported foreign keys, triggers or structure Resolve the dependency or use a repair procedure for that table A decimal or integer exceeds browser precision Enter the value as a string before any floating point conversion The administrator preview returns row values. Task summaries and durable receipts expose table scope, counts and the digest. The destination transaction preserves the source log, GTID and acknowledgment position. While a correction write is pending, use any management entry to cancel the original request and check the commit outcome.

title: Messaging targets
text: Messaging targets: configuration, consumption and recovery 中文：消息目标. Example: messaging-v3.yml. Source/journal operations: V3 manual. Implemented scope Each supported V3 message destination has its own delivery thread, publication and snapshot checkpoint, and error generation. The current profiles cover Kafka, Pulsar, RabbitMQ, RocketMQ, ActiveMQ Classic, Artemis, Redis Streams and NATS JetStream. They can run alongside SQL destinations. A stalled destination leaves other delivery threads running. All subscriptions govern journal retention. The contract is confirmed at-least-once publication . The broker and journal database do not share a transaction. Lost confirmations, or a crash between confirmation and receipt persistence, can cause duplicates. Retries retain event IDs and content; consumers must deduplicate durably. A publisher checkpoint means broker confirmation, not completion of downstream business processing or readiness for cutover. Configuration and UI Choose a message product in the V3 wizard, map each source database to a message namespace and add other SQL/message destinations. The UI provides topic/stream, Kafka security/SASL mechanism, Pulsar admin/cluster, RocketMQ prefix/cluster/broker/retention, token, replica count and size limit, masks credentials, and saves a stopped configuration. Import YAML for multiple endpoints or advanced deployment settings. Namespaces start with a letter and contain only letters, digits and underscores, up to 63 characters. url and messaging.endpoints reject embedded credentials and query parameters. Use separate username/password fields or messaging.token for NATS. Passwords/tokens support $ ENV NAME references and are excluded from events/status. Check opens connections and reads capabilities; it creates no business queues, streams or replication connection. Artemis uses a temporary non-durable management reply channel. Destination cards expose only product, mapping, consistency and consumer topic/stream names; connection URLs and credentials are excluded. A broker confirmation and the downstream consumer's business checkpoint are distinct. Setting Meaning --- --- autoCreate Create resources before first publication. False requires pre-provisioning. Previously initialized missing resources are never recreated automatically replicas JetStream/Kafka replicas, Redis total copies (primary included), or the initial quorum queue member count; does not provision broker nodes maxMessageBytes Complete UTF-8 JSON envelope limit, default 1 MiB; broker limits also apply connectTimeoutMillis / requestTimeoutMillis Connection and confirmation/management timeout, 100–120000 ms endpoints Additional entrances to the same broker cluster, never independent replacement clusters Kafka topic Dedicated topic for this subscription; all mapped databases/tables share it Kafka securityProtocol / saslMechanism PLAINTEXT, SSL, SASL PLAINTEXT, SASL SSL; SASL supports PLAIN and SCRAM-SHA-256/512 For Rabbit's default / vhost use amqp://host:5672 or amqp://host:5672/%2f . amqp://host:5672/ selects an empty vhost name under the AMQP URI specification. Additional nodes must use the same scheme/vhost. amqps:// and NATS tls:// use JVM trust configuration. Username/password or token authentication is implemented; NKey/JWT files, certificate wizard and a complete TLS acceptance matrix remain pending. Resources and confirmation Each namespace uses namespace. schema , namespace. transactions and namespace.table . Names containing routing syntax, excessive length, or a / rm prefix use rm followed by SHA-256(table ID) for the table channel. The envelope/schema retain the original database/table names. Control channels are reserved. Kafka writes all logical channels into messaging.topic , retaining the channel in the rivomesh channel header. A dedicated single-partition topic is required, with acks=all, enable.idempotence=true and max.in.flight=1. This is not a native transactional Kafka producer; the same at-least-once contract applies. Replicas match configuration, min.insync.replicas is replicas/2+1 , unclean election is disabled, retention.ms/bytes are -1 and cleanup.policy is delete. Plan consumer archival/retention; compaction must not silently evict history. Partition growth or policy changes require a plan. One partition has hardware throughput limits. Every broker must disable auto.create.topics.enable ; explicit first-time Admin creation remains available. Otherwise producer metadata refresh could recreate a deleted empty topic and conceal lost history. Preparation checks every broker and requires the relevant DescribeConfigs permission. Topics need Describe/DescribeConfigs/Write and initially Create. Existing replica/ISR/size/retention mismatches block rather than being overwritten. The stable Kafka clusterId is bound in the journal; reconnecting to another cluster raises BROKER IDENTITY CHANGED . For replication factor 3, check the data partition's ISR separately from the KRaft controller quorum. The Rivomesh topic requires a minimum ISR of 2 and acks=all . Two of three controllers can still commit metadata while a particular topic has only one in-sync data replica. Use kafka-topics.sh --bootstrap-server broker :9092 --describe --topic topic to see the partition Leader and ISR, and kafka-metadata-quorum.sh --bootstrap-server broker :9092 describe --status for KRaft metadata. If the publication receipt is stalled with KAFKA RETRY and too few replicas are in sync, restore original broker storage and wait for the partition ISR to recover. The staged source transaction keeps its original event IDs when retried. Kafka KRaft guide · Kafka 3.9.2 minimum ISR contract Stage event bytes and identifiers durably before committing a consumer group offset. Kafka commits the offset of the next record to read. Keep that offset separately from Rivomesh's publication receipt and use the event ID for replay deduplication. Kafka consumer offset API The Kafka native fixture uses Apache Kafka 3.9.2, a one-partition RF3 topic, three KRaft voters and a broker-only node to isolate data ISR loss. It injects deterministic source transactions into the durable JDBC journal and uses the packaged Kafka transport and native consumer group commits. The fixture covers process failure with retained disk volumes. Live source CDC, TLS, controller-quorum loss, disk loss and workload capacity have separate acceptance scopes. In the five-check Temurin 21 run, the partition elected a new leader after SIGKILL. With one replica in sync, Kafka still committed a metadata change while the publication receipt stayed at sequence 2. After the broker restarted, the publisher delivered the same retained transaction at sequence 3. The consumer reopened its offset at 7, staged six pending records, and committed 13. A fresh consumer then found no pending records and all 13 original event bodies remained readable. Review the preceding Kafka receipts When Kafka is paused on a complete incremental apply failure, pause the entire pipeline and use the target error generation. PRECEDING KAFKA RECEIPTS VERIFIED reports the native offset and bytes digest of each mapped namespace's preceding COMMIT for the acknowledged sequence. The command reads at most the last 512 partition offsets with a group-less, read-committed consumer. It checks the bound cluster and the observed topic identity, rejects a moving partition view and rechecks the journal after the broker read. Missing evidence or a later visible BEGIN / COMMIT fails admission. The observed topic UUID describes this read. The journal's existing transport binding records the cluster only. The result is recovery evidence for the preceding acknowledged transaction. A journal pause leaves any outstanding Kafka producer unconfirmed. A durable Kafka gap notice would require a separate, reviewed operation and broker fencing. This command leaves the original event, broker records, consumer offsets and journal acknowledgment in place. The focused native profile is tests/kafka-cluster-run.py --only-recovery-review . In shared management, enable cluster.recoveryReview on Controllers and Agents running the same release. An administrator with access to the task and its assigned Agent can select Review Kafka receipts on a paused Kafka destination after pausing the entire task. The task history shows when the request completes. View receipt opens the verified offsets and digests. Find receipt by request ID works after the request leaves recent history or the Agent goes offline. API clients send POST /api/tasks/ task /actions with a stable X-Request-ID and a body such as "action":"REVIEW KAFKA RECEIPTS","expectedRevision":" current task revision ","subscriptionId":"kafka","errorCount":1 . HTTP 202 records admission for owner dispatch. Poll GET /api/tasks/ task /recovery-receipts/ request for the outcome. A successful receipt contains kafkaReview , including the observed epoch, error generation, sequence numbers and digests. KAFKA RECOVERY PUBLICATION UNCERTAIN leaves the receipt without verified offsets. Use a new request ID and current revision for a fresh observation. A receipt describes its observation time and gives no approval to skip or replay the failed transaction. Use tests/kafka-cluster-run.py --only-managed-recovery-review to exercise the packaged HTTP management flow against four KRaft brokers. The isolated fixture uses two loopback management entries with a shared H2 control store and checks replay through the second entry, lookup with the owner offline, partial-publication rejection and unchanged target progress. Review a Kafka notice plan An administrator can preview a failure notice for a pre-owned Kafka control topic. Set the optional recoveryNotice fields under the Kafka destination’s messaging configuration, and apply the configuration before reviewing the predecessor receipt. The control topic must differ from every configured Kafka business topic in the task. Management also checks logical destination conflicts across known bootstrap addresses. The planner verifies that the dedicated topic already exists in the original Kafka cluster, with one partition, at least three replicas, a majority minimum ISR, indefinite retention and automatic creation disabled. Publication stays blocked with KAFKA NOTICE GLOBAL OWNERSHIP UNVERIFIED because logical endpoint claims cannot establish physical separation across every external or aliased destination. Set cleanup.policy=delete , retention.ms=-1 , retention.bytes=-1 , unclean.leader.election.enable=false and remote.storage.enable=false on the control topic. Use a max.message.bytes value from 2048 through 65536 and set min.insync.replicas to a majority of configured replicas. Set auto.create.topics.enable=false on all Brokers. The planner needs business-topic read access and access to Kafka topic and Broker configuration metadata. Pause the entire task, run a new successful Kafka receipt review, and select Review Kafka notice plan inside its receipt. API clients can send POST /api/tasks/ task /kafka-notice-plan with "expectedRevision":" current task revision ","predecessorRequestId":" successful review request ID " . The owner rechecks the authenticated predecessor, task revision, administrator, original failure and Topic UUID. The response contains a deterministic plan digest and notice payload digest and always returns executionAuthorized: false . Generate a fresh receipt after a configuration or owner change, or when the original receipt predates the failure-content binding. Use tests/kafka-cluster-run.py --only-managed-notice-plan to exercise the read-only plan through two management entries and a real Kafka cluster. Capture physical ownership for new business publications Set kafkaPhysicalOwnershipEvidence: true in the managed owner Agent's startup configuration to observe new Kafka publications. The Agent checks the exact active shared configuration and the projected Worker file at launch. The Worker receives a signing key scoped to that configuration and owner directory. The first eligible COMMIT per configuration and journal generation records the physical Kafka Topic UUID, the confirmed offset and the exact payload digest. The publication checkpoint stages the proof. The successful subscription ACK and final proof commit in the same journal transaction. On Linux and Docker, set the option at the root of the executing member's platform YAML and restart that member. For manual Kubernetes, edit the Agent ConfigMap's platform.yml , apply the manifest and roll out the Agent. With Helm, set platform.kafkaPhysicalOwnershipEvidence=true on the Agent release or on a combined shared-task release that runs Workers. An enabled Worker checks the receipt tables and its SQL permissions before publication. With schema creation rights, it can provision missing receipt tables. If that check reports KAFKA PHYSICAL JOURNAL NOT READY , check the journal schema and the Worker's SELECT, INSERT and DELETE privileges on the pending receipt table and its SELECT and INSERT privileges on the history tables. MySQL receipt tables use InnoDB with utf8mb4 bin collation. PostgreSQL-protocol receipt tables use permanent ordinary tables. Leave the option disabled to keep using an ordinary journal without the receipt tables. The shared control authority signs the issuing Agent's node, incarnation, lease epoch and lease time window. This proves the lease observed when the grant was issued. The journal stamps and signs the publication checkpoint and subscription ACK in UTC milliseconds. It compares only those two journal times, so clock differences between the control store, journal and Kafka cannot establish event order. If the journal clock goes backward between the writes, the business ACK still commits and that COMMIT remains unverified. A restart in the same configuration can preserve the original Agent witness on a pending receipt. Older physical receipts stay unchanged and lack the new member and time evidence. A newly observed COMMIT can supply the new evidence for the same configuration. The Kafka business identity needs READ access to re-read the confirmed offsets. A WRITE-only identity continues to publish and ACK while its physical ownership remains unverified. The profile can read back up to 16 namespaces and retries an unavailable observation at most once every 30 seconds per Worker. The proof begins at its recorded ACK. Older writes and configurations remain unverified. No earlier evidence is backfilled and notice publication stays blocked. Administrators can read exact retained evidence through either managed entry. With the task still paused, open a successful Kafka receipt review and choose Check physical receipt . API clients send POST /api/tasks/ task /kafka-physical-receipt with "expectedRevision":" current task revision ","predecessorRequestId":" successful Kafka receipt review " . The owner checks the current failure and verifies the saved signatures, exact preceding ACK and Kafka Topic identity. VERIFIED returns the receipt digest and its journal timestamps. MISSING includes older receipts that do not cover that exact ACK, unverified signatures and changed physical Topic identities. UNREACHABLE means an owner, journal or broker read could not complete. Refresh the predecessor review if the task or failure changes. This read provides no authorization to publish. Native Kafka 3.9.2 testing uses TLS/SCRAM-SHA-512 and two Controller entries routed to the same Agent. A new Kafka Topic with the same name returns missing evidence. With Temurin 21, run python3 tests/kafka-notice-writer-run.py --managed-physical-receipt application-jar to exercise the retained receipt. Native evidence The preview reports catalogCoverage for the managed task catalog. VERIFIED SINGLETON covers one task, one configuration and one Kafka destination. For a bounded catalog with up to four tasks, eight total retained configuration versions and twelve Kafka routes, VERIFIED AT REVIEW checks the current physical Kafka cluster and Topic UUID of each business route. The check includes stopped tasks and retained versions offered by configuration history. The current owner reads broker metadata using each configuration on file. A physical match with the control topic returns CONFLICT , including when the task uses a different bootstrap alias. When the catalog exceeds these limits, a broker or owner is unreachable, or a retained configuration can no longer be resolved, coverage is INCOMPLETE . A concurrent catalog or configuration update requires a new review. Each owner applies its current Worker secret-reference grants and protected environment rules before reading Kafka metadata. A revoked historical reference blocks that route's probe. Coverage describes where the retained configurations can connect today. Historical physical custody, wider Kafka authorization and approval evidence remain required for publication. All previews keep publication blocked. An owner Agent can additionally inspect a dedicated writer with kafkaNoticeWriters in its private startup configuration. Each entry contains taskId , targetId , clusterSha256 , topicId , bootstrapServers , username and password . Use Agent-only secret references for credentials and a trusted list of Kafka host:port bootstrap addresses. The writer connects to these addresses even when the task uses different aliases. The two roles must use distinct passwords and usernames. Both sessions use hostname-verified SASL SSL with the Kafka target's SCRAM mechanism and the Agent JVM's trusted CA. The preview reports writerEntitlement with the broker's observed effective permissions. The business identity needs metadata access to both topics and read-only access to the control topic. The dedicated identity needs WRITE and its implied DESCRIBE on the control topic and at least DESCRIBE on the selected business topic, with no permissions to mutate it. The check requires the broker's effective operation list for both roles. Installations can exercise the contract with python3 tests/kafka-notice-writer-run.py application-jar . A verified observation covers the reviewed roles and topics at that time. Publication remains blocked pending complete managed coverage, broader broker policy and approved transactional dispatch. Enroll a new task for first-send evidence For a new task with a Kafka target and a LOCAL journal, set kafkaHistoryFromFirstSend: true at the task YAML root before creating it through a shared management entry. Enable kafkaPhysicalOwnershipEvidence on the owning Agent before starting the task. Standalone runs, external journals and changes to the enrollment setting on existing tasks are refused. Task creation signs the initial configuration and assigned journal generation in the control store. Before the first Worker starts, the Agent commits the same origin and empty first-attempt records with the local journal job and subscriptions. It rechecks the live Agent lease and active configuration before marking the origin ready. Restart verifies the existing journal and generation. Keep the owner data directory and control-store backups together. If a ready journal is missing or its origin does not verify, stop and investigate its original storage. A replacement journal cannot be enrolled by restarting the task. For each Kafka target, the journal commits a signed digest before the first business publish attempt. The digest binds the active configuration projection, journal generation, subscription, lease epoch and exact first wire batch. It contains no raw message data or credentials. Each schema, snapshot or incremental send runs the origin check. A failed or ambiguous first publish leaves the first attempt at UNKNOWN , including after ordinary business replay and ACK. Keeping one first attempt per Kafka subscription bounds storage. Later sends and broker-internal retries have no entries in this profile. When no physical Topic is configured, Produce uses the Topic name. First-intent evidence alone leaves historical ownership unresolved. Keep independent control-store and local journal backups coordinated. Bind new Kafka business routes to physical Topics For the approval-and-dispatch profile, create each business Topic before creating the task. Set the following fields on every Kafka target, along with the normal endpoints, credentials, mappings and the Topic policy above. Enter the UUID from Kafka's topic description and the cluster ID from Kafka's cluster administration API. The managed task signs these routes with the initial configuration and journal generation. The Worker sends schema, snapshots and incremental records to each assigned UUID with Produce v13. It saves the latest confirmed COMMIT offset and digest per target and configuration. The owner Agent verifies the exact native record when an administrator reviews a failure. A UUID change needs a newly enrolled task and a reviewed migration. Retained configurations that previously sent by name still block full-history approval. Kafka 4.1 protocol Use Kafka 4.1 or later with transaction version 2 finalized for the dispatch profile. The packaged notice transport uses an isolated Kafka 4.1.2 SDK. Ordinary name-addressed synchronization uses the separate Kafka 3.9.2 SDK. Kafka's CLI or Admin API must report the original physical identifiers after failover. Same-name Topic recreation creates a different identity and requires a recovery decision. Configure the writer on the owning Agent. Grant the business identity the cluster DESCRIBE operation to inspect ACLs affecting the reserved control Topic. Give the notice identity one literal WRITE grant on that Topic and transaction access to Rivomesh's rivomesh-kafka-notice- identifiers for its assigned notices. Keep Kafka administrators and their maintenance access under the broker's operational controls. Exclude external business writers from the dedicated control Topic. The native check verifies matching literal, wildcard and prefix ACLs before enabling dispatch. Kafka authorization Approve, check and send a gap notice Pause the task and open the successful Kafka receipt review. Preview the affected subscription and use Record approval when the managed catalog verifies the complete configured routes. The older profile offers Record conditional approval . Approval records bind the exact failure, actor, configuration version, control Topic UUID, route digest and notice payload. Re-review a changed configuration, writer entitlement or physical Topic. API clients send POST /api/tasks/ task /kafka-notice-approvals with X-Request-ID , expectedRevision , predecessorRequestId and approvalScopeSha256 . A successful response is RECORDED for an eligible approval or RECORDED BLOCKED when proof is missing. Both record types return executionAuthorized: false . The original approver uses Check sender prerequisites . The equivalent route is POST /api/tasks/ task /kafka-notice-approvals/ request-id /preflight with expectedRevision and approvalScopeSha256 . The service checks the original approval and audit record, revalidates the routes and writer, and reads the exact preceding ACK. SENDER READY enables Send gap notice . A blocked check shows the missing evidence or broker requirements. The send action posts to /api/tasks/ task /kafka-notice-approvals/ request-id /dispatch with the same two fields and a new stable X-Request-ID . Either entry can retrieve the delivery operation with GET /api/tasks/ task /recovery-receipts/ dispatch-request-id . An uncertain outcome stays visible until the owner verifies the native Kafka receipt. Reuse the same request ID after a lost HTTP reply. A successful notice records the physical Topic, native offset and payload digest. The failed source transaction, subscription ACKs, business Topics and consumer offsets remain at their original positions during notification. If the owner is interrupted before Kafka commits, the ledger retains the exact native offset and waits. Only Kafka's terminal abort and exact retained bytes permit another attempt. On a lost commit response, the owner reads the original committed notice and preserves its receipt. A missing or changed control Topic leaves the operation unresolved. Rabbit uses durable, nonexclusive, non-auto-delete queues, direct routing through the default exchange, persistent messages, publisher confirms and mandatory/return. Returns/nacks never advance the receipt. Quorum is the default; classic is selectable. Created queues use reject-publish overflow. Broker policies must not silently discard old/expired messages or dead-letter redeliveries without a recovery consumer. Production quorum requires multiple nodes and appropriate replicas. Single-node tests do not establish majority-loss or power-loss guarantees. For three-node RabbitMQ, set messaging.queueType: quorum and messaging.replicas: 3 before the first queue declaration. Use one broker as url and the other two as messaging.endpoints , all from the same cluster and virtual host with the same TLS mode. The replica setting is the initial declaration size. Verify actual members , online and leader with rabbitmqctl list queues -p / name type durable leader members online . Publisher confirms from a quorum queue depend on the available majority. RabbitMQ quorum queues · Publisher confirms If a leader fails and a majority remains, Rivomesh reconnects through a surviving endpoint while RabbitMQ elects the new leader. If the majority is unavailable, retain the RabbitMQ volumes and policies. Start one of the original replicas, confirm the majority has returned, then start the next replica. The native 4.1.4 fixture observed a Mnesia startup failure when two stopped brokers started together. Retrying the affected broker after its peer was ready restored all three original members. RabbitMQ reliability A broker confirmation advances the publication receipt. A consumer should stage the original event ID and bytes before acknowledging and deduplicate retries by event ID across connections. The native profile received 19 deliveries with 18 distinct IDs. The repeated ID matched its original bytes, and manual ACK emptied all three queues after local staging. The consumer's acknowledgement and its business checkpoint have separate meanings. RabbitMQ consumer acknowledgements Run the isolated profile against a frozen release artifact with Python 3.11 or later and a local Temurin 21 JDK. The fixture uses plain AMQP with loopback host bindings. It checks broker process failures, retained source GTIDs, broker publication receipts, original consumer bytes and manual ACK on three persistent RabbitMQ nodes. TLS, storage loss, performance and consumer business transactions require separate acceptance. Native fixture NATS uses JetStream publish ACKs and Nats-Msg-Id , never volatile Core NATS. Streams require File storage, Limits retention, Discard New, no age expiry, exact namespace. subjects and configured replicas. The description binds pipeline/subscription/generation; incompatible existing streams are rejected rather than altered. Finite capacity rejects new publication. The publisher does not automatically delete consumer history: plan capacity, archival and consumer checkpoints. Broker fsync, replication and disk determine power-loss durability. The three-member NATS 2.11.8 profile uses tls:// for the primary and each explicit failover endpoint, messaging.replicas: 3 , and a JVM trust store with the broker CA. The client verifies the endpoint name against the certificate and uses the configured entrances. The native profile verifies leader loss, refusal to confirm without a majority, and original-event-ID retry after recovery. The broker-to-broker routes and mutual TLS require separate validation. JetStream clustering · Evidence Pre-provisioned streams with autoCreate: false must match the same properties and binding. The binding is rivomesh: plus SHA-256(pipelineId + ':' + subscriptionId + ':' + generation) . Read generation from initialized status; prefer service creation for a new task rather than guessing it. Redis Streams The first Redis profile supports a direct standalone primary running Redis 7.2 or newer . Use redis://host:6379/0 or rediss://host:6379/0 , a database number, separate ACL username/password and messaging.stream . Additional endpoints, Sentinel, Cluster routing and proxy failover are not implemented in this profile. rediss verifies the server hostname using the JVM trust configuration. All logical channels share one physical stream. Each entry contains body , rivomesh event id , rivomesh channel , optional rivomesh key , and transport headers. Redis-generated entry IDs are transport positions, not event identities or MySQL order. Consumers use the same envelope staging/deduplication rules as other message targets. The reserved marker consumer group rivomesh stream marker v1 creates an empty stream without a fake business event; it is not a consumer checkpoint. Preparation requires AOF enabled, maxmemory-policy=noeviction , no TTL on either stream or ownership keys, and a writable non-cluster primary. Ownership is bound per stream in rivomesh publication owners v1 . Existing unowned streams require an adoption plan; another binding is rejected. Previously initialized missing resources are not silently recreated. XADD NOMKSTREAM prevents accidental recreation after deletion while connected. Administrators must not purge/trim/expire these keys; same-name replacement or an old storage backup still requires reconciliation. Each batch uses XADD followed by WAITAOF on the same physical connection . Both returned fsync counts must satisfy local =1 and replicas = replicas-1 ; a timeout alone is not confirmation. The socket factory forbids SDK socket reopening: retries construct a new authenticated client with the configured database, preventing accidental writes into database 0. Server run ID and client ID are also compared around publication to reject hidden connection replacement. AOF write failure, insufficient replicas, OOM under noeviction and disconnection preserve the receipt and retry. replicas: 1 confirms only local AOF, without Redis failover durability. Higher counts require the corresponding live replicas with AOF; they do not provision replication or prove lossless promotion. RDB alone and volatile Pub/Sub are insufficient. The publisher ACL needs connection/auth/select as applicable, INFO, CONFIG GET maxmemory-policy, CLIENT ID, EXISTS/TYPE/PTTL, HGET/HSETNX, XGROUP CREATE, XADD and WAITAOF, limited to the selected stream and ownership hash. Consumers need their own read/group permissions. check reads capabilities without creating keys. WAITAOF and fsync can affect latency; measure against the actual storage and replication topology. No automatic stream trimming is performed; capacity and consumer-safe archival remain an operator responsibility. The direct-primary profile can use an externally managed stable entrance. Fence the unavailable primary before promoting the original AOF replica. Verify its stream entries, ownership binding and consumer group state against the retained checkpoints. Point the existing entrance at the promoted replica and restore enough AOF replicas to meet the configured replicas count. With replicas: 2 , an unavailable second fsync keeps the publication receipt unchanged. An earlier local XADD can already be visible, so consumers deduplicate by event ID and wait for COMMIT and the expected rows. WAITAOF · REPLICAOF Stage the raw event and its stream entry ID before XACK . If the consumer must preserve its acknowledgements on AOF replicas, run WAITAOF on the same connection after XACK and check both counts. Recover the failed consumer's pending entries with XAUTOCLAIM before processing new records. The idle threshold should account for the time a healthy consumer needs to finish processing. Redis Streams replication · XAUTOCLAIM The Redis native fixture uses Redis 7.4.2, Temurin 21 and source events seeded into the packaged JDBC journal. It exercises operator-driven promotion, loss and restoration of a replica fsync, immutable retry bytes, consumer acknowledgements and pending-entry recovery, and a cold restart on the promoted primary's original AOF volume. Sentinel, Redis Cluster, cross-node TLS replication and loss of the acknowledged storage have separate acceptance scopes. A separate Redis 8.0.2 native fixture used Temurin 21, a private CA, hostname verification, a restricted ACL username and password, and DB 2. Untrusted CA, a hostname absent from the certificate and invalid credentials create no keys. An AOF cold restart preserves the original native IDs and snapshot. The publisher resumes to ACK 2. Run python3 tests/redis-tls-run.py --artifact sync-app/target/rivomesh-app-0.1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar --java-home "$JAVA HOME" --output target/redis-tls-proof with local Redis 7.2 or newer and OpenSSL. TLS acceptance record The six-check native run kept the publication receipt at sequence 1 until the second fsync returned, then delivered the original transaction at sequence 2. It retained 11 stream entries with 10 unique event IDs. The repeated event had identical bytes. Four earlier consumer acknowledgements stayed effective, and the recovered consumer claimed the three pending IDs. After the promoted primary restarted, its original stream IDs, group cursor and empty pending list were intact. Pulsar Pulsar uses a dedicated persistent, non-partitioned topic for all mapped namespaces. Configure url: pulsar://host:6650 , messaging.adminUrl: http://host:8080 , cluster , and topic: persistent://tenant/namespace/topic . The tenant/namespace must already exist and belong to exactly the configured cluster; geo-replication needs a separate plan. The first profile uses one service endpoint with native broker discovery; extra endpoints and username/password authentication are rejected. Token authentication uses messaging.token . TLS requires both pulsar+ssl:// and HTTPS admin access with hostname verification. A single-broker TLS and Token profile verifies the configured CA, hostname, credentials and history after broker restart. The transport also has a two-broker and three-bookie recovery profile. Configure a reachable service and admin endpoint for the surviving cluster, and allow the Worker to reach all broker addresses advertised by discovery. For a private CA, mount the PEM bundle on the Worker and on any Agent that runs Check. Use its absolute path in messaging.tlsTrustCertsFilePath . The transport uses that CA for both broker traffic and HTTPS administration. Broker names advertised by the service must appear in their certificate SANs. The Token needs the cluster, namespace and topic permissions required by the configured provisioning policy. Pulsar TLS · Pulsar Token authentication Every active broker must disable automatic topic creation and inactive-topic deletion and enable topic-level policies. Namespace overrides must not re-enable automatic creation. The publisher reads these settings through advertised admin endpoints, requiring cluster/broker/namespace management-read permissions as well as topic operations. Native reconnect must not recreate a deleted empty topic. Restrict administrative policy changes during publication; existence/binding checks cannot detect every purge or restoration of an old backup. Initial creation atomically binds rivomesh.owner to the common pipeline/subscription/generation binding and marks rivomesh.provision=BUILDING V1 . Only that unfinished owned topic is provisioned: infinite retention in both time and size, TTL 0, inactive deletion disabled, BookKeeper persistence, and backlog policies that reject producers rather than evict consumers' history. Applied policies are verified before marking READY V1 and opening a producer. Asynchronous policy propagation retries without publishing. Existing READY policy mismatches, unowned topics or another binding require a plan and are not overwritten. Pre-provisioning with autoCreate: false requires matching ownership, READY V1 and all policies; missing initialized topics never get an empty replacement. replicas means minimum BookKeeper ACK copies for this profile. Fresh topics use ensemble/write/ACK quorum all equal to this value. An existing compatible topic may use a larger ensemble/write quorum if its ACK quorum meets the configured minimum. This setting does not provision bookies, broker replicas or failure domains. Confirmations rely on BookKeeper's durable journal/replication configuration and recoverable metadata. A single-bookie test is not a production HA or power-loss guarantee. Retention is infinite, so plan capacity, archival and consumer-safe history removal. The local quorum fixture uses Pulsar 4.0.14, two active brokers, three BookKeeper nodes and one ZooKeeper node. It checks the original topic binding and the 2/2/2 ensemble, write and ACK policy. After the serving broker exits, the publisher can reopen the existing topic through the surviving service endpoint. The message sink closes an unconfirmed publisher before retrying the same event through a fresh connection. With two bookies offline, a publication that needs two acknowledgements cannot be confirmed. After the original bookies return on their volumes, the transport reopens the existing topic and retries the same stable event ID. Consumers must deduplicate retry attempts. This profile uses an isolated plaintext network. The secure quorum profile combines broker TLS and Token with a three-node metadata quorum. Capacity and storage failure domains require separate acceptance. Pulsar cluster configuration · Verification The secure fixture uses a private CA with a separate certificate for each broker's advertised name. Both broker entry points require HTTPS, Pulsar TLS and Token authentication. With one ZooKeeper leader removed, the two surviving nodes elect a leader. The transport then creates and confirms a new owned Topic and rechecks the original confirmed history. The storage and ZooKeeper peer networks are local to the fixture. Production network cryptography and cross-host durability require their own validation. Pulsar TLS · ZooKeeper and BookKeeper Publication sends bytes synchronously with batching/chunking disabled and bounded pending requests. Message properties carry immutable event ID, logical channel and transport headers; the Pulsar key carries the logical row/transaction key. BookKeeper-confirmed send completion precedes the journal receipt. Pulsar message IDs and broker-side deduplication are not substitutes for event-ID deduplication and transaction staging. Native Pulsar transactions are not used; the common at-least-once contract applies across producer replacement and source lease handoff. Rivomesh pins Pulsar client 4.0.14 behind rivomesh-pulsar-transport . Its logging, crypto, Jackson annotations and protobuf are isolated from core dependencies. The installed Worker uses Temurin 21. Build the reactor with mvn verify so the private SDK is packaged before the application. The transport test runs with the core JAR first on the classpath and verifies both dependency sets coexist; it also verifies read-only check, ownership, send/read, broker restart, retention refusal and lost-topic protection. Full mixed-pipeline recovery acceptance is recorded separately in validation. Broker startup and source catch-up are different measurements. The failure harness first verifies that SQL continues while stopped brokers report automatic retry, then waits for broker health, then measures catch-up without manual Resume. A broker whose admin service or storage is still starting cannot be treated as a ready destination. Recovery diagnostics include safe error codes such as PULSAR ADMIN HTTP 503 ; no row data or credentials are copied into status. Pulsar references: Java baseline decision, topics and resource management, retention versus TTL, broker configuration API. Server storage identity and recovery must be validated for the chosen deployment. Envelope and consumer rules Version 1 includes pipeline/subscriptionId/generation/event ID, kind/namespace, table/schema version, source position and sequence. Publication IDs include subscription identity to prevent deduplication across different mappings; Change.eventId still identifies the logical source event. Values are interpreted through the schema. Numeric strings retain precision; present: false means absent and present: true, value: null means SQL NULL. JSON null is a JSON text value and differs from SQL NULL. Kind Meaning --- --- SCHEMA Columns/types/identity/source indexes; message sinks do not execute DDL/index conversion SNAPSHOT BEGIN , SNAPSHOT ROW , SNAPSHOT END Snapshot ID/baseline/parts/row ordinals/counts; complete only after END and deduplicated counts match BEGIN , ROW , COMMIT Source commit boundary/order/before/after images; COMMIT is published after all row confirmations Primary-key updates expose both beforeKey and afterKey : remove the old identity and insert/update the new identity. Keyless duplicate rows each have a separate rowId. Delete the specified occurrence, not all equal rows. Snapshot and CDC share these occurrence identities. Transaction controls include global totalChanges , per-namespace expectedChanges , transactionKind and source attributes; controls preserve BARRIER changes at their original ordinals. Row ordinals cover the whole transaction projected to that destination. Consumers should durably stage and deduplicate events, await the required rows and COMMIT, verify counts/order, then atomically commit their business work and consumer checkpoint. Different queues/subjects can be consumed at different speeds: an application may observe COMMIT before all rows arrive. COMMIT contentHash is the Codec SHA-256 of the normalized SourceTransaction projected through this destination's mappings. A consumer subscribed to every mapped namespace can reconstruct it from BEGIN's transaction ID/generation/position/kind/attributes and ordered ROW.change values. A consumer of only some namespaces cannot claim to verify the entire hash. Transport epochs are headers outside immutable bodies. Track generation/sequence to prevent late old publications from overwriting newer state; timestamps are not source order. Neither the NATS duplicate window nor Rabbit message IDs replace durable consumer deduplication. Consumer ACKs, crashes, transaction staging capacity, missing rows and long outages require a consumer recovery protocol; this version does not ship an automatically running materialization consumer. Kafka producer idempotence also does not cover all replay after replacing a producer instance. Broker offsets are not source sequences. Handle late old-owner publications through generation/epoch/logical sequence/event ID, not physical offset alone. Consumers selecting one namespace filter envelopes and verify that namespace's expectedChanges. Recovery and FAQ Disconnect/restart: retryable failures preserve checkpoints, reconnect, revalidate established resources and replay unconfirmed work. Permanent permission/routing/property failures pause only that destination. Repair and select its generation-bound Resume action in the UI. Missing queue/stream: MESSAGE DESTINATION MISSING REBUILD REQUIRED requires restoring original broker storage or a recovery plan covering consumers, missing history and a new snapshot. Creating an empty resource and pressing Resume cannot prove historical completeness. An administrator purging/replacing a same-name resource or changing broker policies cannot be detected by an existence check alone; reconcile the data. Cross-target atomicity: destinations confirm independently. One may succeed while another fails. There is no cross-database/broker distributed transaction. Source history remains until lagging subscribers catch up; quota exhaustion stops capture rather than dropping their data. Pause/cutover: message destinations return UNCONFIRMED IN FLIGHT PUBLICATION . A journal epoch cannot retract a broker request already in flight. Fence/stop old producers, establish downstream catch-up barriers, reconcile and isolate business writes before cutover. Automated cutover remains in development. Oversized messages: MESSAGE TOO LARGE preserves the transaction checkpoint. Align application/broker limits and consumer memory. Transparent fragmentation/external LOB storage is unimplemented. Large source transactions, catalog memory and growing receipt history still require resource work; there is no hardware-independent capacity guarantee. Redis confirmation does not arrive: inspect AOF health, required replica AOF fsyncs, replication lag, disk and ACL. REDIS DURABILITY NOT CONFIRMED or REDIS CONNECTION CHANGED DURING CONFIRM leaves publication unconfirmed and replayable, even if XADD already reached the server. Fix the cause without deleting stream history or weakening a running task's durability configuration. The UI's source snapshot rows are source preparation progress; per-destination snapshot confirmations are separate and still do not prove consumer completion. Verification: run SYNC MAVEN CACHE=/path/to/cache bash tests/messaging-run.sh . It creates/restarts/removes only its own Compose project. See validation for versions, results and remaining cluster/TLS acceptance. Protocol references: Kafka 3.9 Java baseline, producer configuration, Rabbit Java client/Java 8 baseline, Rabbit reliability, NATS Java client, JetStream. Protocol documentation does not substitute for this project's environment acceptance. Redis references: WAITAOF same-connection semantics and returned counts, persistence, Jedis. The current client is Jedis 8.0.2 using its single-connection API. RocketMQ native TCP profile The ROCKETMQ publisher is implemented using Java-8-compatible native client 5.5.1 with isolated dependencies. Real native-broker confirmation, client/broker restart, unsafe flush refusal and lost-topic protection passed ( target/rocketmq-transport-cached.log ); mixed snapshot/CDC, worker kill and three broker restart rounds passed ( target/messaging-rocketmq-mixed.log , 49 executions). The earlier single-broker acceptance leaves ACL and TLS for separate verification. The default profile is a single ASYNC MASTER broker group with one local synchronous disk copy , not a synchronous replicated or Raft guarantee. The default profile uses replicas: 1 . Username, password and token remain reserved for an authenticated profile. Use a trusted network for this profile. Configure rocketmq://nameserver:9876 , optional additional NameServers in messaging.endpoints , cluster , broker , topic and minimumRetentionHours . The URI is a native TCP NameServer, not a 5.x gRPC Proxy. topic is a prefix of 1–48 characters (letter first, then letters/digits/underscore/hyphen). The physical topic is prefix 64-hex task/subscription/generation binding . The UI exposes that actual name once the journal generation exists. New generations receive different names; restarting the same generation reuses its name. Reserve these names exclusively for Rivomesh and prohibit external creation, deletion, expansion or writes. Opt in to Controller broker promotion Set messaging.rocketmqControllerEndpoints to the trusted native Controller addresses and messaging.replicas to 2 . The target URL and additional messaging.endpoints continue to be NameServer addresses. In the console's RocketMQ target settings, enter the Controller addresses with ports, separated by commas. The wizard sets the minimum copy count to two. Leaving the field empty uses the original single asynchronous-master profile. Prepare one broker group with exactly three configured data replicas and independent storage. The trusted Controller must use clean election. Before publication, its current master address and replica ID must agree with the NameServer's active route and the live broker settings. Every active SyncStateSet member must be live, and at least two must remain. Use Controller mode with SYNC MASTER on the active broker, SYNC FLUSH , allAckInSyncStateSet=true , minInSyncReplicas=2 , syncFromLastFile=false and asyncLearner=false . Apply the retention, forced-cleanup and automatic-topic settings below to all replicas. This profile uses the AutoSwitch CommitLog, with DLedger CommitLog disabled. RocketMQ Controller deployment Each physical topic includes its journal generation. An uninitialized binding can create its topic on the proven active broker. The adapter waits for the exact one-queue configuration to become visible on the safe SyncStateSet before writing the owner or events. An initialized binding always checks retained metadata and its native history. If topic configuration or a safe route is still catching up after promotion, the publisher retries and keeps the last durable confirmation. Fewer than two live synchronized copies prevent publication. When the confirmed master or term changes, the adapter closes the old SDK connection. It sends synchronously directly to the validated active address, verifies the native message and checks the same Controller and replica view before accepting the receipt. It retains the existing topic generation and ROCKETMQ OFFSET V1 coordinates. A lost or uncertain acknowledgement can still replay an event ID. A confirmed payload mismatch requires investigation before recovery. Conversion between durability profiles requires an explicit migration plan because the Controller profile has its own configuration fingerprint. The RocketMQ 5.5.0 acceptance used a running embedded Controller and three independent Broker volumes. The production publisher retained queue offset 1 and physical offset 451 through master epoch 1 to 2, confirmed the next event at 2 / 906, and reopened from its native receipt. After the remaining follower stopped, the confirmed receipt and the broker queue tail stayed unchanged. Controller outage, broker-data loss, DLedger CommitLog, TLS, ACL and a full CDC Worker switchover have separate acceptance requirements. Keep NameServer, Controller and broker traffic on the trusted network. Native fixture and reproduction Topic and retention settings Preparation reads broker configuration and creates exactly one read/write queue on the selected broker group. The broker must have flushDiskType=SYNC FLUSH , transientStorePoolEnable=false , autoCreateTopicEnable=false , cleanFileForciblyEnable=false , and fileReservedTime = minimumRetentionHours (default 87600 hours). The default mode rejects replicated groups. The optional Controller profile requires the live checks above. Deploy these durability settings at broker startup; do not change storage mode live. The client sends persistent synchronous messages with waitStoreMsgOK and accepts only SEND OK ; disk/slave timeout statuses do not advance the journal checkpoint. Retries can duplicate events with the same stable ID. Queue offset 0 contains an ownership manifest identified by user property rivomesh publication manifest . Consumers must filter this manifest before decoding JSON envelopes. Subsequent messages use the common event envelope and rivomesh event id , rivomesh channel , rivomesh key properties. All logical tables/control channels share queue 0. Consumers still deduplicate and verify SNAPSHOT END / COMMIT and row counts; native broker confirmation does not mean application completion. The manifest permits a crash between topic creation and publication to finish on restart. A nonempty topic with another manifest, missing initialized topic, changed queue/policy, or expired offset 0 blocks with a recovery error. Each publication batch rechecks broker settings, topic shape and manifest. No automatic empty-history replacement is permitted. Retention is finite : plan downstream archival and a verified rebuild before its horizon; large retention values are not infinite storage. Storage loss, manual cleanup, quota and retention expiry require a recovery plan. Monitor broker disk capacity; do not lower retention to clear pressure silently. Run bash tests/rocketmq-transport-run.sh for the actual release-JAR/broker test. The test uses isolated native broker 5.5.0, no host ports, startup data-volume ownership initialization and removes only its Compose project. The default anonymous single-node test does not validate ACL, TLS, power loss, controller/DLedger, replica failover or sustained throughput. Protocol references: server configuration and native client source. A matching manifest alone does not prove retained confirmed history. RocketMQ now also persists and verifies a native confirmation receipt as described below. Other message transports still need their own rollback-detection profiles; do not infer that this protects every broker product. RocketMQ broker-native promotion is verified. The original default profile refused Controller mode. The optional profile uses the requirements above. Native evidence RocketMQ native confirmation receipts After a successful publication batch, the journal saves a generation-bound native receipt before schema/snapshot/transaction receipts advance. New table publication transport contains one small row per subscription; this additive table is created when opening existing journals. Its update is lease-fenced and compares the previously read receipt, so a stale worker cannot replace a newer receipt. Confirmation loss or an uncertain metadata commit still replays stable IDs. ROCKETMQ OFFSET V1 binds the physical topic, queue offset, CommitLog byte offset and a SHA-256 digest of the stable event ID plus message body. On reconnect and before each publication batch, native viewMessage reads the CommitLog record and verifies that receipt. This avoids treating asynchronous ConsumeQueue indexing lag as lost confirmed data. Missing, replaced or changed confirmed records block that destination with ROCKETMQ CONFIRMED HISTORY REBUILD REQUIRED , before further publication or resource creation. Normal restart resumes against the saved receipt. An existing publication without its required native receipt blocks with PUBLICATION TRANSPORT UPGRADE REQUIRES PLAN ; a new binary does not invent an unsafe baseline for an older task. target/rocketmq-native-progress-restore.log passed the actual release-JAR test: stop broker, copy its nonempty volume after the first confirmation, restart and confirm another event, restore the older volume, verify the first event remains while the second is missing, and reject continuation with the saved later receipt. It also rejects a changed content digest and accepts a matching receipt through client restart. target/messaging-native-progress.log additionally passed 53 executions: the actual release JAR, six message products plus PostgreSQL, worker kill and three all-broker stop/start rounds with native receipt recovery. These checks protect the saved confirmed record; they are not an arbitrary-history checksum or consumer business checkpoint. Keep the ownership/retention/storage requirements, consumer count/order verification and archival plan. Do not delete the transport receipt or force a lower offset to bypass failure. A validated recovery/rebuild plan is required when confirmed history has been lost. Receipt rows and other metadata require physical storage headroom beyond the logical event quota. target/v3-native-progress-external.log passed 47 executions, including the native receipt persistence/CAS/lease/reopen contract against actual MySQL, PostgreSQL and openGauss journal storage, plus V3 SQL fan-out and HTTP controls. target/ui-native-progress.log passed 16 DOM tests. Artemis Core retained-queue profile ACTIVEMQ ARTEMIS is a separate product from ActiveMQ Classic. Configure artemis://host:61616 , username/password, explicit database mappings and messaging.stream as a 1–48-character queue prefix (letter first, then letters/digits/underscore/hyphen). messaging.broker optionally checks the broker name. The first profile accepts one entrance, replicas: 1 and no token/extra endpoints. The physical queue is prefix . 64-hex pipeline/subscription/generation binding ; the UI exposes it after generation initialization. The client speaks Core protocol through isolated rivomesh-artemis-transport . Rivomesh pins Core client 2.19.1 with private Netty 4.1.130 and separate logging and JSON libraries. The archived profile used broker 2.57.0, which has its own runtime. Current Workers use Temurin 21. This is a tested compatibility profile, not a claim that every older client/broker/security configuration is supported. The broker must enable persistence, transactional and nontransactional journal sync; preparation reads these runtime attributes. Keep journal-datasync=true in the broker configuration: the management attributes used here do not independently expose/verify that setting. The supplied broker fixture sets it explicitly and uses NIO. Physical storage durability and power-loss acceptance remain separate requirements. A synchronous Core transaction commit precedes publication receipts; lost confirmations still permit stable-ID duplicates. Use a dedicated address-settings match such as rivomesh. for that prefix. Disable auto-create queues/addresses and all auto-delete variants for business resources; the service explicitly creates its first reserved queue. Disable expiry ( no-expiry=true , or all expiry delays -1), last-value/ring/purge behavior and delivery discard ( max-delivery-attempts=-1 ). PAGE/BLOCK/FAIL address policies are accepted; DROP is rejected. A persistent non-destructive ANYCAST queue with exactly one queue bound to its address is required. Existing incompatible resources are refused. Do not change journal-datasync or these policies underneath a running task. Management travels over the same authenticated Core connection, not a separate HTTP admin URL. It uses a temporary non-durable activemq.management. uuid reply queue. Grant the needed management, temporary-queue create/delete, send/consume/browse rights and allow cleanup for this internal prefix. Check creates no business objects; its temporary control channel closes afterward. Do not apply the business no-create policy to this reply prefix. The example fixture separates these address settings; merge the relevant settings into an existing deployment rather than replacing its entire broker configuration blindly.
