Queue offset/record ordering is internal to Artemis. A retained ownership message carries rivomesh publication manifest ; consumers filter that property before decoding subsequent bytes as the common JSON envelope. Published properties carry rivomesh event id , rivomesh channel , rivomesh key and the common headers. Normal consumer ACK does not delete messages from this non-destructive queue. After reconnect consumers may receive older events again and must use durable deduplication/business checkpoints. Native Core byte consumption is tested; AMQP/JMS consumer variants still need their own interoperability acceptance. The service binds the broker's persistent node ID and queue ID in the journal after preparation. Missing initialized queues, changed incarnations, wrong ownership or unsafe queue shape block before publication receipts advance. Preparation can finish an interrupted empty reserved queue; initialized resources are not replaced. The identity is rechecked around publication. After each confirmed batch, the journal also saves ARTEMIS RECORD V1 with physical queue, native message ID, event ID and a length-prefixed event/body SHA-256. Before resuming or sending another batch, a filtered Core browser checks that exact persistent record and content. Missing/changed history blocks even when a restored older nonempty backup retains the same node/queue IDs. This checks the last saved confirmation, not every earlier record or downstream business checkpoint. Existing publications without a native receipt require an explicit migration/rebuild plan; never clear metadata to continue. An empty initialized replacement is rejected without writing a new ownership message. Why does ACK retain history? This profile intentionally keeps the publication log. Plan disk capacity, consumer archival and an explicit rebuild/retention workflow; normal consumer ACK does not reclaim this queue. Can I use an ordinary destructive queue? No; it fails profile validation. Can I point this at ActiveMQ Classic? No; Classic has a distinct protocol/profile and is not implemented by this adapter. Why did Check fail with permissions? In addition to data access, Core management needs its temporary reply-channel grants. The response does not expose credentials or message contents. target/artemis-transport-volume-fixed.log passed Java 8 client/current-broker publication, exact bytes/key/channel, non-destructive consumer ACK, broker/client restart with stable identities, unsafe queue refusal and missing initialized queue protection. Its first failed log concerned isolated data-volume permissions, not protocol acceptance. target/artemis-wiring-unit.log passed 44 core executions; target/ui-artemis-fixed.log passed 17 DOM cases after fixing a product-switch credential visibility bug. Earlier seven-message-product runs failed (timeouts); the later focused case passed as separately recorded below. Cluster, paging-pressure, TLS, power-loss and broader version/security acceptance remain pending. Management API, persistence, address settings. target/artemis-native-progress-final.log passed against the actual release JAR: snapshot the stopped isolated broker volume after one confirmed record, publish a later record, restore the older nonempty volume, prove node/queue IDs are unchanged, and reject the later receipt. Matching receipts resume; altered digests, malformed receipts and empty replacement queues are rejected. The empty replacement remains empty. target/ui-artemis-native-progress.log passed 17 DOM cases. Seven-product mixed recovery is being rerun separately after a previous run recorded source/HTTP timeouts during host sleep. These results do not prove cluster, TLS, paging pressure or power-loss behavior. Shared-store primary and backup Configure one stable TCP entry for the active member of the same shared-store pair. Share the bindings, message journal, paging and large-message directories. Route new connections only to the active Core broker. The publisher still uses one artemis:// endpoint and the retained queue identity. Artemis shared-store HA The Artemis 2.57.0 fixture uses two processes, one local named volume and a stable loopback entry. The standby activated after primary SIGKILL. The publisher kept the previous confirmation while the entry was isolated. After rerouting, it verified the native receipt, broker and queue identity and confirmed the same pending event. Ordinary consumer ACK left both events in the retained queue. Validate storage failure domains, broker TLS, automatic failback and capacity in the deployment. Native evidence Admin retry diagnostics and focused recovery reruns PULSAR ADMIN TIMEOUT means a client-side admin timeout; PULSAR ADMIN CONNECT RETRY means a failed connection. The SDK can wrap either in an exception whose default status is 500, without receiving an HTTP 500 response. Check broker access logs before diagnosing a server error. PULSAR ADMIN REQUEST FAILED preserves an ambiguous generic SDK failure without inventing an HTTP response. Actual HTTP response failures retain their status codes. Credential-provider/TLS rejections are permanent configuration faults; this classification does not constitute TLS interoperability acceptance. Snapshot preparation now emits deduplicated retry diagnostics with exception classes and stack locations, excluding exception messages, credentials, SQL and rows. A transient network fault retains RUNNING and the existing error generation; no manual resume should be needed. Inspect host/VM load, heap/direct memory, broker readiness, network and configured request timeouts rather than assuming a hardware-independent startup/catch-up deadline. After a full build, a focused fault rerun can reuse the accepted release and compiled tests: The checker refuses changed Java sources, stale tests/assets or an invalid release, and verifies the pinned Java-8-compatible JUnit console checksum. This runs one pipeline case , not the full 54-execution Maven suite. Default invocation still builds and runs the wider suite. Failed runs retain full Pulsar logs and bounded other-broker logs under target/broker-tests/ project / ; cleanup affects only that test project. Optional RIVOMESH TEST JAVA OPTIONS supplies JVM diagnostic flags to the isolated test and worker processes, for example -Xlog:gc on Temurin 21. It is a test setting, not a production sizing recommendation. Archived focused acceptance target/messaging-pulsar-gc-diagnostics.log : one real pipeline case passed, zero failed/skipped , on the actual Java 8 release JAR (256 MiB worker heap). PostgreSQL plus Kafka/RabbitMQ/NATS/Redis/Pulsar/RocketMQ/Artemis complete snapshot/CDC, worker kill and three all-message-broker stop/start rounds; SQL continues during broker outage, retry diagnostics persist and clear automatically after catch-up. Finally deleting Artemis's initialized queue pauses only that target while all other subscriptions catch up. Native receipts restore through restart. This took about 590 seconds on the busy shared host, with Java 8 GC diagnostics enabled; no heap/deadline increase was used. It is one focused case, not a fresh pass of the entire 54-execution Maven suite, nor a general capacity/recovery-time promise.

title: Node registry
text: Shared node registry and heartbeat For current deployment, see the multi-node guide. Accounts, sessions and audit can now be shared by explicitly enabling shared access. Registry-only installations keep them local. Task operations are local by default. Optional fixed-owner global control is integrated; explicit controller/Agent separation has initial acceptance, while automatic relocation and the full HA matrix remain open. 中文：节点目录. See global task control and shared access for the corresponding deployment requirements. ADMIN opens Node registry . Standalone mode shows one node with an ID retained in private node-id . With a shared control database, all endpoints in the same clusterId read the same directory. VIEWER/OPERATOR retain existing task grants without global registry access. Cards show release SHA/version, real JVM/architecture/CPU/heap, configured task/running capacities, registration epoch, database observation time, heartbeat/expiry and task IDs/Worker state/observation time. HEALTHY means a valid heartbeat lease, not healthy data destinations. STALE means expiry; STOPPED means graceful deregistration committed. Query failure clears old healthy cards instead of presenting cached success. Task lists are observations, not global configuration/scheduling authority. Task pages/actions are local by default; optional fixed-owner routing is described in global control. Do not copy/start configurations elsewhere merely because a node is STALE. CDC/target leases still govern execution; registry leases cannot authorize Worker takeover. Shared access, global commands and explicit separated execution have distinct profiles; see global control and execution lifecycle for current acceptance. Linux and Docker Use independent local control, task and report directories and unique stable nodeIds. Sharing controller.json/audit H2 directories or a PVC is not a shared control protocol. See platform-cluster.yml. Initial native control-store profiles are PostgreSQL17 and MySQL8.4. H2 memory is for in-process protocol tests. For MySQL use com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver , a MySQL URL and a database namespace. Tables require InnoDB/utf8mb4 bin; incompatible existing tables are rejected. Configure TLS through driver parameters; production TLS is not disabled automatically. Startup needs schema/database and control-table creation permissions plus SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE and bootstrap session-lock access. Existing tables are never cleared/dropped; incompatible formats refuse startup. A shared SQL instance is possible with a separate namespace and dedicated privileges. nodeId, username/password and optional advertiseUrl support a whole-value $ ENV NAME reference. advertiseUrl is observational only, with no user info/path/query/fragment. Connection/query timeouts are bounded; directory APIs omit database URLs, credentials, paths and raw business data. heartbeatMillis is100–30000ms. leaseMillis is1000–300000ms and at least three heartbeat intervals. maximumNodes is1–10000. Defaults are2s/15s/1000. Lease/capacity are consistent cluster settings without online editing. Capacity includes retained STALE/STOPPED records; historical-node administration remains future work. Each node publishes up to200task observations. Keyset pages default to20nodes and allow at most50. Helm and native Kubernetes Set the real URL and an existing username/password Secret in values-cluster.yaml. Install independent releases/PVCs: Each release stays a single-replica Recreate deployment with a stable release-name nodeId. Increasing one Deployment's replicas while sharing its PVC is invalid. Registry-only accounts/sessions remain local. Enable shared access for shared identity/session continuity; this does not provide controller HA. For manual YAML edit/apply node-a and node-b, including image/store/Secret references. Static parity is checked; live Kubernetes/CSI/upgrades/controller HA remain unaccepted. See session HTTPS configuration. Failure handling and FAQ - NODE ID IN USE: another live incarnation holds this ID. Stop the duplicate or use a unique stable ID. After confirmed power loss, wait for expiry without editing epochs. - NODE REGISTRATION FENCED: a replacement owns the registration. The old process cannot renew or deregister it. Correct deployment IDs and restart; this does not establish Worker takeover. - CONTROL STORE PROTOCOL MISMATCH: cluster format/lease/capacity differ or authority metadata is missing. Restore consistent settings/state; startup never overwrites it automatically. - CONTROL STORE UNAVAILABLE / readiness503: registry connection/query failure or expired heartbeat. healthz remains live; Workers follow their own journal leases. After recovery, an expired but unreplaced incarnation re-registers with a higher epoch; replaced processes remain fenced. - Killed nodes briefly remain HEALTHY: until expiry, death cannot be confirmed. Use heartbeat/expiry timestamps; the observation window is not failover authorization. - Old process overwrites replacement: active-ID and incarnation/epoch checks reject old heartbeats and shutdowns. - Graceful shutdown did not show STOPPED: kill, storage failure or lost commit confirmation falls back to STALE through expiry. - Backup/restore: back up the SQL control namespace and each node's existing accounts/audit/configuration/reports. Restoring the registry alone does not restore tasks or provide HA. Rollback of metadata/epochs requires review; external immutable backup anchors remain unfinished. Docker deployment uses http://127.0.0.1:18088 and http://localhost:18089 for two endpoints reading one registry. Different hostnames avoid same-name cookies overwriting across ports. Existing private preview credentials remain; sign in separately. Acceptance fixtures are removed; the development preview remains available.

title: Nonempty target adoption preview
text: Existing PostgreSQL target preview Use preview-adoption to assess existing MySQL data copied to PostgreSQL before registering or starting a pipeline. The preview compares mapped tables with source primary keys. It reports how many rows are missing, extra, changed or equal. Checks use the same canonical types as replication, including JSON values, timestamps and decimals. The second argument names a V3 target ID. The target must be a PostgreSQL primary. Grant the target account schema usage and SELECT privileges on the mapped tables and any existing Rivomesh ownership and job tables. Use the MySQL read and lock privileges documented for common-cut validation. The preview reads PostgreSQL in a READ ONLY transaction and does not open a journal or write ownership, business rows or checkpoints. Schedule the preview during a maintenance window. It holds the MySQL write gate for up to 15 seconds while it establishes the source snapshot and pins the target tables and PostgreSQL REPEATABLE READ snapshot. It releases the write gate before scanning rows. Read locks can delay DDL until the views close. The preview requires the original MySQL lock and snapshot sessions. A disconnect or driver reconnection invalidates the comparison. The report describes the two views at the recorded boundary. New commits after that boundary can change the result. PostgreSQL transaction isolation - MATCH REQUIRES VERIFIED BASELINE means the examined rows compared equal. Keep the report for planning and verify the original data baseline, retained source logs and destination ownership before any adoption. - DIFFERENCES FOUND means at least one comparison found rows to add, remove or reconcile. Stable primary keys determine the corresponding rows. Choose a separate reconciliation or staging plan. - BLOCKED means at least one mapped table cannot be compared safely. Review each table's blocker and any comparisons that succeeded. Existing owners or checkpoints, missing tables, keyless sources, structural mismatches, inheritance, partitions, row security, generation, triggers and extra constraints can block this profile. The preview covers at most 100 discovered source tables, 100,000 rows per side of each compared table, 4 MiB per decoded or canonical row and 64 MiB of accounted retained comparison data per table. Read deadlines are 120 seconds for each view. The limits apply to decoded data in the verifier, while JDBC fetches and JVM overhead require additional memory. Limit, permission and view errors terminate the command without a comparison result. The JSON result contains table names and totals, and uses a SHA-256 digest to identify the observed source position. Plan adoption at a frozen source boundary Use plan-adoption after preview-adoption finds matching data. This profile covers one nonempty InnoDB table in one directly connected MySQL 8.4 database and one UTF-8 PostgreSQL 17 primary. Configure one target and an external PostgreSQL journal with the same JDBC URL as the target, separate absent metadata schemas, and no existing writer assignment. Hold all application writers and pipeline workers stopped while reviewing the plan. PostgreSQL transaction isolation The source operator must enable and persist read only and super read only and keep persisted globals load enabled. The MySQL account must see all tables and related schema metadata and have the grants for the global read lock and replication status checks. The planner refuses inbound replication and group membership. It takes a bounded lock on the original MySQL session and verifies the original physical server and exact binlog boundary before and after comparison. MySQL FLUSH statement The source has a single signed BIGINT primary key, with an optional business UNIQUE on one other signed BIGINT or supported VARCHAR column. The optional UNIQUE requires DOWNGRADE BUSINESS and its exact ordinary PostgreSQL B-tree index before planning. preview-adoption lists the expected ordinary index name under indexPlan . The source profile requires ordinary columns with defaults limited to NULL and admits signed integers, JSON and utf8mb4 0900 bin VARCHAR up to 4,000 characters. Target columns must have matching order and nullability and map to bigint , jsonb or equal-width varchar with explicit pg catalog."C" collation. The target role needs ownership authority, schema and database creation privileges and permission to read pg control system() . Foreign keys, triggers, other indexes and constraints, existing Rivomesh metadata and target subscription membership stop the plan. For UNIQUE(email) , the admitted key is one full VARCHAR(1..320) column. MySQL uses utf8mb4 0900 bin with NO PAD . PostgreSQL uses UTF-8, an equal-width varchar with the built-in deterministic pg catalog."C" collation, the built-in B-tree text ops and blocks of at least 8 KiB. The proof verifies the padding attribute, native comparison behavior and actual index operator class and collation. Case variants, trailing spaces and distinct Unicode normalization forms remain distinct, and multiple NULLs are permitted. This profile rejects case- or accent-insensitive collations, PAD SPACE , blank-padded types and prefix or expression keys. Values must be representable by both engines. PostgreSQL text types exclude U+0000. MySQL binary collations · PostgreSQL collations · PostgreSQL character types · PostgreSQL B-tree entry limits ADOPTION PLAN OBSERVED binds the exact source position, matching row count and digest, configuration and native target identities to the plan SHA-256 digest. The digest stays stable while those inputs match. Limits are 10,000 rows, 1 MiB per row, 16 MiB of retained comparison data and 30 seconds per read guard. JDBC and JVM overhead require additional memory. Keep the result in the operator's private records. PostgreSQL uses a read-only snapshot, so the approval step rechecks the plan while the target has an exclusive table lock. Adopt the approved PostgreSQL baseline Keep the MySQL freeze active and keep application writes and every Rivomesh worker stopped. Use the same configured PostgreSQL user for the journal and the target. The role must be able to lock the target table and the event trigger catalog, and create both private metadata schemas plus the ownership table. Use the source table name from the plan, its exact digest and a stable request UUID with the local operator's audit identifier. The command recomputes the source cut, schema, target native catalog and matching rows under the held freezes. PostgreSQL creates ownership, an already-complete snapshot and its acknowledgement, the captured MySQL position, the empty delivery checkpoint and the approval receipt in one transaction. The adopted job starts PAUSED . Business data remains where it was copied, so the normal worker can begin streaming from the approved binlog position. If the command returns ADOPTION COMMIT UNKNOWN , keep the freeze and use the identical approval to confirm the durable receipt before resuming. A confirmed replay verifies the paused baseline, native table, rows, target ownership and both checkpoints. A changed request, incomplete metadata or drift fails closed. Keep the original review and receipt in the operator's private records. If the job has already resumed, use its normal status and recovery commands. After a confirmed receipt, the maintenance operator can remove the source write fence and run resume-pipeline with resumeErrorGeneration , then start the ordinary worker. Keep target application writers stopped during sync. Retain the source binlog covering the approved cut until the worker catches up. Application write handover and failback remain separate operations. Restore the approved business UNIQUE at the original adoption cut When the adoption includes restoreUnique , its planSha256 includes the expected name and key of the new UNIQUE and the physical identity of the existing ordinary index. Keep the original MySQL freeze and the adopted job paused. Run the following command with a new restoration request UUID and operator. The command rechecks the original cut, table rows and native catalog, then adds a nondeferrable UNIQUE NULLS DISTINCT and commits one native receipt with the DDL. Keep the existing ordinary index. The approved restoration receipt becomes part of readiness for this table. On ADOPTED UNIQUE COMMIT UNKNOWN , keep the freeze and retry the identical request. prepare-target-writer checks the approved restoration, including the physical constraint and ordinary index. Building the expected constraint manually does not supply the required receipt. The constraint remains in force after pre-write failback and ordinary CDC accepts it only with matching native proof. Record application writer readiness Use prepare-target-writer while the single-table adoption is still paused at its original baseline. Keep the original MySQL source physically connected and durably frozen, and keep the application and Rivomesh writers stopped under exclusive administration of both databases. Provide the original adoption digest, request UUID and actor, plus the PostgreSQL writer login, a new request UUID and the reviewing operator. The target administration account needs to lock pg authid , pg auth members and the event trigger catalog. PostgreSQL privileges The dedicated PostgreSQL login needs CONNECT , schema USAGE and table SELECT . Admission requires the role to be disconnected, have no role memberships and hold no table or column write privileges. Other grants that introduce a parallel writer, writable views accessible to this login, and executable user-defined SECURITY DEFINER routines also stop the review. Privileged administrators must keep exclusive control of schema, role and application-routing changes during the maintenance window. TARGET WRITER READINESS RECORDED identifies a native receipt recording the exact adoption, source cut, target rows and authority evidence, role identity and review approval. On WRITER READINESS COMMIT UNKNOWN , repeat the original request while the source is still frozen and its cut can be verified. Replay checks the live row state, authority and cut again. Keep the receipt and its receiptSha256 with the original migration plan. Activate one PostgreSQL writer or return the original source before any committed target write This procedure covers the original paused single-table adoption cut. Keep the MySQL write fence in effect and keep application connections stopped while changing authority. Use the same adoption identifiers and the full readiness receipt SHA-256 with a fresh operation request UUID and actor. The operator owns application routing to the target after the acknowledged grant. Activation holds exclusive target table and role catalog locks, checks the frozen source and approved rows, grants the reviewed login INSERT , UPDATE and DELETE on this table, and records TARGET WRITER in the journal. The normal resume-pipeline command refuses this state. The same PostgreSQL commit installs a protected statement trigger that records attempted business DML in its transaction. A rolled-back statement leaves no committed witness. A committed write followed by restoring the old row contents still leaves a witness. PostgreSQL CREATE TRIGGER Stop the target application and disconnect the dedicated login before requesting failback. Keep both administrative and application routes under exclusive control. The command locks the table, verifies the witness definition and catalog revision, checks both original row digests, then revokes the target write privileges before marking the pipeline PAUSED . TARGET WRITER REVOKED confirms that the original source is eligible for the operator to re-enable. If needed, resume the pipeline using the returned resumeErrorGeneration after reopening source writes. On TARGET WRITER COMMIT UNKNOWN , keep application routes closed and the MySQL freeze active, and repeat the identical operation. TARGET WRITER WRITE OCCURRED requires a separately reconciled reverse migration with an approved new source baseline. TARGET WRITER HISTORY UNCERTAIN indicates the continuity marker is missing. PostgreSQL clears it after crash recovery, when an asynchronously acknowledged application commit and its write witness might both have been lost. A changed or missing witness requires investigation before any source write re-enable. PostgreSQL unlogged tables Review downgraded UNIQUE indexes before handover For an already managed PostgreSQL target, establish and complete a common-cut report for the destination, and keep the pipeline paused. Suspend business writes and DDL on the target, then run the review with the same task configuration and report ID. The review verifies the report scope, durable journal cut, target ownership, completed snapshots and physical checkpoint. It acquires the journal and target checkpoint locks, queries PostgreSQL, then rolls back the lock transactions. Business rows, indexes and checkpoints keep their current values. Scans cover up to 100 mapped tables and 128 relevant indexes under a 120-second deadline. Use the synchronization account, which can lock the current checkpoint rows. For a downgraded simple business UNIQUE, the review counts conflicting key groups and rows using PostgreSQL's target column collations and default NULLS DISTINCT behavior. A multicolumn key with at least one NULL does not contribute to these counts. The response lists key column names and counts. Different collation rules can produce conflicts even when the original MySQL and PostgreSQL row contents compared equal. PostgreSQL unique indexes · ICU collations - DUPLICATES FOUND identifies conflicts to reconcile before restoring the constraint. - REQUIRES RECONCILIATION points to recorded exclusions, differences in the historical comparison or a special index that needs its own plan. - NO DUPLICATES OBSERVED describes this read view. Review the final cut, SQL definition and expected business semantics before approving any constraint or write handover. Resuming or moving the checkpoint invalidates this report for a new review. - NO DOWNGRADED UNIQUE indicates the selected scope has no relevant candidate. This profile checks mapped plain PostgreSQL tables and default B-tree key semantics. GSI uniqueness, expressions, prefix lengths, nondefault operator classes and alternate null policies need separate review. Constraint creation, write handover and failback remain operator actions under the migration plan. Observe a frozen restoration plan The bounded restoration planner covers one downgraded business UNIQUE on a keyed InnoDB table. It requires a direct standalone MySQL 8.4 endpoint with source.topology: AUTO , no configured candidate nodes, and a UTF-8 PostgreSQL 17 primary. Stop application writers on both sides, establish a matching common-cut report and keep Rivomesh paused. Then have the source database operator place the same MySQL instance in read only and super read only mode. The source must stay on the report's exact server UUID, GTID, binlog file and offset. MySQL can still admit replication writes in read-only mode, so any configured inbound channel or Group Replication membership is rejected. MySQL server variables Use the table ID and original index name shown by review-unique . The planner verifies a sealed matching report and rejects recorded source or target exclusions. It obtains a bounded MySQL global read lock on the already frozen server, checks the original session and rehashes source rows. It holds the paused journal fence and a PostgreSQL table and checkpoint lock while reading target rows, confirming ownership, checking uniqueness and observing the original ordinary index. The supported scope is 10,000 rows, 1 MiB per canonical row, a 16 MiB private scratch budget and a 30-second fence. The source account needs the common-cut read, lock and replication status privileges. The target account also needs permission to execute pg catalog.pg control system() for physical identity. PostgreSQL control data functions Supported key columns are signed integers mapped to bigint , or ordinary MySQL utf8mb4 0900 bin VARCHAR mapped to PostgreSQL varchar or text with explicit pg catalog."C" collation. The planner checks the existing ordinary B-tree index's columns, order, collation and default operator classes. Neither GSI nor expression or generated key columns are covered. Case variants, trailing spaces and NULL handling follow the stated profile. MySQL binary collations · PostgreSQL unique indexes RESTORE PLAN OBSERVED includes a stable SHA-256 digest of the plan, including report seal, exact positions, current table content, journal namespace and target physical identity and timeline. Keep the output as a review artifact. To compare the reviewed digest, rerun the command with --expect-sha256 digest . It verifies the live state again and refuses a changed plan, including an index rebuild. A change in source GTID, even outside the table, rejects this cut. Fresh row hashes also detect writes excluded from the MySQL binlog and external target edits. The observation expires when the freeze, target state or cut changes. Apply an approved PostgreSQL UNIQUE restoration This CLI profile requires one destination and a PostgreSQL external journal configured with exactly the same JDBC URL as the destination. The operator runs with the PostgreSQL privileges to lock the journal, target metadata, business table and event trigger catalog, and to add a constraint and write a receipt. Enabled target event triggers stop execution. The operator keeps exclusive control of both databases during the maintenance window, including startup configuration, replication, privilege changes and application writers. The direct, standalone MySQL source must have both read only and super read only active and persisted, with persisted globals load enabled on the original instance. Native persistence supports a restart on the same host and data directory using the same startup options. Rivomesh checks both persisted flags, original source and binlog cut, and the pinned session immediately before committing PostgreSQL. Keep the write fence in place through receipt resolution and the separately managed business handover. MySQL persisted system variables Review a version-2 plan and use its exact digest, a stable request UUID and the local operator's audit identifier. The command recalculates the plan under the source freeze and a single PostgreSQL transaction that holds the journal cut, subscription, target checkpoint, snapshot, owner and business table locks. It adds one validated, nondeferrable UNIQUE NULLS DISTINCT , retains the ordinary index and stores the approved digest, actor, request ID and native catalog evidence in the same transaction. PostgreSQL must have fsync enabled, and the transaction uses synchronous commit. Business rows, pipeline state and write authority keep their existing values. PostgreSQL ALTER TABLE UNIQUE RESTORED indicates an acknowledged PostgreSQL commit or a verified native receipt for the identical request. UNIQUE RESTORE COMMIT UNKNOWN indicates that the driver could not confirm the commit. Keep the freeze and report, and retry the identical request to resolve it. A request with a different actor, scope or digest conflicts with the stored approval. A receipt whose native constraint has changed also requires operator review. Application write handover and failback remain separate operations. FAQ Does equality let me start a new pipeline on the existing tables? A new run still requires compatible empty tables. The preview neither establishes a usable replication position nor grants ownership. For a nonempty target, plan a verified baseline and write handoff, or synchronize into separate empty schemas and reconcile before switching. Does it examine other tables in the destination schemas? The preview examines same-named tables selected by the configured source-to-target schema mappings. Inventory any extra schemas or tables as part of the migration. Can this repair existing data or restore a downgraded UNIQUE constraint? Use common-cut repair for already managed targets and its own validation. Constraint restoration, final write handoff and failback need a product-specific plan. 中文

title: OceanBase
text: OceanBase destination and FAQ 中文：OceanBase V3. Example: oceanbase-v3.yml. Current scope V3 configuration, CLI, fan-out workers and the bilingual wizard support OceanBase. The historical OceanBase CE 4.3.5.6 ARM64 and Java 8 profile passed native transactions and mixed MySQL-to-OceanBase-and-PostgreSQL snapshot, CDC and recovery. The MySQL-mode tenant profile remains EXPERIMENTAL. Oracle mode, OBProxy, multi-node and further Temurin 21 combinations require separate acceptance. Verification product: OCEANBASE uses MySQL Connector/J 8.4.0 and jdbc:mysql:// , normally port 2881. Connect to a MySQL-mode user tenant , usually with rivomesh@business , rather than root@sys . Every new connection verifies OceanBase identity, mode and a non-system tenant, then forces ob read consistency=STRONG . A MySQL wire version is not the OceanBase product version. Oracle mode, seekdb and other compatible products are outside this verified profile. Start and recover Fill in source candidates, the user tenant and explicit database mappings, then supply MYSQL PASSWORD and OCEANBASE PASSWORD . Source GTID/ROW/FULL and privileges are documented in the V3 manual; UI steps are in the console manual. In another terminal use status config/oceanbase-v3.yml . After repairing a deterministic failure, resume the affected target in the UI, or use resume config/oceanbase-v3.yml oceanbase-business 7 with the same java -jar ... prefix. Replace 7 with the current errorGeneration from status; never guess it. Resume retries the original transaction. OceanBase is V3-only; select it in the wizard and provide a user-tenant identity. Extra destinations can select PostgreSQL or other products independently. Data, transactions and indexes Explicit mappings send each source database to a destination database in the same tenant. A configuration can fan out to OceanBase, PostgreSQL and other targets with independent acknowledgements and pauses. Rivomesh can create mapped databases/tables; it does not provision clusters, pools, tenants or users. Business changes and the sink checkpoint commit in one destination transaction, with a metadata row lock and epoch fencing. An uncertain commit is resolved by rereading the sink checkpoint. Capture progress never substitutes for apply progress. Independent destinations do not share a global atomic commit. Keyless tables gain rivomesh row id to retain duplicate multiplicity; business users must not edit it. UINT64 uses DECIMAL(20,0), decimals keep declared precision, JSON uses native JSON, binary uses LONGBLOB, and temporal values follow the relational-target mappings. Supported source generated expressions are evaluated by the existing source adapter and their values are copied into ordinary target columns. Procedures, triggers, foreign keys, partition layouts, physical index distribution and generated expressions are not automatically reproduced. Existing incompatible targets require an adoption plan. The default uniquePolicy: DOWNGRADE BUSINESS converts business UNIQUE indexes into ordinary indexes. Primary/actual identity keys must remain unique. Plain BTREE/simple GSI can use the current ordinary-index plan; global routing, global uniqueness and source partition semantics are not preserved. Expressions, prefixes, descending keys, fulltext and spatial methods require an explicit plan. PRESERVE can retain representable business uniqueness, subject to native DDL constraints; it does not reproduce arbitrary GSI semantics. Downgrading assumes exclusive synchronization writes, valid source constraints and complete ordered source transactions. It does not guarantee uniqueness under independent target writes. Existing UNIQUE constraints are never silently dropped. Before takeover, stop incremental writes, reconcile the data and restore required constraints. The complete automated takeover workflow remains pending. Deployment and privileges Use the same V3 task document with Linux, Docker, Helm or native Kubernetes deployment. Rivomesh manifests do not deploy OceanBase itself; database operations manage production clusters, OBProxy, tenant resources and isolation. The target account needs metadata access and appropriate mapped-database/table/index creation and business/metadata read/write privileges. A successful connection check does not prove all DDL/DML privileges. Supply passwords through environment references or protected configuration. LOCAL Journal supports same-host recovery. Cross-host worker takeover uses the already-supported external PostgreSQL/openGauss/MySQL journal. journal.product: OCEANBASE is rejected until that backend has its own acceptance. Controller HA and live Kubernetes/CSI acceptance remain separate work. Failures and FAQ - Tenant mismatch: verify the user suffix, OBProxy routing and tenant compatibility mode. System/Oracle tenants are rejected; mode is never changed automatically. - Outage/restart: recognized transient connection failures back off and reconnect, then catch up from destination progress. Other sinks continue until journal backpressure applies. OceanBase manages its own leader elections; multi-node/OBProxy failover needs separate acceptance. - SQL failure: only the affected subscription pauses. Repair permissions, types or constraints, then use the current errorGeneration in UI/CLI to replay the original transaction. Restart does not bypass the pause or skip events. - Deleted tables/metadata: an empty replacement is not silently created under an old checkpoint. Preserve evidence and plan a rebuild. A normal resume cannot repair deleted data or lost history. - Why STRONG reads: a recovery decision must observe committed checkpoint state. WEAK reads can return an older value; URL settings cannot override this profile's STRONG requirement. - Why a separate product from MYSQL: the wire protocol is similar, but vendor, tenant and consistency requirements differ. - Source DDL: initial auto-creation does not imply complete online DDL. Unsupported structural changes retain safe progress and require a conversion plan; do not edit GTIDs to bypass them. Full DDL, reconciliation/repair and migration workflows remain pending. - Existing targets: compatible empty tables can pass shape/ownership checks. A newly adopted nonempty table needs a provable baseline and adoption plan even if it looks identical. Rivomesh does not silently clear it or attach an unproved checkpoint. - Capacity: fixture CPU/memory/disk quotas are correctness-test settings, not hardware throughput standards. Benchmark row width, transaction size, indexes, fan-out, backlog windows and tenant resources. Hardware capacity reports remain pending. Official references - Official Docker fixture and resource settings - MySQL-mode transaction control - System variables Test-image startup diagnostics The official all-in-one fixture passed with an 8 GiB observer limit, 1 GiB system memory, 3 GiB tenant unit, 10 GiB container cap and six CPUs. It used 5 GiB observer log and 2 GiB data sizing. These settings reproduce the correctness run. Size production from its own measured workload. Unit memory is not exclusively business-tenant memory: an actual 2GiB unit probe showed roughly 1GiB for the user tenant after splitting with its metadata tenant. Other tenants, caches and host load affect recovery. A boot success! banner is insufficient; this image can print it even when OBD memory checks prevented observer startup. Check the actual observer process, user-tenant connection, container health and OBD logs together. Do not delete existing data or skip synchronization checkpoints to repair inadequate startup resources. Do not blindly use obd cluster start -f ; this version's -f means force-delete, not bypassing resource checks. Reproduce native recovery Build the current release, then run tests/oceanbase-pipeline-run.sh . It checks the tenant and transaction fence, then exercises full load, CDC, outage catch-up, SIGKILL resume, independent SQL failures on both targets, repair and missing-table isolation. It cleans up its own database resources. RIVOMESH TEST ARTIFACT selects a frozen repository-relative JAR. Earlier 6 GiB-container attempts included OBD memory admission, tenant recovery and administrative DDL timeouts. The passing fixture used the resource settings above and the original transaction checkpoints.

title: OIDC sign-in
text: Sign in with your organization 简体中文 Rivomesh can sign browser users in through one OpenID Connect (OIDC) provider across Controllers behind a shared HTTPS origin. Each provider identity must be explicitly bound to an existing Rivomesh account. The shared account directory supplies the role, task grants and node grants. Provider claims such as email, username, role and groups carry no Rivomesh authority. Existing browser token sign-in and Bearer API calls remain available. Prepare the provider and Controllers Register a confidential OIDC client for authorization code flow, PKCE S256, token endpoint authentication with client secret basic and ID tokens signed with RS256 . Register the exact callback, such as https://sync.example.gov/auth/oidc/callback . Use the immutable, case-sensitive sub the provider issues to this client. A pairwise subject can differ between OIDC clients for the same person. Authorization and token endpoints must be fixed HTTPS URLs on the configured issuer's origin. Obtain the correct kid and RSA public key from your provider through a trusted administrative channel. OpenID Connect Core, OAuth 2.0 Security BCP Start from a working shared global control deployment. Upgrade all members to a build that understands external bindings before adding them. Apply the same OIDC profile and external origin to all Controllers serving the login URLs. The database account must be able to initialize the shared rmc oidc attempt table. Agents need no OIDC configuration or provider secret. rsaPublicKey is standard base64 of the DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo for a 2048–4096 bit RSA public key. Remove whitespace and PEM delimiters from the exported public key. The client secret belongs in its Controller service environment. On Linux and Docker supply it with the platform configuration above. For manual Kubernetes mount the platform configuration through ConfigMap and supply RIVOMESH OIDC CLIENT SECRET through secretKeyRef on the Controller pods. For Helm, apply the existing global-control values, set sessions.publicOrigin and set oidc.enabled=true . Use the same OIDC keys except clientSecret ; set oidc.existingSecret and oidc.clientSecretKey for the Kubernetes Secret instead. Route / , /auth/oidc/ and /api/ through the same HTTPS frontend. Keep callback query parameters out of proxy access logs. Check that the JVM trusts the provider's TLS certificate chain and that Controller clocks are synchronized. Once configured, the sign-in screen shows Sign in with your organization . Bookmarks can use /auth/oidc/start on the same hostname. Bind or revoke access Sign in to the console as an administrator and open Accounts and grants . On the existing account, choose Bind organization identity and enter the case-sensitive subject issued for this client. The form shows the configured issuer, and the preview shows whether a subject was entered. Afterward, the account card shows the issuer and subject digest. Use Replace organization identity to supply a new subject or Revoke organization identity to remove the binding. Sign in again after a successful change. Existing bindings can still be inspected and revoked when organization sign-in is disabled on this Controller. Reload the account directory before retrying a revision conflict. If a request result is uncertain and the current session still works, retry with the same fields to reuse its request ID. If the session ended, sign in again and check the account card. API 1. Sign in as an existing Rivomesh administrator and create or review the local account and its task and node grants. 2. Get the current directory revision with GET /api/accounts . 3. Send PUT /api/accounts/ accountId /external-identity with a fresh X-Request-ID , the current revision, exact issuer and subject. Existing browser administrator sessions must send the matching Origin and X-CSRF-Token . An administrator can also use Bearer API authentication. 4. To remove the external identity, send DELETE to the same URL with a fresh X-Request-ID and just expectedRevision . The local account and its token remain usable unless separately disabled or rotated. Example binding body: The account directory exposes the issuer and a SHA-256 digest of the subject to administrators. Each provider identity can be bound to one account. Binding, replacing and revoking follow the shared directory's revision policy and invalidate all existing browser sessions across Controllers. Admin actions are recorded as ACCOUNT EXTERNAL BIND and ACCOUNT EXTERNAL REVOKE . The audit trail records the local identity for a successful callback and omits provider codes, tokens and subjects. Troubleshooting and lifecycle - OIDC LOGIN DENIED . Start again from the Rivomesh login screen. A callback can be used once, within five minutes, and only with the browser that started it. Repeated or invalid callbacks are denied. If a fresh attempt fails, confirm the exact issuer, provider subject, audience, signing key and current local account status. - OIDC PROVIDER UNAVAILABLE . Check access from each Controller to the fixed token endpoint and the JVM's TLS trust, then start a new sign-in. A used callback cannot be retried. If the shared control store is unavailable, the response is CONTROL STORE UNAVAILABLE . - ACCOUNT EXTERNAL IDENTITY CONFLICT . Review the existing binding in the shared directory and explicitly revoke it before reassigning that identity. - Provider account disabled or signed out . Revoke the local binding or disable the Rivomesh account to stop existing Rivomesh sessions immediately. Each OIDC session expires by the earlier of the signed ID token expiry and the configured session limit. Rivomesh logout ends the local session. Provider logout notifications and automatic provider-session checks are outside this profile. - Provider changes a signing key . Coordinate a fixed profile update on all Controller entries and restart them with the replacement kid and public key. Pending sign-ins must restart after the profile changes. The profile uses a configured key and endpoints and has no runtime discovery or automatic key rotation. Local token sign-in remains available during the rollout. The H2-backed HTTPS fixture covers invalid signatures and claims, one-time state and cross-entry revocation. Real Keycloak 26.7.4 also passed with two Controllers sharing PostgreSQL and one trusted HTTPS ingress. Chrome starts on A and completes S256 PKCE on B. A signed provider role leaves the local Viewer, task and node grants in force. Revoking the binding through B invalidates both entries while the provider session is active. Native verification · Reproduce

title: Oracle source
text: Oracle source, archived capture and preflight 中文 The Oracle 26ai profile verifies one writable CDB/PDB, archive mode, force and minimal supplemental logging, source identity and Flashback read access. Archived capture and durable SCN recovery to PostgreSQL were revalidated on ARM64 with Oracle Free 23.26.4.0.0, Temurin 21 and Oracle JDBC 23.26.4.0.0. SO-07 tracks the remaining versions, types, RAC and failover. 1. Provide an Oracle JDBC JAR compatible with your Java runtime alongside the Rivomesh JAR. Oracle JDBC compatibility 2. Give the CDB-root account read access to V $DATABASE , V $INSTANCE and the selected PDB in V $PDBS . Configure its CONTAINER DATA visibility for that PDB. Give the PDB account read access to its V $PDBS identity and SELECT and FLASHBACK on the declared tables. Oracle container data privileges 3. Configure the two services and uppercase OWNER.TABLE names with the probe example. The report includes DBID, the resetlogs SCN, PDB GUID and a common snapshot SCN. It checks a Flashback read in each table at that SCN and reports primary-key presence. For ORACLE WRITABLE PDB REQUIRED , verify the PDB is open read/write and the root account can see that PDB. For ORACLE PDB AUTHORITY MISMATCH , compare the supplied service and PDB identity. The native fixture verifies keyed and keyless tables, a historical update/delete and rejection of the root service supplied as the PDB. Add --logminer for the native archive verification. One commit XID contains an update and keyless delete with redo and undo SQL, and the committed-only result excludes a rolled-back insert. Oracle LogMiner Add archiveWindow.startScn and archiveWindow.endScnExclusive as decimal strings to validate a selected archived interval. The root account needs read access to V $THREAD and V $ARCHIVED LOG . The check covers the current resetlogs incarnation and one redo thread. CATALOG CONTIGUOUS reports uninterrupted catalog coverage. ORACLE ARCHIVE LOG GAP indicates that the archive catalog does not cover the entire interval. Retain the original interval and verify physical files with LogMiner before a recovery. Set archiveWindow.decodeCommitted: true to read the registered archive files with LogMiner. The CDB-root account additionally needs LOGMINING , EXECUTE on SYS.DBMS LOGMNR and access to SYS.V $LOGMNR CONTENTS . The report includes the committed transaction count, operation counts and SHA-256 of typed changes. The probe reads the generated redo and undo statements as data. It accepts complete images for supported NUMBER(p,s) , VARCHAR2 and DATE columns, and refuses crossing transactions, split redo statements, missing supplemental images and unsupported operations or types. Enable appropriate supplemental logging on each table before recording the interval. The decoded output includes the last typed commit coordinate with commit SCN and XID. Replay groups complete transactions with per-transaction event ordinals. It refuses an ambiguous sequence if different XIDs share a commit SCN. The native fixture also rotates an initially unarchived suffix and verifies a second distinct commit coordinate. V3 Oracle to PostgreSQL Use the V3 example with source.type: ORACLE . The first experimental profile uses Oracle 26ai Free 23.26.4.0.0 on ARM64 and PostgreSQL 17.12. Declare uppercase source owners and tables, owner-to-destination schemas and one writable PDB. The root account additionally needs read access to V $TRANSACTION and V $PDB INCARNATION , plus the archive and LogMiner permissions above. Use all-column supplemental logging for each selected table. The PDB account reads the selected tables, their metadata and the common Flashback SCN. For the UI, launch the runtime that owns the Worker ( serve in combined mode or agent in a separated cluster) with the same classpath. In New task choose V3 → Oracle or import the V3 task. Enter the CDB root and PDB services separately, the PDB name and uppercase OWNER.TABLE selections. Map each source owner to a PostgreSQL schema and run Check on the assigned Agent before starting. The supervised Worker inherits the separately supplied Oracle JDBC driver from the owner’s classpath. The profile supports bounded NUMBER(p,s) , VARCHAR2 and DATE in keyed and keyless rows. The snapshot uses one SCN per capture start. An interrupted unfinished snapshot can restart from a new Flashback view while completed snapshots remain reusable. Capture polls closed archive segments. The durable coordinate binds CDB DBID and resetlogs, PDB GUID, UID and incarnation, captured SCN and the retained archive floor. A transaction already open at the snapshot can hold that floor back. When its commit lands in a closed archive, the complete transaction enters the journal. The floor advances only after coverage passes the SCN of a later active-transaction sample. Retain archives starting from the reported floor. Verify archive rotation and retention under the real workload. A missing archive, unsupported record, ambiguous ordering or unreviewed DDL stops capture with the previous durable position. Use the capture review and preserve the source and journal. Source promotion, RAC, online-redo capture, native binary JSON, LOBs, other generated expressions and further target profiles require separate acceptance. Oracle active transactions · PDB incarnation Archived DDL review When a selected PDB's archived DDL stops capture with ORACLE REDO DDL REQUIRES PLAN , open Capture recovery on the failed task or call its read-only GET /api/tasks/ id /capture-recovery endpoint. The report binds the error generation and the last durable checkpoint hash. The CURRENT ORACLE PDB CATALOG VS JOURNAL comparison uses the last recorded schema version and digest for each selected table, plus a separate digest of the definition visible now. It reports changes in supported column names, types, sizes, nullability, column order and the recorded primary key. Checkpoint admission checks that the retained Oracle source is eligible to revisit the cut. The current catalog may reflect later DDL. It cannot establish the historical shape or the SQL at the blocked archive record. Oracle's versioned LogMiner dictionary tracking requires a different dictionary mode than the current online catalog reader. An unsupported shape or unavailable catalog check produces an UNAVAILABLE result with its source error. An unchanged visible definition can coexist with a blocked DDL record because the selected tables or the recorded metadata may omit the changed object. Preserve the archive floor and review a replacement baseline. Applying or advancing past Oracle DDL requires a separate approved transition. Oracle LogMiner dictionary tracking The disposable acceptance fixture uses tests/oracle-source-probe.py --logminer --pipeline --ddl-review with a Temurin 21 artifact and the Oracle JDBC driver. It compares the first current schema, a later edit and an unsupported current shape against the same recorded checkpoint. When the stopping scan supplies a complete USER DDL or INTERNAL DDL row with verified PDB identity, the report also includes blockedArchiveEvent . The top-level USER DDL (PlSql=0 RecDep=0) form seen on Oracle Free 26ai qualifies. The report records the SCN, RS ID , SSN , archive window and SHA-256 of the SQL text as read by JDBC. The journal stores the fingerprint with the failure generation under the capture lease. It checks the checkpoint hash again when serving the report. A subsequent catalog query or archive scan cannot substitute a different row for that failure. The journal keeps at most one observation per pipeline. A newer failure can replace the stored observation under its own generation. An older failure, incomplete row or failed evidence write returns ORACLE DDL EVIDENCE UNRECORDED . A corrupted or differently bound record returns ORACLE DDL EVIDENCE INVALID . Both leave the existing DDL stop in force. The fingerprint documents the observed row from the online catalog session. Approval of a nullable column addition still needs the historical dictionary and complete DML at the boundary, a verified schema delta and target receipts at the original cut. Add --ddl-fingerprint to the disposable DDL review fixture to compare the stored hash with the archive record and then archive a later DDL and DML. Savepoints and partial rollback Archived capture uses LogMiner with COMMITTED DATA ONLY . On Oracle Free 26ai 23.26.4.0.0, the nested SAVEPOINT and ROLLBACK TO fixture produced seven canceled changes and seven compensation records in the unfiltered archive. The committed-only scan returned the four surviving changes for that transaction on both reads. The test covers successive changes to the same keyed row, a canceled primary-key change, a canceled delete and duplicate keyless rows. Oracle LogMiner · Oracle redo record fields This acceptance covers the tested scalar columns on a single Oracle instance and closed archives. If a selected row still exposes a rollback flag, capture can stop with ORACLE REDO PARTIAL ROLLBACK UNSUPPORTED in the SOURCE DECODE phase. Inspect the capture status with the DBA and retain the reported SCN, its archive floor and the journal. The target's skip and row repair workflows apply to journaled transactions. A source decode failure must be resolved at the source or through a reviewed rebuild from a new baseline. Reproduce the closed-archive and Flashback comparisons with tests/oracle-source-probe.py --logminer --savepoint-evidence , the Temurin 21 JAR and the Oracle JDBC driver. Add --pipeline --savepoint-pipeline to check independent PostgreSQL subscriptions with separate data and metadata schemas, including original snapshots and target receipts after a forced Controller and Worker restart. BLOB and CLOB preflight For a selected Oracle table with BLOB or CLOB , preflight checks the storage mode in ALL LOBS and refuses archived capture. ORACLE SECUREFILES LOB UNDO UNAVAILABLE identifies SecureFiles, for which LogMiner does not supply LOB undo SQL. ORACLE BASICFILES LOB REQUIRES PROFILE identifies BasicFiles, which needs a separate complete-image and replay profile. ORACLE LOB STORAGE UNPROVEN applies to partitioned LOBs or when the reader cannot determine the storage mode. Oracle LogMiner data types and SecureFiles · Oracle ALL LOBS On Oracle Free 26ai 23.26.4.0.0, Flashback recovered the original nonempty values for BasicFiles and SecureFiles BLOB and CLOB. All 12 short-value updates for those tables yielded undo SQL with PAYLOAD = NULL , including updates with a known non-NULL prior value. A two-byte or two-character write into a 5,000-unit value emitted SEL LOB LOCATOR and LOB WRITE records with status 2 and no undo. Two scans of the closed archive returned the same 30 records byte for byte. To reproduce with a disposable database and the source probe, add --logminer --lob-evidence --lob-preflight and supply the JAR and Oracle JDBC driver. When preflight refuses a table, check the selected owner, table and LOB storage with the database administrator. Keep the durable SCN and its archives when investigating an existing job. If that table must migrate, arrange a separate LOB-capable migration and verify the contents before cutover. LOB locators and fragments alone cannot serve as full values, and empty LOBs have a different meaning from SQL NULL. Character data and padding The Oracle source profile admits VARCHAR2 with byte or character length semantics. It also admits CHAR when the PDB database charset is AL32UTF8 , and NVARCHAR2 and NCHAR when the PDB additionally uses AL16UTF16 as its national charset. The three added types must be declared with at most 4,000 bytes in the Oracle dictionary. Preflight reports ORACLE CHARACTER CHARSET UNSUPPORTED or ORACLE CHARACTER STORAGE UNSUPPORTED when these checks fail. The PostgreSQL target stores the source character values in variable-length text, including the padding supplied by Oracle. Oracle character types Oracle Free 26ai 23.26.4.0.0 preserved supplementary characters, combining code points, quotes and trailing spaces in the tested Flashback and archived transactions. Empty character input became SQL NULL. Oracle padded CHAR(8 CHAR) by characters and NCHAR(8) by UTF-16 code units. LogMiner emitted escaped UNISTR literals for the national character rows and column extraction matched Flashback across 60 required images. Capture validates Unicode escapes and paired surrogates without executing the generated SQL. Oracle nulls · Oracle UNISTR The restart acceptance used two PostgreSQL 17.12 subscriptions. Each kept its original snapshots and matched Oracle Flashback byte for byte through archived inserts, updates, SQL NULL assignments and keyed or keyless deletes. The Controller and Worker were forcibly stopped before the last two transactions. Reproduce archive and Flashback checks with tests/oracle-source-probe.py --logminer --character-evidence , Temurin 21 and the Oracle JDBC driver. Run the independent dual-subscription restart fixture with --logminer --pipeline --character-pipeline . Native binary JSON The Oracle SQL JSON type stores OSON. Rivomesh preflight returns ORACLE REDO COLUMN TYPE UNSUPPORTED for a selected table with that type. In a disposable Oracle Free 26ai 23.26.4.0.0 PDB, enabling all-column supplemental logging succeeded, but traditional LogMiner returned 24 native JSON table records with status 2 and Unsupported in both SQL image fields. Four transactions covered keyed and keyless inserts, whole-document updates, path updates and deletes. LogMiner decoded each regular VARCHAR2 marker, and both reads of the closed archive returned identical records. Oracle JSON data type · Oracle LogMiner supported types The local PDB LogMiner session recovered all four scalar control values. For the 24 native JSON records, COLUMN PRESENT reported zero for both images and MINE VALUE returned SQL NULL. Those results indicate absent images. Flashback JDBC could still read the full documents, distinguish SQL NULL from JSON null and preserve typed date and binary scalars with OracleJsonValue . On the tested driver, getBytes() on the native JSON column returned UTF-8 JSON text. The diagnostic uses tests/oracle-source-probe.py --logminer --native-json-evidence with a Temurin 21 runtime and the Oracle JDBC driver. Oracle LogMiner column extraction · Oracle JDBC JSON value types Textual JSON columns An Oracle VARCHAR2 column declared with up to 4,000 bytes maps to PostgreSQL jsonb when an enabled, validated, nondeferrable CHECK tests that single column for strict JSON and unique object keys. The check can be declared at column or table level. Other VARCHAR2 columns retain their string mapping. Oracle SQL/JSON constraints Keep both modifiers inside the same parentheses. Oracle Free 23.26.4 returns ORA-02252 for the split form IS JSON (STRICT) WITH UNIQUE KEYS in a CHECK . Both Flashback and archived capture verify strict syntax, one complete JSON value and unique object keys. SQL NULL remains distinct from JSON null . PostgreSQL jsonb preserves the value and may change whitespace, member order and numeric formatting. Preflight returns ORACLE TEXT JSON PRIMARY KEY UNSUPPORTED for a textual JSON primary key because distinct source strings can become equivalent target keys. Values outside either database's JSON representation use its usual error and recovery flow. PostgreSQL JSON types Adding or removing this constraint on a synchronized column changes its target type mapping. Review the destination schema and existing data before resuming capture through the DDL recovery workflow. Oracle returns ORA-40664 if the column already has an IS JSON constraint. Replace the existing constraint during the reviewed schema migration. Oracle ORA-40664 Oracle DATE in PostgreSQL Oracle DATE maps to PostgreSQL timestamp(6) without time zone and preserves the date, hours, minutes, seconds and SQL NULL . Capture sets the Gregorian calendar and American date language on its own Oracle sessions. PostgreSQL reads and writes use LocalDateTime so the Worker time zone does not move a valid Oracle wall-clock time during a daylight-saving transition. An existing destination column must also use timestamp without time zone . Oracle DATE storage · Oracle format models · PostgreSQL JDBC date and time types The profile accepts dates from 1582-10-15 through 9999-12-31. A value before that range, including BCE, raises ORACLE DATE VALUE OUT OF RANGE when its era and format can be decoded. Unexpected LogMiner date masks raise ORACLE DATE FORMAT UNSUPPORTED . Inspect the source values, the affected table and the durable position before retrying an interrupted run. Oracle's TIMESTAMP variants require a separate profile. Run tests/oracle-source-probe.py --logminer --pipeline with the frozen JAR and Oracle JDBC arguments to reproduce the temporary real databases and actual SIGKILL/restart. Add --text-json for strict textual JSON or --date-values for Oracle DATE, covering Flashback, archived CDC and recovery for both keyed and keyless tables. Evidence Integer virtual columns For Oracle 26ai, select Sync supported integer virtual columns in the Oracle source form or set source.oracle.allowVirtualNumericColumns: true in the V3 YAML. Check the task before starting. The profile accepts three expressions for virtual NUMBER(p,0) columns. Multiply one physical integer column by a literal integer from 1 to 999, add two physical integer columns, or subtract one physical integer column from another. Each operand and output needs an explicit precision of at most 18. The output precision must hold the entire declared operand ranges. With AMOUNT NUMBER(12) and ADJUSTMENT NUMBER(12) , for example, TOTAL NUMBER(16,0) GENERATED ALWAYS AS (AMOUNT + ADJUSTMENT) VIRTUAL fits this profile. Virtual primary keys, function expressions and decimal operands require a separate profile. Oracle column expressions The Worker reads the original Flashback value and verifies it against the same arithmetic used on archived physical operands. PostgreSQL receives a regular numeric column containing that value. Redo and undo generate separate before and after images, so repeated writes within one transaction and keyless duplicate rows keep their original values and multiplicity. A SQL NULL in either operand produces a SQL NULL result. Enable the setting when creating the journal. It changes the source fingerprint. An existing task needs a separately reviewed schema and checkpoint migration before it can adopt this profile. Run tests/oracle-source-probe.py --logminer --pipeline --virtual-columns --startup-timeout 480 with the frozen application and Oracle JDBC arguments. The fixture checks old and new outputs, keyless duplicates, restart from the same snapshot IDs and unsupported expression refusal. Use --virtual-evidence for the separate dictionary, Flashback and archived operand inspection. Verification evidence Oracle virtual column feasibility Oracle Free 26ai 23.26.4.0.0 exposed the virtual NUMBER definition "AMOUNT" 2 without a physical segment column. A native Flashback read returned the original generated values and duplicate multiplicity at one SCN. The archived redo and undo contained the physical operands for two successive updates of the same row, a SQL NULL insert and a keyless delete. They omitted the generated value. The independent COLUMN PRESENT probe returned ORA-00904 for the qualified operand, so its presence flags are unavailable. That feasibility run established which operand images are available in native archives. Use tests/oracle-source-probe.py --logminer --virtual-evidence --startup-timeout 480 with the frozen application and Oracle JDBC arguments. This profile inspects a disposable native database. Evidence

title: Performance & runtimes
text: Performance measurement and hardware reference 中文：性能测量. Hardware capacity must come from reproducible measurements of a stated workload. No rows/second or recovery-time promise applies independently of CPU, memory, storage latency, network, row width, transaction size, table count, target count, indexes, journal mode and competing workloads. Reproduce the first baseline Build the release before starting the benchmark. Do not rebuild that JAR during a run. Python 3, Docker Compose and the three fixture images are required. On macOS, prefix the Python command with caffeinate -i to prevent idle system sleep; lid closure, manual sleep and other suspension still invalidate timing. For a specified resource envelope: The CPU and database-memory limits apply to each database container; the CPU limit also applies to the worker. Default limits are one CPU and 1 GiB per container, with a 256 MiB Java worker heap and 256 MiB database buffers. They are limits, not reserved or dedicated host resources. Results identify actual image IDs, Docker VM CPU/RAM, container limits, database durability settings, JVM version, workload and release SHA-256. The local journal uses a host bind mount; database files use fixture volumes. Record their physical storage separately. Every run uses a random Compose project and copies the release to target/benchmarks/ run-id /app.jar . It creates only its own source/target, ports remain internal, and cleanup removes only that project's containers/volumes. The copied release, private fixture configuration, bounded logs and report.json remain for review. Failed runs produce status: FAILED ; they must not become capacity reference rows. Inspect containers.log for startup/runtime failures. What the measurements mean Field Meaning --- --- snapshotVisibilitySeconds Worker startup through visibility of all initially loaded target rows; includes JVM startup, discovery and automatic target creation snapshotRowsPerSecond Initial row count divided by that visibility interval sourceMutationSeconds Time to commit updates, deletes and inserts at the source cdcCatchUpSeconds First source mutation through visibility of the final target state; includes source writes cdcChangesPerSecond Number of changed rows, including deleted and inserted rows, divided by that interval afterWritesCatchUpSeconds Observed time between finishing source writes and observing the final target state snapshotContentSha256 , cdcContentSha256 Source and target ordered row streams must match, including IDs, versions and exact payload bytes Transactions are bounded to at most 500 changed rows. Validation streams row bytes rather than collecting the dataset in Python memory. Byte validation runs after each timed phase; a count-only match cannot produce a passing report. The final target contains updated rows, the expected deletes and newly inserted rows. Polling and Docker CLI overhead are included in observation times. This profile is one MySQL 8.4 source, one PostgreSQL 17.12 target, one primary-key table, fixed-width ASCII payload and either journal mode. Source loading warms caches; it is not a cold-storage experiment. It measures neither peak sink throughput nor p95/p99 event latency, durable snapshot-END acknowledgement, failover RTO or steady-state saturation. It does not establish JSON/keyless/large-catalog, multi-target, remote-journal, commercial database or cluster performance. Measured 100,000-row reference One run per journal mode used the same artifact, MySQL 8.4.13, PostgreSQL 17.12 and Temurin 8u512. The Apple M1 Pro ARM64 host had 10 logical CPUs, 16 GiB RAM and Docker Desktop on SSD. Each service was capped at 1 CPU and 1 GiB. The Worker heap and database buffers were 256 MiB each. The workload used 1,024 payload bytes per row, 1,000-row snapshot parts and at most 500 changes per source transaction. Journal Snapshot visibility Snapshot rows/s 120,000 changes visible Changes/s Catch-up after writes --- ---: ---: ---: ---: ---: LOCAL, host bind mount 24.83 s 4,027 53.55 s 2,241 23.13 s EXTERNAL, schema on target PostgreSQL 21.61 s 4,628 46.25 s 2,595 14.04 s Both runs matched source and target content hashes after snapshot and CDC. During diagnosis, a Worker with the same heap exhausted memory while loading an unbounded payload batch. The journal now limits fetched transaction prefixes to 8 MiB and processes an oversized first transaction alone. PostgreSQL also changed from a sequential scan to a primary-key index scan for the benchmark UPDATE when the BIGINT key was bound as BIGINT. Individual transaction limits and large-catalog scaling remain separate measurements. Reports and exact artifact Repeated Temurin 21 capacity reference The Apple M1 Pro ARM64 host had 10 logical CPUs and 16 GiB RAM. Docker Desktop 29.9.2 reported 10 vCPUs and 15.6 GiB RAM. Three independent runs per combination used MySQL 8.4.13, PostgreSQL 17.12, Temurin 21.0.13+9 and the same release artifact. Each of the three containers had 1 GiB RAM and the listed CPU quota. The worker heap was 256 MiB. Both database services used persistent fixture volumes. The LOCAL journal used a host bind mount and EXTERNAL used a separate schema on the destination PostgreSQL instance. Each trial loaded 20,000 rows with a 256-byte payload, then checked 24,000 insert, update and delete changes. Figures show the median and the minimum–maximum range across all three trials. Journal CPUs per container Snapshot rows/s CDC changes/s Catch-up after source writes --- ---: ---: ---: ---: LOCAL 1 1,943 (1,758–2,222) 2,983 (2,133–3,699) 0.27 s (0.26–0.42) LOCAL 2 2,986 (2,442–3,345) 2,962 (2,954–3,000) 0.29 s (0.29–0.36) EXTERNAL 1 2,558 (2,469–2,763) 2,925 (2,784–3,030) 1.00 s (0.88–1.29) EXTERNAL 2 3,143 (1,554–3,382) 3,038 (2,169–3,472) 0.36 s (0.28–0.37) All 12 cases matched exact ordered source and target bytes after both phases. The visibility check includes the expected first and last IDs, because the intermediate update-only state can share the final row count and version sum. The measurements include worker startup for snapshots and source writes for CDC. They apply to this workload and the recorded host. Trial values, image IDs and artifact SHA-256 256 mapped databases and a large transaction On the same artifact, a separate run used 256 MySQL databases in one instance and 256 explicitly mapped PostgreSQL schemas. Each held one keyed table with two rows and an 8,192-byte payload per row. Each container had two CPUs and 1 GiB RAM, the Worker heap was 256 MiB, and the journal was LOCAL. Check Observed --- ---: Start Worker through 256 durable snapshot acknowledgments 25.84 s One source transaction with 768 changes and 8,505,279 binlog bytes through target acknowledgment 4.32 s Restart after SIGKILL and catch up on 256 changes committed while offline 21.42 s Each phase compared all 512 ordered rows from both databases with the generated fixture data. Snapshot identifiers were identical after restart. The fixture uses Python 3.11 or later and Docker Compose. Content hashes and exact fixture resources Slow destination and external journal quota The slow-target profile uses a separate PostgreSQL instance for the external journal. At the default 32 mappings and 8,192 payload bytes per row, each of 24 source transactions updates one keyed row in each schema with full row images. Each of the four services uses the requested CPU quota and 1 GiB RAM. The Worker heap is 256 MiB. After all snapshots are acknowledged, the fixture pauses only the destination. It observes JOURNAL BACKPRESSURE while the journal stays reachable. For at least five seconds, the durable capture offset must stay behind the final source offset, and neither the capture offset nor the destination acknowledgment may advance. Each observation checks that pending transaction, snapshot and identity bytes together fit the logical quota, calculated as 12 × schemas × (payload bytes + 1,024) . The report retains the maximum observed logical size and separately measures total journal relation size. Relation size includes heap, indexes and TOAST, and excludes WAL and other database files. The fixture kills the Worker during the outage, unpauses the destination and starts a fresh Worker process. Recovery must reach the final source offset and target acknowledgment in the original journal generation at a newer epoch. It compares all ordered source and target row bytes and the original snapshot identifiers. The reported recovery time runs from Worker restart through the final acknowledged transaction. On the same Temurin 21 artifact with two CPUs per service, the source committed 768 changes and wrote 12,724,136 binlog bytes. Capture held at sequence 3 and target acknowledgment at 0 for 5.34 seconds over nine observations. The maximum observed logical size was 3,244,602 bytes against a 3,538,944-byte quota. Journal relations occupied 638,976 bytes at the stalled cut. After SIGKILL and restart, the Worker reached acknowledgment 24 and the final source offset in 18.76 seconds. All 64 rows matched, all 32 snapshot identifiers stayed identical, and collection reduced pending logical bytes to zero. Exact artifact, measurements and content hashes Building the hardware standard Keep raw reports and run at least three repetitions for every workload/resource combination. Report medians and ranges; compare identical artifacts, versions, durability, dataset and storage. Record idle and loaded host conditions, disk latency/IOPS, network RTT/bandwidth, utilization and sustained backlog growth. Do not extrapolate linearly from CPU quotas or this small local profile. The broader reference matrix still needs independent physical-host runs, remote targets, row-width/transaction/table-count sweeps, additional targets, sustained soak and consumer backpressure. The slow-target result covers one separately journaled SQL target with the stated quota and workload. Harness validation scope The earlier process and journal runs retain their tested artifacts, runtimes and scope. Current candidate measurements use Eclipse Temurin 21 LTS. Compare capacity only with the recorded host, workload and storage. Verification baseline · Fixed historical snapshot Runtime and journal profiles The benchmark uses Temurin 21. --journal-mode LOCAL EXTERNAL defaults to LOCAL. The EXTERNAL profile uses a separate journal schema on the same PostgreSQL instance as the target, so journal and sink compete for that container's resources. It is not a remote dedicated journal benchmark. For example: Selecting a runtime is not a compatibility claim. Inspect a passing raw report and actual JVM version. This SQL profile can establish only MySQL-source/PostgreSQL-target snapshot/CDC coverage on that runtime; messaging/security/failover and other drivers need separate runtime acceptance. To compare CPU quotas with both journal modes on one Temurin 21 artifact, run independent trials sequentially: The matrix retains progress, per-trial logs and links to each raw benchmark report in target/runtime-matrix/ id / . Each trial uses fresh services. A passing trial requires source and target byte checks, the observed journal backend, successful cleanup, the expected JVM version, the same artifact SHA-256 and the requested CPU quota on all three containers. The matrix continues after a failed trial and reports the median and range only for combinations whose trials all pass. Changing the artifact aborts the matrix. Run it without competing workloads or a concurrent release build to make comparisons reproducible.
