Transaction boundaries Operation Contents committed in one destination transaction --- --- Create task Configuration fingerprint, B0, table manifest, scan upper bounds and discovery watermark Snapshot chunk Business rows, cursor, row count, completion state and read-dependency GTIDs Capture commit Complete ordered row events, origin, GTID, capture/required sets Apply commit All row changes, applied sequence, phase changes and queue deletion Record failure Error history, shared run state, safe context and owner release An uncertain commit ends the current work session. The new session rereads persistent progress instead of reusing an old in-memory cursor/GTID. Business tables, queues and state tables must be backed up/restored as one recovery unit. SQL errors and shared pause Connection/serialization SQL states 08/40, lock waits and recoverable resource failures retry with backoff. Data, constraints, permissions and syntax errors pause. Safe error context includes table, source GTID, queued transaction sequence, SQLState and vendor code; row payloads and SQL literals are excluded. A failed destination transaction rolls back completely and retains the queue head. Capture may already have safely persisted later commits; application does not pass the failed transaction. PAUSED is shared database state: restarting or adding standby processes cannot bypass it. Repair the cause, then resume the original transaction. Resume does not skip rows, alter GTIDs or empty queues. Database operators repair source replication SQL errors. The service does not execute SQL SLAVE SKIP COUNTER, inject empty GTIDs or RESET. A failed replica does not interrupt capture from a healthy primary; promotion of that unhealthy replica is rejected until repaired and caught up. V1 file-position tasks lack complete GTIDs and read dependencies. Automatic in-place upgrade is refused and old state is preserved. Consult validation for accepted versions and fault profiles; current-format transactional SQL targets have separate reviewed recovery profiles. Configuration-format migration and automated business cutover remain open.

title: Release packages & driver inventory
text: Release inventory and Apache preparation 中文 Build the release candidate with Eclipse Temurin 21 LTS, then generate the dependency inventory from the repository root. This produces one CycloneDX Maven SBOM and a comparison against the actual shaded JAR. CycloneDX Maven plugin The comparison binds the exact JAR and Maven BOM by SHA-256. The outer Maven fields describe the outer JAR. packagedComponentEvidence adds component locations and the hashes of the identifying entries or JARs. embeddedNestedJars lists each nested JAR, its coordinates and license files. Examine packagedCoordinatesOutsideMavenBom and unidentifiedNestedJars when reviewing the complete binary contents. The scan reads Maven properties inside the Hive SDK, identifies the three packaged Bouncy Castle 1.86 JARs by their published Maven Central SHA-256 digests, and reads Kafka build properties when the client class is present. In the external-vendor candidate at SHA-256 02906330f9cc73efa8e4516ef3838f3ee3607a12f943e0352664a8db5711b5f3 , it finds 151 packaged coordinates against the 175-component Maven BOM, including 46 absent from that BOM. The requiredComponentReviews map includes the newly identified components. An empty license list requires upstream evidence, and unidentified contents still require manual review. Oracle source preflight uses an operator-provided driver. Hive JDBC build · Bouncy Castle downloads · Kafka build properties The normal Temurin 21 JAR from 6491ea3 has SHA-256 33c95ba4ab9c39ed98a7d6cba377fa236aa493a4846019c04cb2d3d8ea7d585c . Its CycloneDX 1.6 Maven BOM has 175 components and SHA-256 5af703c8df65db5544097f32c233934fb51043084f1a42dd4263e17ceaac8492 . The scan identifies 155 packaged coordinates, including 48 absent from the Maven BOM, and 21 outer license or notice files. Of 151 component reviews required for this JAR, 50 have no declared license in the Maven BOM and need separate evidence. The source preserves exact upstream GaussDB and GBase8c notices under META-INF/rivomesh-licenses/ . The inventory checks these against the corresponding upstream bytes when it finds the driver marker. ASF distribution review The development JAR bundles MySQL Connector/J 8.4.0 Community under GPLv2 with the Universal FOSS Exception. The current ASF Category X policy covers GPL and exceptions it does not specifically allow. The review check reports BUNDLED MYSQL CONNECTOR J while this driver is present. Apache Flink CDC documents a separate operator-installed driver. Rivomesh's external JDBC candidate follows that packaging pattern and still needs ASF review of its integration model and all other distributed components. Connector/J 8.4.0 license · ASF third-party license policy · Flink CDC MySQL documentation Candidate with an external MySQL JDBC driver Build the distinct JAR and check its contents against the aggregate Maven BOM. The external profile excludes Connector/J from this JAR, including its service provider and bundled notices. The Maven BOM still describes build dependencies. Review mavenComponentsWithoutEmbeddedCoordinates alongside the binary inventory to distinguish the remaining build components from packaged components. --expect-external-mysql checks the candidate and its nested JARs. The binlog reader remains packaged separately from the JDBC driver. On a manual installation, obtain a supported Connector/J JAR separately under its applicable terms. Provide the driver from an operator-controlled file wherever the configuration uses a MySQL-protocol JDBC connection, including the source, a target or the control database. Launch with the explicit classpath and main class. An execution Agent uses agent in place of serve and inherits the same JDBC classpath into its Workers. For a systemd service that uses this candidate, set its ExecStart to the classpath command with absolute paths. The repository's standard Docker build continues to package the development JAR. Check a MySQL pipeline using the same classpath and check with its pipeline configuration. JDBC DRIVER UNAVAILABLE indicates that the JVM could not load the driver class. Verify the operator JAR path and the process's read permissions. Run a disposable MySQL 8.4 acceptance profile to exercise the external JAR through Controllers, an Agent and its Worker. This uses the MySQL control store, PostgreSQL and MySQL targets, and a rolling restart. Candidate with external vendor JDBC drivers Build the external-vendor-jdbc profile on its own. The resulting application JAR keeps the binlog reader, PostgreSQL and H2 drivers. It excludes MySQL Connector/J, the GaussDB and GBase8c wrappers, Kingbase and Dameng JDBC. The separate external-mysql-jdbc profile continues to bundle the four target connectors. Maven's build BOM still includes dependencies used to build and test the application, and the reactor may produce driver JARs separately. Maven Shade artifact selection The inventory scans the candidate and nested JARs for known classes, JDBC service providers, Maven metadata and identifiable upstream notices. The external profile check covers the binary application candidate. Source archives and deployment images have their own contents and review evidence. Supply only the driver files needed by a deployment, from locations controlled by the operator. For GaussDB or openGauss, use the project's separately built relocated GaussDB wrapper for the supported profile. Its class name lets it coexist with the bundled PostgreSQL driver. GBase8c can use the verified upstream gbase8c-jdbc-3.0.0B02.jar . The existing checked Kingbase and Dameng versions are kingbase8-9.0.1.jar and DmJdbcDriver18-8.1.3.140.jar . Use the same launch classpath for the Agent or standalone pipeline. The Agent passes that classpath to its Workers. The offline acceptance checks the exact application JAR with an empty vendor classpath and again with all five operator files. It checks class origins, URL matching, the typed missing-driver error and the Dameng error classification. The native Dameng profile uses this same candidate with only the external Connector/J and Dameng driver files on the operator classpath. It verified actual authentication and driver origins, missing-driver refusal, Dameng error handling and reconnect after a database restart. Dameng native reproduction The native Kingbase target profile runs the candidate with only its external Kingbase JDBC JAR. It exercises actual authentication and class origin, then verifies native transaction receipts and replay through the same endpoint after an outage. Kingbase native reproduction Contents review of the external vendor candidate The external-vendor JAR at SHA-256 02906330f9cc73efa8e4516ef3838f3ee3607a12f943e0352664a8db5711b5f3 has 105 outer Maven coordinates against its 175-component BOM at SHA-256 0eb72993c39c1c048ac9739dbb6410e39ea93e162a420eb39f6af6ecb2390e89 . Its four outer BOM differences are Logback Classic and Core 1.3.5, the RocketMQ Logback extensions 1.0.1, and JCTools Core 4.0.5. Logback 1.3.5 publishes alternative EPL 1.0 and LGPL 2.1 terms. The extensions and JCTools publish Apache 2.0 terms for their own code. Review Logback separately from the extension, including the selected terms, the relocated classes and the applicable binary notice conditions. Logback 1.3.5 · RocketMQ logging · JCTools 4.0.5 · ASF third-party policy The same candidate embeds a Hive JDBC 4.0.1 standalone JAR with 44 Maven coordinates, 42 of which are absent from both the outer Maven metadata and the aggregate BOM. Inspect that JAR's contents and notices independently. Three separately nested Bouncy Castle 1.86 JARs expose their versions in bundle manifests and carry their own MIT license files. Use their payload hashes and manifests to associate the packaged files with the corresponding BOM entries. Hive JDBC 4.0.1 build · Bouncy Castle license The outer NOTICE matches Kafka Clients 3.9.2 byte for byte. Its META-INF/NOTICE matches ActiveMQ Classic Client 5.16.8. Kafka's version marker and a consumer class also match its upstream JAR. The scanner uses the version marker to include Kafka in requiredComponentReviews . The normal build also contains the Connector/J licensing manual at LICENSE and a copy of the GBase8c upstream license at META-INF/LICENSE . The report's outerPackageDocumentDependencyMatches records each recognized match with the exact package path, SHA-256, upstream component and upstream path. A match identifies the reference bytes. Standard license templates can appear in multiple artifacts and are outside this matching rule. ASF licensing documentation Prepare package documents from separately reviewed files After the rights holders provide the reviewed LICENSE and NOTICE files, use the opt-in Python 3 step on Linux or macOS to prepare a separate JAR from the exact shaded build. Obtain the three SHA-256 values from the build and review records. Use a new output filename in an existing directory without symbolic links on a filesystem that supports hard links. The ordinary Maven profiles remain available without these materials. The step copies the reviewed bytes to both root paths and both META-INF paths. It refuses missing or mismatched inputs, known dependency documents supplied as project documents, signed outer JARs, duplicate outer entries and existing outputs. The JAR manifest and the content and compression methods of the other entries are preserved. Any original files in the four paths are preserved under META-INF/rivomesh-licenses/ . META-INF/rivomesh-release-documents.json records their old and new paths and hashes, along with verified upstream references when available. Use the prepared JAR and its new SHA-256 for the package inventory and candidate tests. Document preparation assembles the supplied files. Review the rights, dependency terms and actual distribution independently with the gate below. Distribution review record Run the inventory with --asf-review target/candidate/distribution-review.json to check an exact JAR against a completed manual review. Use the following fields in that record. Field Review evidence --- --- formatVersion Integer 1 artifactSha256 , mavenBomSha256 Corresponding SHA-256 values from this candidate's inventory sourceRightsEvidence Reference to the source provenance, rights and contribution review packagedContentsEvidence Reference to the review of the exact package, including nested or shaded dependencies, native libraries, notices and other assets packageLicenseFiles Object mapping META-INF/LICENSE and META-INF/NOTICE to their reviewed SHA-256 values in the JAR componentReviews Object keyed exactly by requiredComponentReviews . Each value has a license string for the selected terms and an evidence string for the corresponding review record With --asf-review , the inventory writes ASF DISTRIBUTION REVIEW BLOCKED and exits with code 1 on an incomplete record, digest mismatch, missing package licensing file, missing or changed vendor notice, bundled Connector/J, or an unidentified nested JAR. PACKAGE DOCUMENT MATCHES DEPENDENCY also blocks a known individual dependency document at the JAR root or at META-INF/LICENSE or META-INF/NOTICE , even with a complete review record. A copy in a dedicated dependency attribution location remains available for review. UNIDENTIFIED NESTED JAR includes the full nested location and the JAR's SHA-256. Run the inventory without --asf-review to collect these findings and identify the component from verifiable metadata or its published binary digest. ASF DISTRIBUTION REVIEW RECORDED confirms the record matches the inspected JAR and that the scanner found no known blocker. Reviewers determine the applicable terms and verify all content. Repeat the review for each source archive, binary and image that will be distributed. ASF distribution licensing requirements The source tree still needs project-level LICENSE and NOTICE files after review by the rights holders. Record the contribution rights and provenance of code, assets and vendor components before preparing those files. Verify that the exact JAR carries the resulting package-level documents and the required dependency attributions. For a new podling, follow the initial codebase process in the Incubator's podling IP guide. Podling IP clearance Use the project name Rivomesh and namespace io.github.rivomesh during preparation. The ASF proposal, naming and branding guides define the later review and adoption process. Proposal guide · Name search · Branding Candidate functionality gate Keep an immutable copy of the candidate JAR and pass it to the Chrome, native CDC, and Kubernetes fixtures. Set --artifact-sha256 on the Kubernetes fixture to verify the JAR inside both running workloads. Pass the exact candidate and each generated manifest to the gate. The gate also checks acceptance evidence, local links, bilingual API and connector coverage, packaged resources, and all shipped YAML examples using synthetic credentials. --examples-only runs these checks by themselves. The full command requires a real browser, successful native recovery with separate Agents, and both live Kubernetes deployment profiles on the same artifact. Record separate native results for each additional adapter or deployment profile on the verification baseline. Record the distribution review separately using the same candidate digest.

title: Rename migration
text: Rivomesh rename and existing-task migration Updated: 2026-11-17. 中文：更名迁移. The Java base package and Maven groupId are now io.github.rivomesh . Entry points, reflective loading, relocated drivers, tests and deployment scripts use that namespace. Rebuild every module; do not reuse transport SDK JARs or compiled directories from the previous namespace. The initial public repository is <https://github.com/rivomesh/rivomesh . Historical scripts, source manifests, logs and checksums under docs/verification/ retain their original package names and belong to their historical candidates. They do not certify the renamed build. See implementation status for current recovery evidence and outstanding compatibility profiles. This change migrates project identity/build references without changing replication algorithms, v2 state formats, configuration fingerprints, or SQL-error handling. Names Object New value --- --- Project / root Maven artifactId Rivomesh / rivomesh Directory rivomesh , alongside canal Maven groupId / Java base package io.github.rivomesh Executable artifactId / entry point rivomesh-app / io.github.rivomesh.Main Relocated driver artifactId / JDBC class rivomesh-gaussdb-driver / io.github.rivomesh.gaussdb.jdbc.Driver Source module directories Retain sync-app and gaussdb-driver ; directory names need not equal artifactIds Technical naming does not establish domain/trademark ownership or Apache acceptance; review separately before public release. Existing installations 1. Stop every old service node for the task; do not mix driver-package versions on one task. 2. Back up configuration and business/management data as one recovery unit. Preserve jobId, logical clusterId, source database, target URL/schema, and metadata schema. Never delete state or clear business tables for a rename. 3. Change any explicit target driver to io.github.rivomesh.gaussdb.jdbc.Driver ; omitting it selects the new default. Do not substitute the test PostgreSQL driver for the relocated Gauss driver. 4. Update working directories, classpaths, JAR paths, monitoring/log references to sync-app/target/rivomesh-app-0.1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar . Recompile custom code using renamed entry/model classes. 5. Run check/status, verify existing state, then run. PAUSED remains paused; repair and resume rather than bypassing errors through renaming. Moving the root does not update external file contents. Check relative paths against the new working directory. Private local.yml is not rewritten automatically; repository examples/defaults are updated. Recovery boundary The rename introduces no multi-source/multi-target/new-journal state format. Those changes require separate migrations, compatibility checks, and rollback plans; package changes alone cannot make incompatible checkpoints reusable. See README and validation for current operation, and platform design for planned capabilities.

title: Security audit
text: Security audit, retention and export 中文：安全审计. This records management API/controller events separately from the 40-operation task history and configuration revisions. Scope and permissions Only ADMIN can read/export or open Security audit . VIEWER/OPERATOR attempts are denied and audited. API requests record HTTP BEGIN / HTTP END : authenticated actor/role, fixed route category, known task ID, direct peer IP, HTTP status and safe error code. Authentication failures have no actor and status 401; authorization/Origin denials record 403. Health probes/static files are excluded. Raw URLs/queries, Authorization, bodies, credentials, rows and exception text are excluded. Client request IDs are SHA-256 hashes for correlation, not raw arbitrary headers. Forwarded IP headers are not trusted. HTTP END means response prepared, not delivered. A 202 is not successful execution. OPERATION COMMITTED records durable PENDING and SUCCEEDED/FAILED outcomes, actor and operation-request hash; configuration edit/restore outcomes are included. Startup/orderly shutdown have separate events. Internal calls without HTTP attribution and older history are not assigned invented identities. CLI replication, business SQL and OS activity are outside this controller audit. Durability and failures dataDirectory/audit/events.mv.db uses H2 transactions, synchronous writes, contiguous sequences and a SHA-256 chain. The private audit directory is 0700 and database 0600 where POSIX permissions exist; protect other platforms with ACLs. Startup verifies the retained chain/tail. The controller registry binds the audit store identity: deleting/replacing it with a new empty database refuses startup. Stop the controller and coherently back up registry, audit, configuration revisions and journals; copying a live H2 file is not a consistent backup. An API begin event must persist before the request executes. Failure returns 503 AUDIT UNAVAILABLE , preventing that HTTP management action. Already accepted asynchronous results commit an outbox entry with controller state, then append the event. A crash between append and outbox removal replays by event ID without duplication. If completion was committed but audit/outbox cleanup failed, the operation may have happened: inspect/replay its original request ID and revision, rather than blindly submitting a new request. A BEGIN without an END means the result needs investigation. Audit failures do not terminate independent replication workers. Management requests are blocked while process probes can remain healthy. Repair private volume capacity/permissions; restore coherent backups for chain corruption or identity mismatch. Never erase audit files to bypass verification. Retention auditMaxEvents defaults to 1000000, range 1000–10000000. Set it in Linux/Docker platform YAML, Helm --set platform.auditMaxEvents=2000000 , or the native ConfigMap, followed by a controlled restart. The UI/API expose the limit and pruning anchor. Each new-event transaction prunes the old prefix while retaining anchorSequence/anchorHash ; the remaining history never pretends to start at zero. This count is not a physical disk byte quota: monitor H2/backup storage. Status polling also generates events; choose retention from measured request volume. Pages use fixed after/through bounds, oldest first, 100 by default, maximum 1000. after=0 selects the current retained beginning; through=0 fixes the current head. Continue with next and the same through . A cursor overtaken by retention receives 409 AUDIT HISTORY EXPIRED , never silent data omission; invalid rollback/range changes receive409 AUDIT HISTORY CHANGED . Console and exports ADMIN opens Security audit , reviews sequence/time/identity/route/task/result and uses Next page . Refresh retained window starts a new window. Export this page downloads only the current 100 events and proofs, not all history; changed boundaries prevent download. Close/sign-out clears records and fences late responses. For a full streaming export, use a management machine with Python 3 and an environment-supplied ADMIN token: The full exporter fixes one tail, verifies sequence/chain/store identity/tail hash page by page, streams to a 0600 file, writes COMPLETE, then publishes the final filename. Memory is bounded by page size. Existing outputs are never overwritten and HTTP redirects are refused. Failures/expired retention leave .partial , without a successful final file; export to a new path. Events generated during export lie beyond its fixed tail. Successful single-page verification with non-null continuation proves that page, not full-history completeness. Verify against an independently retained checkpoint From a trusted administrative export, record the verified audit-store ID, last sequence and SHA-256 chain hash. The checkpoint file contains these four fields including the format version. The command writes a new private file after validating the complete JSONL export. Place the checkpoint with a separately controlled audit custodian or in an external archive with retention and access controls. Choose an export cadence that keeps consecutive exported windows overlapping. To verify an export taken after new activity or backup recovery, supply the earlier checkpoint from that independent archive. AUDIT ANCHOR MATCHED confirms that the export contains the trusted sequence and hash for the same store. It can match either an exported event or the boundary immediately before the first event. Retain the newer checkpoint separately after a successful verification. The tool reports AUDIT ANCHOR TAIL ROLLBACK for an older tail, AUDIT ANCHOR HASH MISMATCH for changed history, or AUDIT ANCHOR STORE CHANGED for a different store. If retention advances beyond the trusted sequence, AUDIT ANCHOR OUTSIDE EXPORT WINDOW requires an independently retained intermediate export to establish continuity. Signed checkpoints An independent custodian can sign the checkpoint using OpenSSL. The example uses an existing ECDSA P-256 key on the custodian's machine. Verify the initial export's provenance and store identity before signing the first checkpoint. Keep the private key outside Rivomesh and the checkpoint archive. Preserve the original JSON bytes and detached signature as a pair. OpenSSL signature commands Configure the PEM public key and expected storeId in the verifier's independent trust configuration. Obtain them from the trusted enrollment process. Read the latest trusted checkpoint from custody, then verify a later export using Python 3 and OpenSSL on PATH . Replace your-enrolled-store-id with the actual enrolled ID. AUDIT ANCHOR SIGNATURE VERIFIED confirms signature validation and that the signed checkpoint matched the expected store and verified export. A missing required option, invalid signature, wrong key, changed store, or unavailable verifier fails the command without writing the next checkpoint. Once verification succeeds, the custodian can sign the new checkpoint separately. The signed checkpoint establishes the history hash at its sequence. A later portion of the export gains an independently authenticated hash when the custodian signs a newer checkpoint. Retain signed checkpoints in S3 Object Lock Run tools/audit-retain-s3.py from the custodian's scheduled job after signing the verified export head. The job needs Python 3, OpenSSL, and AWS CLI v2 that supports put-object --if-none-match and head-object --checksum-mode . Configure the enrolled AWS Region, bucket name, 12-digit bucket owner account, audit storeId , and PEM verification key independently of the export. Use a general-purpose AWS S3 bucket with Object Lock enabled and an IAM workload identity. The tool ignores configured custom endpoints. AWS S3 Object Lock Scope the job identity to its archive prefix with s3:PutObject , s3:PutObjectRetention , s3:GetObject , s3:GetObjectVersion , and s3:GetObjectRetention . With SSE-KMS, authorize the job's required KMS operations separately. Apply a bucket policy that requires If-None-Match on archive writes. Restrict deletion, governance bypass, and bucket administration to identities outside the scheduled job. Keep the signing key and AWS credentials outside job arguments, the checkpoint, and the receipt. Conditional-write bucket policies Choose a future UTC retention deadline for each cut and retain that choice with the original signed files for retries. A Linux timer or Kubernetes CronJob can invoke the command for each signed export. The tool checks the export, detached signature, store identity, and exact export head before writing. It uploads one object per store and sequence, with COMPLIANCE retention and a SHA-256 checksum. After a write or a lost response, it confirms the exact S3 version's checksum, lock mode, and retention deadline before printing an AUDIT CHECKPOINT RETAINED JSON receipt. Store the receipt's object key and versionId with the independent archive catalog and alert on a nonzero exit. Retries accept the identical retained pair and sufficient retention. A conflicting body or unverifiable version needs review. S3 conditional writes S3 version metadata For recovery, set RIVOMESH ARCHIVE KEY and RIVOMESH ARCHIVE VERSION to the receipt's key and versionId and retrieve that version. The versioned object is a JSON envelope with formatVersion , checkpoint , and signature . Decode the two Base64 fields to recover the original JSON and detached signature, then use signed-checkpoint verification above. Retain complete audit event windows Add --retain-events to the same retention command to archive the original JSONL export with its signed final checkpoint in one COMPLIANCE object version. Keep the receipt in the independent archive catalog. It records the exclusive starting sequence, the final sequence, the event count, SHA-256 and the exact S3 version ID. Schedule exports before local pruning removes events beyond the last accepted cut. For the first archive, the export must include the initial audit boundary at sequence zero. For later cuts, add --previous-checkpoint /custodian/checkpoints/previous.json --previous-signature /custodian/checkpoints/previous.sig , using the signed head from the last independently accepted full archive. The prior sequence must appear as an event or as the boundary just before the first event. If the export starts after that point, the tool returns AUDIT ANCHOR OUTSIDE EXPORT WINDOW before uploading. Recover an intermediate archived window or an earlier database copy to prove the missing interval. For retries, reuse the exact export and signing artifacts. The first line of the retained object contains the signed checkpoint pair. The remaining bytes are the original JSONL export, including the first boundary and completion marker. Each command spools a private local copy before verifying it and uses bounded memory. The single S3 PUT accepts up to 5 GB per archive and allows ten minutes for the upload. Provision temporary space for the entire object, and choose an export cadence that fits the available disk, uplink and local audit retention. S3 single-upload integrity Recover the cataloged object version with the same get-object command above, saving it as /private/retained-events.jsonl . Use the independently configured key and store ID for offline verification. Supply the preceding checkpoint and signature for a rolling window. Compare the printed checksumSHA256 , fromExclusive , sequence and checkpointHash with the independent receipt. AUDIT EVENT ARCHIVE VERIFIED confirms that the embedded signed head and each event chain link are valid. MinIO acceptance verifies exact version recovery, retention, retry, continuity and tamper detection. Validate the enrolled AWS identity and bucket policies in the deployment. API - GET /api/audit?after=0&through=0&limit=100 : ADMIN pages, events/next/storeId and integrity boundaries. - GET /api/audit/export?... : same range/permissions with JSON attachment headers; the streaming tool continues through this endpoint. Only those three nonnegative integer query parameters are accepted; limit is 1–1000. Reads/exports themselves are audited. Security and acceptance boundaries The local chain and registry detect ordinary corruption, missing rows and replacement by an empty store. Offline comparison relies on independent custody of the latest trusted checkpoint. A signature authenticates checkpoint bytes and can remain valid on an older checkpoint. Keep the latest accepted sequence and enforce archive retention independently. S3 protects each confirmed COMPLIANCE object version until its recorded deadline. Storage policy and custody of the latest trusted sequence remain the operator's responsibility. See the authorization handbook for task grants and verification for tested profiles. Local account changes record ACCOUNT COMMITTED with subjectId and directory version; the UI shows the affected task/account. Directory mutation and audit outbox are saved together, with a separate durable version anchor unaffected by event retention. Legacy export payload/hash bytes are preserved; see accounts.

title: Shared access
text: Shared accounts, sessions and audit 中文：共享身份. Acceptance follows implementation status and candidate evidence. Set cluster.sharedAccess: true consistently before first deployment,following thefirst-release baseline. Shared identity uses one SQL authority;restart recovery remains supported. Existing namespace modes are not automatically migrated. Global tasks additionally require sharedTasks. Bootstrap imports the selected node's verified managed directory or seeds from configured accounts. Existing shared grants are never overwritten by stale deployment tokens. Start the chosen import node first when migrating existing managed identities. Imported non-administrator accounts are restricted to the importing node to preserve their prior local access. The account editor exposes “All nodes” and selected node IDs; an empty selection grants no node access. Administrators can explicitly expand access after reviewing task-ID collisions. API nodeIds: null means all nodes, an array limits nodes, and an omitted field on update preserves the prior grant. Administrator accounts always cover all nodes. Conflicting independent managed directories are not automatically merged; review/export identities and grants before planning adoption. Back up coordinated local control/accounts/audit/configuration/reports and SQL metadata before migration. Local controller state becomes format3 and binds clusterId/shared-store identity. Old software, disabling sharedAccess and missing/wrong authority refuse startup rather than restoring stale local grants. This is the control-state format, not task formatVersion. Rollback requires coordinated backups and review of revoked credentials, not merely an old JAR. Pre-import local audit history retains its original chain/payload. The shared chain records its storeId/last-sequence/hash anchor. New HTTP/account/task-outbox events enter the shared chain; endpoints see the same storeId. pendingOperations currently counts only the responding endpoint local outbox; other nodes pending diagnostics remain future work. Local outboxes drain only after shared confirmation; duplicate IDs are idempotent and payload collisions are rejected. A login at A resumes at B and survives A shutdown/kill/restart. Logout revokes its session globally. Any directory mutation atomically updates revision, revokes all old sessions and writes account audit. Audit failure rolls the transaction back. Every authentication/grant check reads the SQL identity/policy/content marker and audit anchor; matching immutable verified payloads may be reused without offline authentication fallback; outages return503 without local/memory fallback. Session creation checks current revision and expiry uses database time. Bearer and HTTPS/Origin/CSRF rules remain in browser sessions. Members must agree on enabled/Secure/remember policy, idle/absolute expiry, session capacity and audit retention. publicOrigin can differ by direct endpoint; a common HTTPS frontend uses the same external origin. Limits:200accounts,10000task grants per account and4MiB serialized directory. Capacity rejects a change without changing prior state. Sessions share one global maximum. Audit uses auditMaxEvents; non-HTTP idempotency receipts are retained separately without automatic cleanup yet, so monitor disk growth. Retention governance remains LG-09. Organization sign-in with an explicitly bound OIDC identity uses this same session and access authority. Configure organization sign-in Worker credential references An Agent can opt in to a task-scoped environment allowlist in its platform configuration: Provision the named variables in that Agent deployment and reference them in the corresponding task's existing source (including Oracle root and PDB), destination or journal password fields or messaging token field. A task accepts only its assigned names in those fields. The Worker receives only the names actually referenced by that task, plus essential OS variables. Names assigned to another task, references used as a task or node identity and missing values return a typed refusal. Management, control-store and process override variables remain protected. An omitted allowlist keeps the existing deployment behavior. An empty map allows no task environment references. Set and maintain grants on the execution Agent, because the Controller sends the task configuration with unresolved references. Configuration responses show opaque, field-bound retain references in place of credential values and original variable names. Workers run as trusted SDK processes under the installation user. Keep Agent access and private data directories under the corresponding deployment identity. Correlate a remote operation Export the shared audit window from either Controller. Compute SHA-256 of the operation's request ID and match it to clientRequestHash and taskId . In a GLOBAL COMMAND OUTCOME row, subjectId identifies the executing Agent. For a repair, the matching owner OPERATION COMMITTED row carries the repair plan ID as its subjectId . Both records are available in the same shared audit chain. Deployment Enable the field in platform-cluster.yml, keeping independent local directories. Helm has values-shared-access.yaml; native YAML has shared-a / shared-b. Supply dedicated store credentials through Secret. Live Kubernetes/CSI/controller HA remain separate acceptance. Recovery and FAQ - WORKER SECRET REFERENCE DENIED or WORKER SECRET REFERENCE UNSET : check the task ID, credential field, Agent-local grant and provisioned variable. After changing the deployment policy, restart the Agent to load it and retry the task. - Lost all admin tokens: stop one local controller and use the existing access-recover command with a protected configured ADMIN seed. Shared mode updates SQL authority, revokes sessions and audits recovery atomically. Verify and rotate temporary credentials. - SHARED ACCESS QUIESCENCE REQUIRED: stop all old members gracefully; STALE is not confirmed stopped. If isolation is uncertain, plan/verify it before switching, without editing STOPPED records directly. - SHARED ACCESS REQUIRED: restore the bound cluster/sharedAccess configuration; disabling it cannot revive old local tokens. - SHARED ACCESS STATE REQUIRED/IDENTITY CHANGED: restore matching SQL identity/backup/connection settings. Missing authority is never reseeded from stale configuration; do not delete local bindings. - SHARED ACCESS DIRECTORY CONFLICT: back up/export/review the independent directories before adoption/merge; privileges are not silently expanded. - SHARED ACCESS POLICY MISMATCH: align expiry/cookie/capacity/audit settings across members. - ACCOUNT DIRECTORY CAPACITY: review account/grant volume; rejected changes preserve prior state. - Recovery still shows login: check real expiry/logout/directory revocation. Valid shared sessions recover without the failed controller's memory. - Different local/shared audit sequence: they are separate store chains linked by migration anchors/event IDs. Never rewrite/concatenate historical payloads as one chain. - Can old backups restore revoked access: a consistent old backup can contain old grants. External immutable rollback detection remains unfinished; review revocation/rotation after restore.

title: Task authorization
text: Per-task authorization 中文：按任务授权. Complete example: platform-task-scopes.yml. Roles determine actions. users[].taskIds limits the tasks visible/operable by VIEWER and OPERATOR. IDs match exactly: no wildcard, prefix, database or destination-schema matching. Grants may name tasks not loaded yet. - Omitted taskIds , including older configurations, preserves deployment-wide task access, including future tasks. An explicit empty list grants no tasks. Supply the list when access must be restricted. - VIEWER reads; OPERATOR checks/starts/stops/pauses/resumes granted tasks. Neither can create/import, read/edit configuration or read global audit. - ADMIN is deployment-wide and cannot configure taskIds ; global management endpoints are not task-scoped. Keep at least one ADMIN. The compatible authToken is also a global administrator. - Duplicates, wildcards, paths and invalid IDs are rejected. At most 10000 exact grants are accepted; this does not raise the platform task-loading limit. GET /api/tasks returns only granted tasks; UI counts use that filtered list. Scoped accounts do not receive invalid-file listings, since unloaded files cannot reliably be attributed. ADMIN still diagnoses them. Unauthorized and nonexistent task routes both return 404 TASK NOT FOUND . Rejection precedes body parsing, revision changes and actions. A role-forbidden endpoint, such as OPERATOR configuration/audit reads, still returns 403. GET /api/session returns this account's taskScope : an array is exact grants, null is unrestricted. The console shows a grant count and IDs in the identity tooltip. An account without loaded granted tasks gets a dedicated empty-state explanation. Sign-out clears grant/task data. Server checks enforce access independently of the UI. Deployment and revocation Linux/Docker use the configuration above with environment-supplied tokens. HTTP startup takes an immutable snapshot of grants, roles and token digests. Editing the file/Secret does not affect a running service; perform a controlled controller restart. New grants then apply without resetting replication checkpoints. Every request checks the current snapshot; an old request ID does not bypass revoked access. Helm uses deploy/helm/rivomesh/values-task-scopes.yaml with the existing RBAC Secret references. Manual Kubernetes uses deploy/kubernetes/rivomesh-task-scopes.yaml . Choose this instead of default/RBAC manifests, not as extra copies of the same resources. Custom auth.users[].taskIds is an array; empty grants render as [] . Native YAML comes from the same Chart. Restart under an operational plan after changes. Live Kubernetes/CSI acceptance remains pending. Denials enter the global audit for ADMIN review. Local account/grant UI is implemented; see accounts. OIDC/SSO, groups and individual-action grants remain unfinished; private configuration is still administrator-managed. This protects console task access, not database accounts, OS files or cross-deployment tokens, and does not establish multi-replica controller scheduling. Default CONFIG retains startup snapshots. Explicit managed activation makes the durable directory authoritative; restart does not resurrect configured tokens. Changes affect subsequent requests; accepted async operations may continue.

title: Failed transaction compensation
text: Failed transaction compensation 中文 Compensation restores affected destination rows to their states before the next unapplied source transaction. Use it when destination drift prevents that transaction from applying. The initial implementation targets transactional PostgreSQL and MySQL destinations. Enable the existing transaction recovery gate to make preview and approval available to administrators. 1. Pause the whole task and confirm the destination fence. Retain fresh failure evidence and review the target apply phase and original commit state. 2. Choose “Generate compensation preview” in the evidence dialog. The preview shows affected tables, identity counts and row insert and delete counts. Restoring a changed row appears as a deletion followed by an insertion. 3. Under “Transaction recovery and data gaps”, choose “Review compensation plan”, check the scope and provide an approval reason. 4. After the compensation commits, review the destination and explicitly resume. Normal delivery replays the original transaction. A preview covers one destination and one complete transaction with up to 1,000 affected identities. It folds repeated changes, primary key moves and insert/delete chains in source order. For keyless duplicates it uses the retained ROW ID. Point reads use the same JSON, numeric and temporal normalization as reconciliation. Execution checks the reviewed rows and checkpoint again. Generate a fresh preview after drift. Reconcile acknowledgment first when the original transaction has committed. Triggers, foreign keys or unsupported table shapes require separate dependency handling. The connection needs the same dependency visibility as reconciliation repair. Send COMPENSATION PLAN or COMPENSATION EXECUTE to POST /api/tasks/ task /actions . Supply X-Request-ID , expectedRevision , subscriptionId , the subscriber's errorCount , compensation.evidenceId and compensation.evidenceHash . Execute also requires compensation.approvedHash from the preview result and compensation.reason . If the response is lost, inspect operation history or retry with the same request ID and original payload. Rows and the receipt commit together in one destination transaction. The task stays paused. Cross-node cancellation and recovery Open the task from any management entry and select “Request recovery cancellation” under “Transaction recovery and data gaps”. Each button identifies the original compensation preview, compensation write or manual correction write. Administrators can also send RECOVERY CANCEL to the task actions endpoint with the current expectedRevision and the original parentRequestId . Give the cancellation its own X-Request-ID . A successful response acknowledges the request. Check the original operation for the final outcome. Original operation code Action --- --- CANCELLED BEFORE DISPATCH The request was still queued. Inspect the cancellation audit and original request. RECOVERY CANCELLED The preview stopped or the destination confirmed the absence of a commit receipt. Address the original fault before previewing and approving again. RECOVERY CANCEL RESOLVING The Agent is checking the original receipt using a read-only path. Restore destination connectivity and wait for the original outcome. COMPENSATION COMPLETED or CORRECTION COMPLETED The destination committed. Inspect the original receipt for scope, digest and checkpoint. Cancellation and restart preserve the paused state and journal acknowledgment. If a controller goes offline, inspect the original request through another entry. Restart a failed Agent with its original private directory to recover pending requests automatically. Committed rows and the receipt come from the same destination transaction. The Agent reads that receipt under the original request ID. The database rolls back an uncommitted transaction, then the Agent retries the original approval or checks the receipt for an accepted cancellation. Manage gaps and cutover approvals through their own workflows.

title: Controlled transaction skipping
text: Complete-transaction skipping and gap recovery For apply failures caused by target drift, see transaction compensation. The first RC-03 skip and RC-08 gap verification profiles passed with a MySQL 8.4 source, the original Agent and LOCAL journal, a PostgreSQL business target, and PostgreSQL/MySQL control stores. Those archived runs used Java 8. Release builds and deployments use Eclipse Temurin 21 LTS. Native MySQL target contracts passed. Its full public skip matrix and other destinations remain in progress. Shared cluster skip is opt-in. Administrators must retain complete evidence and explicitly approve execution. Evidence · 中文 Gap verification API/UI are integrated,with54 native contracts passing on each of PostgreSQL/MySQL;27 real-CDC checks pass with each PG/MySQL control store. See the operator guide for approval,cancellation and status semantics. Scope and consequences The initial scope is a MySQL source and transactional PostgreSQL/MySQL destinations. The next complete incremental transaction must have retained raw and normalized evidence. Only the synchronization service may write the destination. Schema, snapshot, ownership and dependency checks must pass. Cross-table transactions cannot be split. Snapshot, capture/decode, unknown transaction boundaries and other destination products are excluded. Repair the underlying fault first. Missing binlogs require restored logs, a qualified source or a new baseline;never change GTIDs to simulate success. A proven native APPLY commit requires acknowledgment reconciliation, not skipping. Skipping performs no business DML for that transaction. It records a native SKIPPED receipt and a durable gap for the selected subscriber, then advances only that subscriber acknowledgment. Source logs and other subscriber ACKs are unchanged. Later updates may fail because of missing rows, keyless identities or business dependencies. Continuing replication does not establish data equality. UI workflow 1. Pause the whole task and wait for destination fencing. A paused subscriber alone is insufficient. 2. Retain fresh transaction evidence for the failed destination;review the complete raw/normalized events, source position and scope. Historical observations do not authorize execution. 3. The observation must show CHECKPOINT NOT ADVANCED and TARGET APPLY, with current epoch, error generation and ACK. If no skip form appears, check capability, state and evidence;do not edit metadata to bypass guards. 4. An ADMIN enters an 8–1000-character reason, explicitly accepts the data gap and submits.202 means accepted;inspect the final operation result. 5. Both task and subscriber remain paused. Review the plan and gap, then explicitly resume only after checking subsequent transactions and recovery conditions. Open the original plan after a failed or timed-out operation. FAILED does not prove native absence:the plan may exist or the native skip may already have committed. Plan/native observation Allowed workflow --- --- PREPARED, no inspection Explicit read-only inspection;opening a window does not probe or mutate automatically PREPARED, COMMITTED Recover the committed gap acknowledgment;cannot cancel PREPARED, ABSENT Reapprove with a reason and explicit loss acceptance, or cancel with a reason PREPARED, UNKNOWN No continue, recover or cancel;resolve connectivity, metadata and backup consistency COMPLETED Historical receipt/gap;same-request same-parameter replay returns its result CANCELLED Historical cancellation;new approval requires fresh evidence/error generation Original approval, native execution and later source resolution retain their own actors and reasons. Cancellation requires proven native absence, does not advance ACK or repair the SQL fault, and invalidates the old error generation. Linux, Docker, Helm and manual Kubernetes upgrades Set the following consistently on every original controller and Agent, retaining all other global-control identities, roles, storage and keys: Use thefirst-release baselinefor Linux,Docker,Helm and manual Kubernetes. Control mode is fixed at creation;development-candidate automatic migration is unsupported. The first PREPARED plan atomically upgrades journal data format 3 to 4. The task configuration still uses formatVersion: 3 . The format3-to4 transition is part of the current journal lifecycle,not compatibility for old development programs. Pending plans block normal resume. Missing format 4 plan/gap tables are not recreated as empty history;restore the consistent recovery unit. When preparing the first skip, the journal connection needs permission to create the recovery metadata tables and their collection indexes. Routine restart and status reads use the existing tables. Preserve the indexes with the journal schema when backing it up. Controlled native metadata migration adds a receipt table and two nullable checkpoint markers. MySQL implicit DDL commit does not release the source-journal fence. Appropriate metadata DDL privileges are required. Nontransactional tables and lost native receipts are not silently converted or rebuilt. API POST /api/tasks/ task /actions requires the current revision and X-Request-ID ;cookie writes retain CSRF/Origin requirements. Retry the same request with identical parameters. For SKIP RETRY , SKIP RECOVER or SKIP CANCEL , replace evidence references with planId and planHash . Retry requires acceptDataLoss: true ;recover/cancel explicitly require false . It must be a JSON boolean;strings, numbers, NULL and missing values are not approval. - GET /api/tasks/ task /recovery-plans/ planId :bounded metadata summary, no business-row reads. - POST .../recovery-plans/ planId /inspect with :point-in-time read-only native proof, no DDL/checkpoint advancement. - POST /api/tasks/ task /recovery-plans with "subscriptionId":"pg","after":"","limit":20 . - POST /api/tasks/ task /gaps with "subscriptionId":"pg","after":"0","limit":20 . All ledger reads are ADMIN-only. Pages permit at most 100 entries;use returned next cursors. Sequence/gap cursors are strings and must not be converted to JavaScript floating-point integers. Raw event values remain in separately authorized evidence pages. Oversized source positions are omitted as a whole with a hash;truncated GTIDs are never presented as usable resume positions. The gap page reports journalPayloadRetained when both the raw and normalized payload rows are present in the journal. A false value on an open gap means the journal no longer has both payloads. Use the separately retained evidence archive or a consistent backup in that case. The status does not read business values or attest their content. FAQ Native commit followed by Agent interruption or failed source ACK? Keep the original plan;PREPARED blocks ordinary resume. Restore the original Agent directory and inspect. Only COMMITTED permits acknowledgment recovery. A new unrelated skip request is not recovery. Force-cancel UNKNOWN? Unsupported. Already committed and absent operations require different actions;connectivity failure, missing metadata or inconsistent backups cannot establish either outcome. The original administrator was disabled? Execution rechecks current directory revision and ADMIN authority. Another authorized administrator can explicitly reapprove the original plan;original approver, native executor and source resolver remain separately recorded. When can the journal reclaim the original payload? A live open gap or prepared skip holds the exact transaction until its pin is lifted. After every subscriber acknowledges the sequence and the common-cut verification receipt proves closure of each gap for that sequence, the collector can reclaim its payload. The original skip plan, receipt and gap history remain available. An unrelated later apply or a historical comparison report leaves the pin in place. Does RUNNING mean equality? No. Check hasGaps and the UI warning; gapCountLimited means a bounded count. Replication recovery and data equality are separate facts. Refusal codes? SKIP DISABLED :capability off. SKIP REQUIRES PIPELINE PAUSED :pause the whole task. SKIP RECOVERY PENDING :resolve the original plan. SKIP CHECKPOINT RECONCILIATION REQUIRED :inspect native APPLY first. SKIP NATIVE COMMIT NOT PROVEN :cannot recover. SKIP ALREADY COMMITTED :cannot cancel. SKIP NATIVE CHECKPOINT CHANGED / SKIP PLAN CHANGED :reload and verify the recovery unit.Invalid request fields return 400 REQUEST INVALID without accepting a command.

title: Validation records
text: Verification scope Current status · First-release baseline This entry points to the current baseline rather than repeating build/attempt histories. Separate versions/products/JDK scopes do not establish a complete compatibility matrix. Local regression with Temurin 21 On macOS, the default JVM temporary directory can pass through the /var symbolic link. The recovery tests reject symbolic links in evidence paths. Give the Maven test JVM a temporary directory under the physical project path to exercise the same guard. MySQL 5.7.44 V3 profile The archived Java 8 run used Connector/J 8.4.0 and MySQL 5.7.44 linux/amd64. It passed standalone fan-out, GTID asynchronous promotion and single-primary Group Replication. The checks include keyless duplicates, JSON, supported generated expressions, crash restart, DDL refusal, replica SQL failure and binlog-loss refusal with the checkpoint retained. Restore the missing logs or select an eligible source that still has them before resuming. With the current release JDK, Eclipse Temurin 21 LTS, run tests/matrix.sh --v3 5.7.44 to exercise this MySQL version. See the acceptance record.

title: 恢复与一致性
text: 恢复、主库切换与一致性 本文描述 v2 单 database、单目标核心 ，不是 v3 快照和独立日志协议。English: V2 recovery。已实现的 v3 多库多目标、可选日志、Web 和消息恢复见 V3 手册 与消息手册。完整设计见 完整平台方案（English）。已确认的多库显式映射、同源多目标及独立恢复设计见 需求与决策（English）； 业务次级 UNIQUE/GSI 转普通索引及接管约束恢复见 Gauss 索引策略（English）。剩余适配器、修复和接管范围见实施状态。 同步服务主备 各进程首次启动幂等创建 v2 元数据；并发目录对象创建冲突单独处理，首个任务的配置和表清单原子插入。 工作前通过条件 UPDATE 获取 owner 和租约。独立心跳线程持续续期，数据/进度事务也校验同一 owner。 每次重新建立工作会话都生成新 owner，防止旧复制连接的回调在新会话中继续提交。 同一任务行的锁将采集、全量提交和增量应用的提交顺序串行化。 租约转移后，旧 owner 的业务事务在任何业务写入前就被拒绝；旧节点也不能替新 owner 暂停任务或释放租约。 节点只是备用时不会连接 binlog，同一任务正常只有一个复制客户端。 GTID 状态 - capture gtid：已经进入持久化队列或不影响业务库的已提交源事务，加上首次基线。 - required gtid：capture gtid 与全量扫描已读取状态所依赖的 GTID 的并集。 - applied sequence：已经写入目标业务表的队列事务序号。 源的物理 UUID 和文件位点只用于诊断、连接后端校验，不用于跨服务器恢复定位。 每个源提交事件先完整持久化，才把该事务 GTID 加入 capture gtid；不使用客户端可能提前更新的内存 GTID 直接覆盖状态。 重复 GTID 在持有任务锁时检查，已经持久化的事务不会重复加入队列。 全量期间也允许安全切主 记录基线 B0 后开始采集 FULL 行镜像，并按主键游标扫描业务表。 每次分块读取之后获取源 GTID 水位；分块数据、最后主键和该依赖水位一起提交到目标。 表发现和初始扫描上界读取的结束水位也保存为初始 required gtid。 若全量读取到了旧主库已提交、但采集器尚未持久化的事务，仅检查 capture gtid 会遗漏这一依赖。 因此切换候选必须包含 required gtid，不能只包含已采集事件。 所有分块完成后取结束 GTID B1，等待 capture gtid 覆盖 B1，再按源提交顺序回放队列。 对 B0 后没有变化的记录，扫描负责导入；有变化的记录，由最后一条完整行镜像或 DELETE 决定最终状态。 主键修改按删除旧键、写入新键处理，游标之前的插入及扫描上界之后的记录也由日志补齐。 全量和早期回放期间目标不是某一个时间点的一致性快照。持续增量阶段，每个源事务（包括跨表）在一个目标事务中应用。 主库发现与切换 1. 逐个检查候选地址，读取 UUID、server id、只读标记、GTID 模式、executed/purged 集合及复制状态。 2. 普通主从仅选择可写且没有活动上游线程或残留复制错误的节点。 3. Group Replication 仅选择 ONLINE、PRIMARY、可写、单主模式的节点。 4. 多个可写主库时等待外部高可用系统完成隔离，不能任选一个节点。 5. 要求 required gtid ⊆ candidate.gtid executed ；不满足则等待追平。 6. 要求 candidate.gtid purged ⊆ capture gtid ；不满足说明还有未采集的必要事务已无日志，任务暂停。 7. 新建复制连接使用持久化 GTID auto-positioning，禁用自动回退到 purged 集合。 JDBC 查询会校验物理 UUID 和可写性；复制连接在处理事件前校验握手查询到的 server id。 这也能发现 Router/VIP 在两种连接之间切换了后端，届时退出本次会话，重新发现而不混用数据。 心跳超时、源连接断开和源角色变化会触发新会话，重新读取持久化 GTID。 候选需要由运维保证全量复制、没有业务数据过滤或伪造 GTID，属于同一逻辑复制拓扑。 GTID 一致不等于能检测所有人工修改数据的情况。数据库自身丢失的异步未复制事务，不能由 CDC 重建。 提交边界 操作 一个目标事务内的内容 --- --- 创建任务 配置指纹、B0、表清单、扫描上界、发现水位 全量分块 业务行、游标、行数、完成状态、读取依赖 GTID 捕获源事务 有序完整行事件、来源、GTID、capture/required 集合 应用源事务 全部行修改、applied sequence、阶段变更、队列删除 记录故障 错误历史、共享 run state、最近错误上下文、释放 owner 提交响应不确定时退出本次会话，不复用旧内存游标或 GTID；新会话读取目标数据库的持久化记录。 数据表、队列和状态表必须作为同一个恢复单元备份和恢复。 SQL 错误与暂停 SQLState 08/40、锁等待和可恢复资源错误退避重试；数据、约束、权限和语法错误暂停。 错误记录保留表、源 GTID、队列事务序号、SQLState 和 vendor code，不记录行载荷或 SQL 字面量。 目标事务失败整体回滚，队列头不删除；采集端可能已把其他事务安全存入队列，这不会使应用越过错误。 PAUSED 是数据库中的共享状态，重启进程或新增备用节点不会绕过它。 修复数据类型、权限或约束后执行 resume，只重试原事务，不跳过、更改 GTID 或清空队列。 源复制 SQL 错误由数据库运维修复；服务不会自动执行 SQL SLAVE SKIP COUNTER、注入空 GTID 或 RESET。 正常主库可用时，故障从库不影响当前采集；故障从库被提升时会拒绝其接管，等待修复。 v1 文件位点任务缺少完整 GTID 和读取依赖，不能直接自动升级；新版本会保留旧状态并明确拒绝同名旧任务。

title: 验证记录汇总
text: 验证范围 当前实施状态 · 首版验证基线 本页统一指向当前基线，不再重复记录逐次构建、失败尝试和旧发布候选。不同版本/产品/JDK的记录不能合并为全矩阵通过。 Temurin 21 本地回归 macOS 默认 JVM 临时目录可能经过 /var 符号链接。恢复测试会拒绝证据路径内的符号链接。运行回归时，把 Maven 测试 JVM 的临时目录设为项目下的物理路径，保留同样的证据路径校验。 MySQL 5.7.44 当前 V3 档案 早期 Java 8 记录使用 Connector/J 8.4.0 和 MySQL 5.7.44 linux/amd64，已通过单机多库多目标、GTID 主从切换和单主组复制。当前复验使用 Eclipse Temurin 21 LTS。覆盖无主键重复行、JSON、支持的生成列表达式、进程强杀续传、DDL 暂停、主从 SQL 错误与日志缺失保护。日志缺失时保留原断点，恢复缺失日志或切换到持有完整日志的合格节点后再恢复。执行 tests/matrix.sh --v3 5.7.44 复验。见验收摘要。

title: 首版验证基线 / Verification baseline
text: 首版验证基线 / First-release verification baseline 仅保留当前基线索引；开发过程中的重复源码/脚本副本、失败尝试和逐次快照已从工作树移除。Git提交历史保留追溯。操作文档见中文实施状态和English。 The compact baseline preserves the exact bounded acceptance provenance. Earlier results are not relabelled as fresh validation of cleanup changes. Current validation status is tracked in baseline.json.
