title: Installation and sign-in
text: Install and sign in Build from the core repository using Eclipse Temurin 21 LTS and Maven, or build the image locally with Docker Compose. Use mvn -version and java -version to confirm the JDK for a local build. Source and deployment commands · Quick start Prepare the environment Use a reachable MySQL source with GTID, ROW logging and FULL row images, an independent empty target, persistent storage, and database accounts with the privileges required by the pipeline manual. Snapshot initialization requires a brief global read lock and appropriate permissions. Start the console Run the documented commands from the quick start. Open http://127.0.0.1:8080 and sign in with your own RIVOMESH TOKEN . Default local settings are for loopback access. Configure HTTPS, Cookie and Origin policies before remote use. Docker Compose builds from source. Use addresses reachable from the container, and retain the named data volume. Docker Desktop can reach host services through host.docker.internal when appropriate. Before sharing the installation 1. Provide an HTTPS entry point and assign individual accounts. 2. Persist task, controller, journal, configuration and report directories. 3. Verify inserts, updates, deletes and restart recovery on a small test pipeline. 4. For several nodes, read multi-node deployment before sharing any storage. Create a task · Deployment reference · Browser sessions Deployment profiles and probes Standalone uses persistent local control data. The default task journal uses H2. An external journal can use PostgreSQL, openGauss or a separate MySQL instance. Shared control profiles have PostgreSQL 17 and MySQL 8.4 records. Keep the control database and journal namespaces and credentials distinct. GET /healthz checks process liveness. GET /readyz can return 503 when a configured control service is unavailable. Check end-to-end replication in the task workspace. The Dockerfile builds and runs on Temurin 21. Native Kubernetes YAML and Helm use a prebuilt image. The live two-node tests cover same-volume remounts, image and configuration replacement, and Secret rotation. Verify cross-node volume availability and additional failure modes separately. See execution lifecycle. Shared control examples use RIVOMESH NODE ID , RIVOMESH CONTROL USERNAME , RIVOMESH CONTROL PASSWORD and, for shared tasks, RIVOMESH TASK KEY . Set the control mode before initialization. See first-release configuration and deployment commands and profiles.

title: Create a synchronization task
text: Create your first synchronization task This walkthrough uses MySQL → PostgreSQL , a small source and an independent empty target. Additional destinations have their own connector profiles. Prepare connection details For MySQL, collect host, port, databases, credentials and a unique replication client serverId . It must differ from database node IDs and other replication clients. For the target, collect host, port, database/schema, credentials and the intended source-to-target mappings. The source must meet snapshot and replication requirements. Target business tables must be empty and exclusively written by this task. Configure and check ScreenshotPreview name="task-wizard" locale="en" alt="Pipeline wizard in the RivoMesh English-language console." / 1. Choose Create task and keep the default multi-database, multi-target format. 2. Assign stable task and logical source identities, then enter MySQL details. 3. Add one PostgreSQL target and explicit mappings for each source database. 4. Select a persistent journal. Local storage is suitable for same-host trials; cross-host continuation requires the external journal profile. 5. Save, check connections and objects, then start. A check does not validate every runtime or snapshot privilege. A saved task remains stopped until started. In optional global mode, select an Agent or use automatic placement on an eligible profile. Check the original command receipt for the execution outcome. Validate the first run Watch snapshot, catch-up and target delivery. Insert, update and delete a test row and compare actual destination values. Restart the worker and confirm it continues from its persisted state. Keep task identity, journals and target state for recovery. Monitoring · Troubleshooting · Pipeline reference See MySQL capture mechanics for the transition from snapshot to CDC and the position used after restart. The architecture diagram shows the responsibilities of each node and store. Configure another capture source - PostgreSQL 17/18. Select PostgreSQL in the V3 wizard. Enter one database, the source schemas, publication and slot prefix. Prepare explicit publication tables with REPLICA IDENTITY FULL , set wal level=logical , and allow for slot capacity and WAL retention. Choose a MySQL or PostgreSQL destination and run the check on the owning Agent. See logical capture configuration. - Oracle 26ai Free. Select Oracle in the V3 wizard. Enter the CDB-root and writable PDB services, PDB name and uppercase OWNER.TABLE entries. Map each owner to a PostgreSQL schema. Supply Oracle JDBC to the runtime that launches the Worker and check Flashback privileges, all-column supplemental logging and archive coverage. See archived capture configuration. For details, see PostgreSQL slots, WAL and LSNs and Oracle snapshots, archives and SCNs. Evaluate a populated PostgreSQL target If MySQL data was already copied into PostgreSQL, use preview-adoption for a read-only comparison of mapped tables. It reports equal, missing, extra and changed rows. Schedule the brief MySQL write gate needed to establish the two read views. When the compared rows match, plan-adoption can prepare a digest for the bounded single-table MySQL 8.4 to PostgreSQL 17 profile. Keep the source frozen and all application and task writers stopped through approval and durable receipt confirmation. The adopted task starts paused. Moving application write authority requires a separate review.

title: Progress and daily operations
text: Read progress and operate tasks Check both the synchronization phase and each target's confirmed position. A running process does not mean all destinations are caught up. ScreenshotPreview name="console-overview" locale="en" alt="Task workspace in the RivoMesh English-language console." / State Meaning --- --- Snapshot Existing data is being read/prepared or delivered; target data may be incomplete Streaming Incremental changes are being handled; lag can still exist Target paused Inspect that target's error and repair the cause before retrying Shared pipeline paused Standby claims are blocked; inspect target isolation confirmation Local worker stopped Only this machine's process is stopped; inspect shared state separately UNKNOWN in global mode The owner or reliable receipt is unavailable; do not infer success or a stopped process Daily checks Watch phase, backlog trends, per-target acknowledgements, SQL errors, connectivity and disk space. Check binlog, WAL or archive retention against the outage and catch-up window. For PostgreSQL, watch disk space used by WAL retained for the logical slot. Journal retention is governed by the slowest destination. Stop, pause or recover - Stop local worker stops only the local process. - Pause shared pipeline blocks ordinary standby claims; unreachable targets still need isolation verification. - Resume this target retries that target's original transaction after its error is fixed. - Resume after repair handles the pipeline-level error; it does not silently clear independent target pauses. Optional fixed-owner global mode routes commands to the execution owner. HTTP 202 means accepted, not finished; inspect the original command receipt. An offline STOP waits until the original owner can recover it. Administrators can review configuration history and restore versions according to identity/state restrictions. Configuration revisions · Global control · Backup Read incremental progress after a skip Coverage counts explicit skips. The contiguous applied watermark stops before the first skipped transaction and stays there after historical verification. For brokers, confirmation covers publication; consumer processing requires its own tracking. See gap verification and watermarks.

title: Troubleshooting
text: Troubleshoot a synchronization task Preserve the error, task identity and persisted state. Fix the cause before retrying; do not reset GTID, checkpoints or queues to bypass an error. Symptom First checks --- --- Console unavailable Service startup logs, bind/port, token/session configuration, HTTPS proxy Source connection fails Container/network address, credentials, GTID, replication privileges and required logs Target SQL pause Exact SQL error, privileges, type mapping, table structure and target identity Backlog grows Slowest target, independent target errors, journal quota and disk headroom Source waits after failover Candidate topology, writable role, required executed/purged GTID history Global command pending/unknown Original request receipt, owner availability, control database and matching private directory/key Temporary connectivity, locking and serialization errors may retry under policy. Deterministic SQL/type/DDL errors need intervention. Recovery retries the original transaction; it does not skip records. If logs or state are lost, restore a coordinated backup or create an explicit rebuild plan. Never delete controller or journal state and reuse a nonempty target as if it were a new task. Recovery rules · Backup and restore · Global control · Report an issue Review a persisted transaction failure For supported transactional PostgreSQL/MySQL profiles, an administrator can retain and inspect failure evidence, check whether the destination already committed, and then choose before-image compensation or typed row corrections. These paths require a whole-task pause, a confirmed destination fence and fresh evidence. Approval keeps the task paused. After checking the result, explicitly resume delivery of the original transaction. Whole-transaction skip is a separate approval that records a durable data gap. Gap verification reviews equality at a common historical cut. It preserves skip history and the contiguous applied watermark. See the first-release gates before enabling these controls. Review a capture failure Open the capture recovery review on the task's failure card. Verify the original checkpoint, source admission and affected destinations. If logs are missing, preserve the journal, coordinates and available source logs. Check GTID and binlog for MySQL, the logical slot, timeline and WAL for PostgreSQL, or the original source identity, SCN and archive coverage for Oracle. If the original checkpoint cannot be recovered, review a replacement baseline and affected destinations. The documented MySQL profile can verify and retain the original binlog transaction. Separate administrator approval can exclude one verified source transaction. The task remains paused, with a recorded gap for its affected destinations. See capture recovery. Review the preceding destination commit The Kafka notice profile enrolls the business Topic UUID before first send. It requires Kafka 4.1 or later with transaction version 2 finalized and Produce v13. Pause the task, review the preceding acknowledgment, and approve the notice for the exact failure. Check sender prerequisites and the control Topic before dispatch. If the response is lost, reuse the request ID to resolve the native receipt. The notice leaves the failed transaction and consumer offsets at their original positions. See messaging targets. ClickHouse, Doris, Hive, ActiveMQ Artemis, ActiveMQ Classic, RocketMQ, Redis Streams, NATS JetStream and Pulsar have scoped read-only predecessor receipt checks. Pause the task and select Check destination receipt on the failed subscription. Keep the complete failed incremental transaction, the preceding acknowledged commit, the original destination and the matching error generation. A match verifies the previous commit. Resolve the failed transaction separately. Classic can still resume an existing task with older receipts. Its next confirmed COMMIT provides the digest required for exact review. Redis Streams reads the saved entry ID, JetStream checks the original stream identity and sequence, and Pulsar reads the saved ledger entry. Keep those records available through review. RabbitMQ relies on retained consumer evidence after acknowledgement. Console, API and CLI receipt review

title: Validate data and review repairs
text: Validate data and review repairs Progress describes how far replication has advanced. Validation compares actual source and target content at a historical common checkpoint; a report does not assert permanent equality afterward. The initial native row validation and repair profile uses a MySQL 8.4 source and MySQL 8.4 / PostgreSQL 17 transactional destinations. Other SQL versions and modes require separate verification. Common-cut validation for experimental PostgreSQL capture is still pending. Create a validation report 1. Finish initialization, run the task and allow the chosen target to catch up. 2. An administrator starts row validation from task details, selecting the target and lock/read/staging budgets. 3. Inspect the operation and completed report for source/target row counts, missing, extra and changed rows. 4. Review task state and explicitly resume when appropriate. Validation does not repair data automatically. Establishing the common checkpoint briefly affects source writes. Raw values may contain sensitive business data and require the appropriate permissions. Find, retain and recover a report In Data validation , browse historical reports or open one by report ID. Reports remain available after they leave recent operations. In global control, administrators can also find recovery receipts by request ID to locate the associated report, failure evidence or plan. The report database contains original business values. Keep it on the Agent's protected persistent volume and include it in task backups. In View storage , administrators can inspect file sizes. Configure validationRetentionMinimumDays to enable approval of a minimum retention period. A report that reaches this date still requires a separate approval and eligibility checks for reclamation. With a separate validationArchiveDirectory mounted, an administrator can seal a checksum-verified copy of a completed report after approving the retention minimum. If the live database is missing, use the report's original ID to restore the sealed copy. See managed validation for limits, receipts and reclamation conditions. Review and execute a repair Keep the task paused, explicitly select targets/tables, generate a plan, and review its scope and budget before execution. Check per-table results and explicitly resume after completion. Unsupported foreign keys, triggers or dependencies can reject a repair. Canceling cannot roll back tables already committed. After an interrupted operation, recover the original request/report/plan and inspect committed results rather than assuming nothing happened. Optional global mode supports cross-entry workflows within its documented fixed-owner acceptance profile; it is not automatic owner migration. Managed validation · Managed repair · Global maintenance Verify a gap after a reviewed skip On the scoped PostgreSQL/MySQL profile, run a fresh complete common-cut comparison after correcting the differences. From its matching report, select gaps and prepare a verification plan for administrator approval and a fresh scan. The receipt covers the reviewed historical cut and leaves the task paused. See data-gap verification. A completed validation report ScreenshotPreview name="data-validation" locale="en" alt="Common-cut validation report from the RivoMesh English-language test console." /

title: Backup and recovery
text: Preserve state for recovery A recovery plan must retain task configuration and identity, journal events and checkpoints, destination business and management state, and private Controller and Agent data. Retain the source logs through the outage and catch-up window. Keep the MySQL binlog and GTID, the PostgreSQL slot, WAL and LSN, or the Oracle archives and SCN for the saved cut. Back up together - Controller state, account/audit data, configuration history, reports and task-specific keys. - Local journal directories or external journal storage, including snapshot artifacts and unacknowledged events. - Target business tables and their atomic checkpoint/receipt state. - Shared control database and original node directories/keys when shared or global mode is enabled. Choose a coordinated backup/restore plan. Restoring a checkpoint alone cannot reconstruct already removed events, and an old consistent backup can reintroduce old permissions that need review. Stop the task and close all connections before copying an H2 journal. For separated deployments, also preserve original Agent directory identity, keys, receipts and private evidence. See first-release operations and capture recovery. Rehearse recovery Stop according to the operation plan, preserve directories/volumes, reopen the original identities and verify snapshot/CDC content and target acknowledgements. For global mode, inspect the original command/report receipt and restore the fixed owner's matching directory and key. An empty directory cannot impersonate that owner. Cross-host continuation uses an external journal. For a global task, use the documented handoff if its original writer was durably frozen before the Agent became unavailable. Otherwise recover the original Agent and its private state. Treat database source promotion and Worker ownership as separate operations. Multi-node guide · Pipeline journal requirements · Recovery reference

title: Accounts and permissions
text: Assign accounts and permissions Use individual identities and grant the least access needed for each role. Role Typical access --- --- VIEWER Read authorized task states and permitted report summaries OPERATOR Perform permitted daily operations within task/node grants ADMIN Manage accounts/configuration and administrative validation/repair workflows The API and UI enforce both roles and task/node scope. If a task or action is absent, inspect grants before changing data or state. Shared access With explicit shared-access configuration, nodes share account authority, sessions and audit. Account changes revoke old sessions. Cookie domains, HTTPS, Origin and session limits still apply across entry points. Optional shared-task mode additionally routes task commands to fixed owners. Shared login alone does not enable global task operations or controller HA. Sign in with an organization account A shared control deployment can use one OpenID Connect provider. Configure the same HTTPS origin across the sign-in Controllers, with authorization code flow and PKCE S256. An administrator binds the exact case-sensitive sub issued for the client to an existing RivoMesh account. The local directory still governs roles, task grants and node grants. Binding, replacing or revoking an identity invalidates browser sessions across entries. Revoke the binding or disable the local account in RivoMesh to stop existing access immediately. Token sign-in and Bearer API access remain available. See the OIDC guide for deployment and troubleshooting. Account management · Task grants · Shared access · Security audit

title: Use cases and evaluation
text: Choose a representative evaluation Begin with a defined business scope and an independent test target, then preserve configuration and measured results for review. Cross-database and heterogeneous integration Replicate MySQL data to supported database targets with explicit database/schema mappings. Review text, NULL values, temporal precision, decimals, JSON, keyless duplicates, generated columns, indexes and constraints. Each product/mode has its own connector profile. Continuously updated analytics Deliver snapshots and changes to ClickHouse, Doris or Hive. Validate update/delete behavior, views and materialization before measuring latency under your workload. These targets do not all use transactional JDBC semantics. Multiple downstream systems Deliver one logical source to independently acknowledged targets. Rehearse a slow or failed destination and plan retained journal capacity. Message consumers must interpret snapshot/transaction boundaries and handle duplicates. Migration and parallel validation Populate an independent environment while preserving the original business database. Review actual values, object differences, restarts and recovery. Application SQL, write cutover, rollback and business constraints require their own plan. For data already copied to PostgreSQL, use the existing target preview to compare keyed tables and review business UNIQUE constraints separately. The bounded MySQL 8.4 to PostgreSQL 17 single-table profile can bind a reviewed adoption plan to the write freeze and a durable receipt. Rehearse application writer preparation, activation and failback before the first committed destination write. For openGauss, DM, KingbaseES, GBase 8c and OceanBase, use the database compatibility guide. Managed row validation/repair has a MySQL/PostgreSQL acceptance profile; do not assume all target profiles support the same maintenance workflow. Performance measurement · Multi-node evaluation · Compatibility boundaries

title: Frequently asked questions
text: Frequently asked questions Where should I start? Read the introduction, then use the quick start with a small MySQL source and an independent empty target. Database administrators should review logging, replication and snapshot privileges. What does V3 in the console mean? It identifies the task configuration format, formatVersion: 3 , for multi-database, multi-target tasks. It is not a database version or a development stage you need to learn. Keep the default for new tasks; changing the number does not migrate an old task's persisted state. Are other capture sources available? Yes. PostgreSQL 17/18 logical replication and Oracle 26ai archived capture have experimental profiles. Check each source’s log, destination and recovery requirements. Can I start with a populated target? Start an ordinary new task with empty business tables. For data already copied to PostgreSQL, run the read-only adoption preview. The bounded single-table adoption flow requires a write freeze, reviewed plan and durable receipt. Does recovery skip failed transactions? No. Fix the cause, then retry the original transaction. Reviewed data repair is a separate workflow with a documented target profile. Is global task control available? Optional global mode provides shared task views and durable commands. Eligible new tasks can select an Agent automatically. Administrators can approve the transfer of a stopped task after preparing and durably freezing the original writer. See multi-node deployment for the supported profiles. Does this website collect database credentials? No. It is a static product/documentation site. Your actual console runs in your own deployment. Local search loads a static document index from this site. Feedback and contribution · Known limitations

title: Multi-node deployment
text: Multi-node deployment and recovery RivoMesh separates shared node observation, shared access and synchronization failover. Task operations are local by default. Optional global mode supports shared task views, durable commands, configuration history and read-only queries. In a separated deployment, eligible new tasks can select an Agent automatically. Transfer of existing tasks follows a separate reviewed handoff. Capability Current scope --- --- Node registry Administrators can inspect nodes, runtime versions, resources, leases and task observations through a shared control database Shared accounts, sessions and audit Explicit cluster.sharedAccess: true ; PostgreSQL 17 / MySQL 8.4 two-node acceptance records include cross-node revocation and restart recovery Synchronization failover Eligible standby workers use an external journal, matching logical task and target settings, distinct node IDs, leases and target fencing Global task control Optional fixed-owner mode is integrated into HTTP and the console, with cross-entry maintenance acceptance for MySQL/PostgreSQL targets; full migration, cancellation, fault and capacity profiles remain incomplete Each controller needs its own persistent control, task, configuration, key and report directories. Do not share controller.json , a controller directory or a PVC between controllers. Configure the shared control database with platform-cluster.yml, using a stable, unique node ID per node. The control database and external transaction journal have different responsibilities. A shared control database does not make local synchronization events available on another machine. Cross-host continuation requires the external journal profile in the pipeline manual. One task has one active owner, rather than being split across workers for parallel processing. Configure the chosen access and task mode before namespace initialization. The current candidate refuses mismatched modes even when all members are stopped. Read the first-release baseline and shared access manual, and use consistent session/audit policies and HTTPS. Stopping a local worker does not stop every standby. Pausing the shared pipeline prevents ordinary takeover; inspect target isolation results separately. A healthy heartbeat does not prove business synchronization is healthy, and an expired lease does not prove a process has stopped. Helm provides cluster values and shared-access values, with independent releases per node. Live two-node Kubernetes evidence covers same-volume remounts, image and configuration replacement, Secret rotation and recovery with an external journal. Cross-node volume availability and additional HA profiles require separate verification. Node registry · Recovery · Global control progress Enable optional fixed-owner global mode In addition to shared access, set cluster.sharedTasks: true and configure the same protected 32-byte Base64 taskKey on all members. Each node needs a stable ID and its original independent persistent directory. See the global profile and global control manual. Use fresh task directories for initial activation. Existing local task data needs a separately assessed plan. HTTP 202 confirms admission. Follow the original request receipt to establish its outcome. An offline owner keeps a command pending or unknown until it provides a reliable receipt. Separate management and execution Configure explicit Controller and Agent roles. With the tested PostgreSQL/MySQL control stores and LOCAL/H2 journals, the same Worker can continue during a complete management outage. When management returns, read the original request receipt. See execution lifecycle for deployment conditions and exact evidence. Assign a new task automatically Choose automatic assignment when creating or importing a task. With a MySQL or PostgreSQL source, MySQL or PostgreSQL destinations and an external PostgreSQL journal, up to three candidate Agents verify their Temurin 21 Worker launcher, required connectors and journal reachability in capacity order. If all checks fail, AGENT PLACEMENT UNAVAILABLE leaves the task and journal unchanged. Fix the driver, credential or route before submitting again. Other profiles use capacity-based assignment. Once saved, check the selected owner and run connection and object checks against the source and targets. Approve handoff of a frozen task The offline profile requires a MySQL source, MySQL or PostgreSQL destinations, an initial managed journal writer assignment, and one PostgreSQL database for both control and external journal. 1. Stop the task while the original Agent is healthy and confirm that every destination acknowledged the same cut. Assess the candidate, reserve task and Worker capacity, and stage the full set of closed receipts in its private persistent directory. 2. Review the CLOSED RECEIPTS ONLY inventory. Confirm that it has no reports, failure evidence or raw capture files that need a separate transfer, then explicitly freeze the original writer. 3. If the original Agent becomes unavailable after the freeze, verify its expired lease and the candidate's exact sealed evidence and destination cut. A permitted administrator can approve the ownership change. The task stays stopped on the candidate. 4. Wait for evidence adoption, approve SQL target fencing, and approve starting the candidate Worker separately. Retain the request IDs and receipts. If the original Agent fails before a durable freeze, recover its original directory and keys first. See the global control manual for eligibility and receipt states. Node registry in the console ScreenshotPreview name="node-registry" locale="en" alt="Node registry in the RivoMesh English-language console." /

title: Database compatibility validation
text: Database compatibility validation Use a MySQL snapshot and continuous changes to evaluate database compatibility, run parallel checks and prepare a migration in an independent target environment. ConnectorCatalog adaptation / This catalog covers destination adapters. See the connector catalog for exact product profiles and manuals. Start with an empty target and representative business tables. Validate Chinese text, NULL/empty strings, temporal precision, decimal values, JSON, keyless duplicates, generated columns and index/constraint conversions. Rehearse outages and restart recovery. Application SQL compatibility, constraints, write cutover and rollback need their own plan. Managed row-level validation and repair currently have a MySQL/PostgreSQL acceptance profile. Capture source profiles MySQL is the main path for the target profiles above. Experimental PostgreSQL 17/18 capture writes to PostgreSQL or MySQL. Experimental Oracle 26ai Free capture uses Flashback snapshots and archived changes from a single PDB with a PostgreSQL destination. See the detailed compatibility matrix. Multi-node deployment · Compatibility · Roadmap · Platform design

title: Replication architecture
text: Replication architecture Controllers authorize requests and persist configuration and commands. Agents execute commands assigned to their node and manage Worker processes. Workers capture and deliver data. The control store and journal record management state and data progress respectively. Open the interactive architecture diagram iframe class="architecture-diagram" src="/architecture/en.html?embed=1" title="Interactive RivoMesh replication architecture" loading="lazy" /iframe Control and execution Component Responsibility and durable state --- --- Web console and API Accept browser sessions and Bearer tokens. Roles and per-task grants govern visibility and actions. Controller Accepts new tasks, configuration revisions and operations. Records commands and audit history. Global mode exposes the same task owner and command outcome through multiple entries. Shared control store Records task ownership, registered nodes, shared sessions and cross-entry command state. The owning Agent claims durable global commands and records the outcome. Agent Registers and sends heartbeats, claims commands for its node and supervises separate Workers with available configuration, drivers and credentials. Scoped profiles support automatic assignment for new tasks. Worker Checks source and targets, holds the journal lease and writer epoch, and captures, normalizes and delivers changes per subscription. Participates in task-level validation and recovery. Standalone mode combines the Controller and Agent in one service process and still runs tasks in separate Workers. The separated profile lets an existing Worker continue through a management-entry outage within its tested scope. Automatic placement of a new task and approved transfer of a frozen task have separate requirements. Multi-node deployment and handoff · Global control and durable commands Data movement and recovery 1. Source. MySQL uses GTID/binlog, PostgreSQL uses logical slots and pgoutput, and Oracle uses Flashback and archived LogMiner. Snapshot boundaries, decoders and restart coordinates 2. Durable journal. Local H2 covers standalone storage. An external journal supports scoped multi-node profiles. The journal stores snapshot parts, committed transactions, capture positions, subscription acknowledgements and the writer lease. A paused subscription can keep history pinned. 3. Destination delivery. Transactional SQL destinations commit business rows and the checkpoint together. Analytics products use native materialization receipts. Messaging relies on broker confirmations and stable event IDs. Each subscription progresses independently. Connector catalog 4. Validation and recovery. Supported MySQL-to-transactional-SQL profiles compare rows at a common cut. Reviewed repair, commit confirmation and transaction skip each bind to the relevant report, receipt, error generation and destination scope. Data validation · Troubleshooting Platform design manual · Detailed compatibility matrix

title: How source replication works
text: How source replication works RivoMesh takes a consistent source snapshot and delivers committed changes. The Worker persists snapshot parts, transactions and capture positions in the journal. Each destination delivers from its own subscription and checkpoint. To tell whether a task has caught up, check the source position, journal backlog and confirmation position for each destination. Architecture diagram Source Snapshot-to-CDC boundary Preserve for recovery Native test scope --- --- --- --- MySQL Per-table InnoDB read view and GTID set Original journal, required binlogs and destination receipts 5.7.44, 8.0.46, 8.2.0 and 8.4.13 in scoped standalone, asynchronous GTID and single-primary Group Replication profiles PostgreSQL Per-table exported MVCC snapshot and logical replication LSN Original durable slot, required WAL, timeline and journal generation Experimental. Scoped pgoutput profiles on 17.12 and 18.7 with PostgreSQL or MySQL targets Oracle Flashback SCN and closed archived redo Archives from the retained floor, CDB/PDB identity and journal checkpoint Experimental. Oracle Free 26ai with one PDB and one redo thread, delivering to PostgreSQL MySQL 1. Check the source. A task connects to one logical MySQL topology. List source databases in databases and route them with each destination’s mappings . The profile requires InnoDB, GTID, ROW binlogs and FULL row images. Untagged GTIDs and complete row images allow recovery of committed changes and matching of duplicate occurrences in keyless tables. 2. Establish a consistent view per table. The Worker saves the capture start position and opens the binlog stream. For each table it briefly uses FLUSH TABLES WITH READ LOCK , opens an InnoDB consistent read, verifies the schema, records the GTID set and opens a cursor. It releases the global read lock before reading batches from the same view. A large scan can still retain undo history and metadata locks. 3. Apply from each table baseline. The binlog reader assembles and persists committed transactions during the snapshot. After a destination finishes a table snapshot, the Worker excludes changes already represented in that snapshot. Subscribed rows retain the source transaction boundary across databases. Use a common cut when checking consistency across tables with different baselines. 4. Resume from the original GTID. The journal commits each transaction with its capture position. Restart reuses complete snapshots and rescans a table if its incomplete snapshot lost the read view. An external system promotes an asynchronous replica. MySQL elects the primary in Group Replication. RivoMesh checks the writable role, GTID history and log coverage. A missing required binlog pauses capture at the last durable position. Start with the current primary, the saved GTID set and gtid purged , then check whether a paused target pins journal space. Preserve the original binlogs and checkpoint evidence. Pipeline configuration and failover profiles · Capture recovery PostgreSQL 1. Set the publication scope. A task captures one PostgreSQL database. Here databases lists source schemas. Set wal level=logical , publish INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE for selected tables, use REPLICA IDENTITY FULL and reserve capacity for the durable slot and a temporary snapshot slot. 2. Export each table’s snapshot. The Worker creates a temporary logical slot and reads its snapshot name and consistent point . A separate REPEATABLE READ connection imports the snapshot and reads the table in batches. The consistent-point LSN becomes the table’s CDC boundary. The durable streaming slot is bound to the task’s journal generation. 3. Decode committed changes. pgoutput supplies Relation, Begin, row changes and Commit messages. The decoder uses the publication scope and registered schema. The Worker reports applied and flushed LSNs only after the complete transaction reaches the journal. Keepalives and WAL outside the publication leave the business transaction checkpoint unchanged. Out-of-line TOAST values follow the supported row-image rules. 4. Validate the original slot and timeline. Reconnection checks the system identifier, database, timeline, slot and LSN. The scoped PostgreSQL 17.12 test resumed after promotion with a synchronized failover slot. Missing slots or WAL and timeline regression protect the last durable position. Follow the supported review process when a schema change pauses capture. Monitor durable capture position, replication slot WAL retention and destination backlog together. PostgreSQL source configuration, failover and type coverage Oracle 1. Bind the source identity and determine the SCN. Preflight connects separately to the CDB root and the selected writable PDB. It checks DBID, resetlogs and PDB identity, archive mode, force logging, supplemental logging and Flashback access. Declare uppercase OWNER.TABLE names and map owners to PostgreSQL schemas. 2. Read the Flashback snapshot. The Worker records a snapshot SCN for the capture start. It reads selected tables with AS OF SCN and stores snapshot parts. Complete snapshots can be reused. An interrupted unfinished snapshot can restart using a new Flashback view. 3. Decode closed archives. The Worker checks archive coverage and reads committed changes with LogMiner’s COMMITTED DATA ONLY . It groups changes by XID and orders typed row images by commit SCN and transaction order. Redo and undo supply the images. A transaction open at snapshot time can hold the retained archive floor back until closed archives cover the required transaction boundary. 4. Resume from the original SCN and archive floor. The durable position binds the source identity, captured SCN and archive floor. On restart the Worker checks archive continuity and readability. Missing logs, unsupported records, ambiguous commit order or unreviewed DDL pause capture at the previous durable position. Archive rotation affects CDC latency. The experimental profile uses one PDB, one redo thread and closed archives. Online redo, RAC, source promotion, native binary JSON and LOBs require separate coverage. Oracle source privileges, scalar types and strict textual JSON Delivery, checkpoints and repair The Worker normalizes row changes in source transaction order, then delivers each subscription independently. Transactional SQL destinations commit rows and their local checkpoint together. Analytics destinations recover through engine-specific materialization receipts. Messaging uses broker confirmations and stable event IDs to handle redelivery. If capture advances while one destination stalls, inspect that destination’s error generation and receipt first. For row comparisons, run data validation at a supported common cut. Preserve the journal, destination metadata and relevant source history before recovery. Troubleshooting workflows

title: Introduction
text: What is RivoMesh? RivoMesh synchronizes existing database rows and subsequent inserts, updates and deletes to supported target systems. It combines snapshots, CDC, persistent journals, independent target acknowledgements and web task management. MySQL is the primary capture source. PostgreSQL logical replication and Oracle archived redo capture have experimental profiles. Relational, analytical and messaging destinations each define how they acknowledge and recover transactions. See compatibility for exact versions and topology. Start with a small test database and an independent empty target. Check actual values, incremental changes and restart recovery before expanding the scope. Quick start · Compatibility · Capture mechanics · Architecture and data flow

title: Quick start
text: Quick start Install Eclipse Temurin 21 LTS and Maven. Check mvn -version and java -version to confirm both use Temurin 21. Prepare a MySQL test source with GTID and ROW/FULL binlog settings, plus a dedicated PostgreSQL 17 target with an empty business schema. Confirm the replication and snapshot privileges in the pipeline manual. Build the core project Start the console Open http://127.0.0.1:8080 and sign in with the token. Keep credentials out of URLs and Git. Production browser access requires the HTTPS/session deployment settings in the session manual. To build the local container instead, run docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml up -d --build with the same token set. Enter database addresses that the container can reach. Create and verify a pipeline Use the default pipeline wizard to configure source identity, databases, an independent target, explicit mappings and a persistent journal. Save, check, and then start. Validate snapshot values, inserts, updates, deletes and Worker restart recovery. Targets require empty business tables on first use. The check operation does not validate every runtime privilege. Default recovery retries the original transaction; it does not skip failed data. For experimental captures, follow the separate PostgreSQL or Oracle setup guide. Console and deployment · Multi-database pipelines

title: Compatibility
text: Compatibility and capability boundaries Choose a profile by source version and topology, destination product and mode, and Java runtime . Filter by direction and status in the connector catalog. Use the product manuals and detailed compatibility matrix to check the selected configuration before deploying. Capture sources and runtime Capture source Available scope Check before use --- --- --- MySQL 5.7.44, 8.0.46, 8.2.0 and 8.4.13 Each has Temurin 21 evidence for standalone, async GTID promotion and three-member single-primary Group Replication. Destination coverage varies by topology. InnoDB, GTID, ROW/FULL images, replication and snapshot privileges, and binlog retention. See pipeline configuration. PostgreSQL 17.12 / 18.7 Experimental pgoutput capture into PostgreSQL or MySQL. Native evidence covers synchronized-slot promotion on 17.12 and materialization of stored generated columns on 18.7. One source database per task, explicit publication tables, REPLICA IDENTITY FULL , replication slots, WAL retention and supported types. See source configuration. Oracle 26ai Free 23.26.4.0.0 Experimental Flashback snapshots and single-PDB, single-thread archived LogMiner CDC into PostgreSQL. Supply Oracle JDBC separately. Verify CDB and PDB services, supplemental logging, privileges, archive coverage and types. See source configuration. Eclipse Temurin 21 LTS is the sole supported build and runtime for the current candidate, including Controllers, Agents and Workers. Historical driver and destination tests keep their original runtime. Check the exact build, target and driver in the compatibility matrix. Destinations and operations - Relational databases. Destinations acknowledge independently. Native MySQL 8.4 and PostgreSQL 17 profiles commit business data and a destination checkpoint together. Start ordinary tasks with empty business tables. For an existing PostgreSQL copy, use the read-only adoption preview and check the separate conditions for reviewed single-table adoption. - Database adaptation. Verify exact versions, drivers and compatibility modes for openGauss, DM, KingbaseES, GBase 8c and OceanBase. Commercial distributed GaussDB requires native multi-node verification. See the database adaptation guide. - Analytics and messaging. ClickHouse, Doris and Hive use engine-specific materialization and receipts. Messaging uses confirmed at-least-once publication. Track consumer completion separately and deduplicate using stable event IDs. See messaging targets. - Validation and recovery. Common-cut comparison, reviewed repair, transaction compensation and gap verification each have bounded MySQL/PostgreSQL profiles. Kafka receipt review and failure notices use a separate messaging protocol. For unsupported DDL or types, preserve and review the failure and durable position. See troubleshooting. Multi-node deployment Nodes can share accounts, sessions, audit and task views. Separated deployments have specific SQL profiles for automatic initial Agent placement and administrator-approved transfer of a frozen task. Cross-host continuation requires external journaling and a valid execution lease. See multi-node deployment. Linux, Docker, Helm and Kubernetes deployment files are available. Live two-node Kubernetes runs cover configuration and Secret updates, same-volume remounts and recovery with an external journal. Check cross-node volume availability, failure modes and capacity separately. See execution lifecycle and implementation status.
